Akitazama juu kuelekea jua, Beto (jina lililotengenezwa) alikazia hatua zake ambazo zilikuwa zimemkimbiza tayari alipoelekea msituni. Alijua kwamba angenahitaji kuharakisha ili apite msituni kabla ya giza. Paka-wanyama wakubwa walijulikana kusafiri milimani jirani, na hadithi nyingi za kutisha zilikuwa zikihusu paka hao wakiwashambulia watu katika msitu huu mwenyewe!

Akiingia kivulini baridi cha msitu, Beto alitulia kwa muda mfupi ili kunywa maji ya kupumzisha kutoka kwenye mto mdogo uliopita njia ya miguu.

Saa kadhaa baadaye, alipokuwa akisukumana kwa uchovu mbele, Beto alizunguka kona ya njia na, akidhani aliona mwendo kwenye vichaka mbele, alisimama ghafla. Katika giza lililoanza kupanuka Beto alitazama jinsi, si umbali wa mita thelathini mbele yake, mnyama aliokuwa anamtisha kabisa alivyotoka kwenye vichaka na kugeuka kumkabili! Akageuka, Beto akaruka kwa ajili ya maisha yake! Akisikia midomoni ya miguu ya paka huyo mkubwa ikigandamana na sakafu ya msitu nyuma yake, Beto alijaribu kuchochea miguu yake iliyochoka kuwa hata haraka zaidi. Ghafla, bila kuweza kuona njia kwa uwazi katika giza la msitu, Beto aligotwa kwenye mtende na akatanguliwa chini, bubu kabisa. Akilia kwa uchungu, Beto alihitimisha kuwa haikuwa na maana kuendelea kujaribu, hivyo alilala chini, akisubiri yasiyoweza kuepukika. Aliposubiri, alifikiria kwamba alikuwa anaweza kusikia sauti ya paka anayerukaruka karibu, karibu, karibu…

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Je, unajihisi kidogo kama Beto? Kuna “kitu” kikubwa kinachokusumbua maishani na unajaribu kukitoroka? Labda marafiki zako wamekuacha au ndugu yako amekusemwa vibaya. Labda mtu aliyekuwa unamheshimu sana amekukanyaga au unakumbana na hali ngumu ndani ya familia yako. Labda unapitia kitu chenye maumivu ambacho hakuna mwingine anayejua na wote wanaoona ni uso wako unaoketi, wala hawatafahamu maumivu uliyonayo ndani. Icho chochote unachokabiliana nacho, je, kama Beto, umehitimisha kuwa hauna maana kuendelea kujaribu?

Mara kwa mara tunakutana na hali za maumivu zinazotufanya tuhisi kupoteza hamu. Kiasili tunachukia maumivu na tunajitahidi kuepuka. Hata hivyo, tunakutana na mambo hayo magumu ya maisha. Hatutaki kuendeleza mtazamo wa kujitia huruma, kuishi maisha kwa fikra ya “mwanaathiri.” Itakuwa ujinga, hata hivyo, kudhani kuwa hakuna kitu kama mwanaathiri. Wakati mwingine watu hufanya dhambi kwa wenzao. Kuna nyakati tunajikuta ni waathirika wa hali ambazo hatuna udhibiti juu yao.

Hali kama hizi ni za maumivu na za kuchanganya, wakati mwingine zikitufanya tuhisi kama kukata tamaa kabisa. Tunawezaje kutoka kuwa wahanga hadi kuwa …wakishinda bila kukoma kwa yule aliye wapendacho—Warumi 8:37?

Tuchukulie mambo machache ambayo lazima tayaelewe ili tushinde mapigano haya na tuendelee kustawi kiroho…

…Kujiweka mikononi bila masharti

Lazima tupe umuhimu wa kujiweka mikononi bila masharti kwa Bwana Yesu Kristo. Hii inamaanisha kuwa tuko tayari kumtumikia kwa maisha yetu yote, bila kujali gharama. Tunahitaji kutambua kuwa tutakutana na ugumu maishani (1 Petro 4:12,13). Kuwa Wakristo hakutupi maisha yasiyo na majaribu. Kuishi maisha ya Mkristo kwa hakika mara nyingi huleta matatizo yake. Kwa nini basi Yesu anafundisha kuwa lazo lake ni la rahisi na mzigo wake mwepesi?—…Kwa maana lazo langu ni la upole, na mzigo wangu ni mwepesi—Mathayo 11:28-30. Jibu… Kwa sababu Yeye yuko tayari kutusaidia kubeba mizigo yetu, hatuhitaji kubeba peke yetu! Ikiwa tuko tayari kumtumikia Bwana tu katika nyakati nzuri, basi hivi karibuni tutahisi kukata tamaa tukikutana na ugumu.

…Msamaha

Kawaida, tunapopitia hali ngumu, watu wengine huwa wamehusika kwa namna fulani. Wakati mwingine maneno ya moto hubadilishana, au matendo mabaya hufanywa, na watu hukumizana maumivu. Tulipoudhuliwa, tunajua kwamba tunapaswa kumsamehe mwenye kutuharibia, lakini tunachelewa, kwa sababu tungependa kuona haki ikitekelezwa. Tunaogopa kwamba tukimsamehe mwingine, basi tuta waruhusu kabla hawajaelewa jinsi walivyokosea, hivyo tunaamua kutowasamehe!

Kutowasamehe kunasababisha hasira; hasira inatufunga. Daima! Hasira mara nyingi huleta madhehebu mengine ya dhambi na kusababisha machafuko mengi kwa sisi na kwa wengine. (Waebrania 12:14-17) Hata hivyo, tunapochagua kusamehe wengine, Mungu pia atasamehe sisi (Marko 11:25,26), akiwatoa kwa uhuru watu kutoka kwa mchafu wa kutisha ambao hasira huleta maishani mwetu. Hatuhitaji tena kuwa na wasiwasi kuhusu kuendelea kuwashikilia watenda dhambi mateka. Baada ya yote, yeye au yeye hayuko mfungwa kwetu. Hatuwezi kuchagua kama wataachiliwa au la. Ni Bwana tu ndiye aliye na nguvu ya kuwaachilia watu.

Lazima tuelewe msamaha ni nini au vinginevyo tutajikuta tukijiuliza kama tumesamehe au la. Hapa kuna pointi tatu zitakazotusaidia kuelewa maana halisi ya kusamehe:

1. Kubali

Mara nyingine tunakutana na matatizo kutokana na chaguo zetu wenyewe na wakati mwingine kutokana na chaguo za watu wengine. Wakati watu wengine hufanya chaguo zinazoleta maumivu maishani mwetu, tunapata ugumu kukubali. Tunaweza kujaribu kupigana na maumivu haya kwa lengo la kuuyatoa maishani mwetu, au tunaweza kujaribu kukimbia ili kuepuka ukweli wake wa kutisha. Tunaweza kujifanya kuwa imara ili kuwafanya wengine waamini sio mbaya sana ilhali kwa kweli inachoma! Ingawa mizozo hii inatokea kiasili, hatutapata faraja mpaka tufike mahali pa kukubali. Kukubali sio kusema kutofanya chochote kuhusu hilo bali, ni kutambua kwamba wakati mwingine Mungu huruhusu hali za maumivu maishani ili kutusaidia kukua. (Yakobo 1:2-4) Inamaanisha kumtumaini Bwana badala ya kujaribu kufikiri mambo peke yetu. (Methali 3:4,5) Pia inamaanisha kukiri kwamba tumedhulumiwa na tunahitaji msaada wa Mungu ili tupone.

2. Acha iende

Ni njia gani fupi ya kuondoa kitu usichotaka tena? Kuukabidhi! Hivyo hasa lazima tufanye kwa mizigo ile ya maumivu tunayobeba wakati mwingine. Mkabidhi kwa Mungu. (1 Petro 5:6,7) Ni muhimu sana, tunapomkabidhi Mungu mizigo yetu, tuiachie hapo. Tungeona ujinga kubeba takataka hadi kwenye kisima cha kutupia majahanas, kisha kurudi nyumbani nayo bila kuitupa! Hakuna wetu angesukuma kufikiri kufanya kitu kama hicho. Hata hivyo, tunapomletea Bwana mzigo, wakati mwingine tunapitia utaratibu wa kimuundo wa kumwambia Mungu kuhusu hilo lakini hatuiaiache.

Je, unaachaje kitu ambacho kimekuwa sehemu kubwa ya wewe na kinachoumiza kiasi kwamba hauwezi kufikiria jambo jingine? Sehemu nzuri ya kuanzia ni kumtafuta mwamini thabiti ambaye unaweza kuzungumza naye kwa urahisi juu yake. Zaidi ya hayo, ziungumze na Mungu kuhusu hilo. (Waebrania 4:14-16) Haijalishi kama unapata mahali kuchelewa peke yako na Mungu au kama unapata mtu wa kuomba nawe. Kinachojali ni kupata mahali ambapo unaweza kukaa chini ya magoti na kumwambia Bwana hasa unavyojisikia. Unaweza kumwambia kuwa unahisi umetendewa kwa ukatili. Unaweza kumwambia kuhusu maumivu yote, mkanganyiko na hisia za chuki na kisasi unazohisi. Lenga kumwambia Mungu kuwa umeamua kumsamehe mtenda uharibifu. Kuwa maalum, taja jina la mtenda na matukio maalum. Hii inaweza kuwa kuuma sana kwa sababu inaleta kumbukumbu mipya ya hali ngumu. Ni wakati wa kutafakari roho, kusamehe na kuachilia. Kaeni chini ya magoti hadi upate amani kuhusu hali hiyo. Haijalishi inachukua muda gani mradi tu umeondoa mzigo ule wa kutisha—jaribu usiwe makini na muda. Kuwa na uhakika kwamba Mungu kamwe hamtazami mwito wa msaada! (1 Petro 3:12)

3. Wapende maadui zako

Yesu anatufundisha tupende maadui zetu. (Mathayo 5:43-48) Tunaposamehe, tutampenda mtenda kama Mungu anavyowapenda kwa kweli. Kwa mantiki ya kibinadamu, hili haliwonekani kuwa linawezekana. Ni muujiza wa moyo uliobadilika unaotufanya tupende mtu tuliyemchukia hapo awali.

…Mtukufueni Bwana

Mara nyingi, hatutohisi hamu ya kumtukuza Bwana katikati ya jaribio lakini kwa nini tustaafu kumtukuza wakati tunamhitaji zaidi? (Wafilipi 4:4-7) Tunapaswa angalau kufikiria mambo baadhi ya kushukuru, kisha kumshukuru Mungu kwa hayo. Katika Matendo 16, tunasoma simulizi ya Paulo na Silas wakihubiri huko Filipi. Baada ya kuponya msichana aliyekuwa amezongwa na roho mbaya waliangukwa vibaya na mamlaka za eneo hilo, waliwekewa mitala, na kufungwa gerezani. Hali yao ilibidi iwe ya kukata tamaa. Walikuwa wanateseka, hawawezi kusonga, na ilikuwa usiku. Pengine ilionekana kuwa wakati wa giza maishani mwao. Licha ya haya yote, waliomba na kuimba sifa kwa Mungu! Waliishi maisha ya kujiweka mikononi bila masharti kwa Mungu waliompenda na kumtumaini. Mwishowe, Mungu alichagua kuwaowea kwa muujiza.

Kumwimbia Mungu katikati ya majaribu inawezekana tu wakati Kristo anakaa juu ya enzi katika maisha yetu.

…Endelea mbele

Tunapokumbana na ugumu kila wakati kuna mambo tunayoweza kujifunza. Tunajifunza umuhimu wa kutegemea kabisa na kujiweka mikononi bila masharti kwa Bwana. Tunapata, kwa kiwango binafsi, faraja ya Mungu na tunaitwa kuwafikia roho nyingine zilizoomboleza kwa faraja hii. (2 Wakorintho 1:1-7)

Marafiki wapendwa, kumbukeni, mara ijayo mashaka ya maisha yatakapotufanya tuhisi kutaka kukata tamaa, leta mzigo wako kwa Bwana, uweke yote mikononi mwake, na uachiye!

This hymn is generally considered to be one of the greatest hymns ever written and is found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. It was written by a man who was frail in body, but strong in spirit. It was he who coined the phrase, “It is better to wear out than to rust out.” Let us now take a glimpse into the life of this servant of God.

Henry Francis Lyte, the author of this great and noteworthy hymn, was born June 1, 1793, in Ednam, near Kelso, Scotland. At a young age, he was left an orphan and was in comparative poverty. He was educated at Trinity College in Dublin, Ireland. It was there that his gift of poetry began to appear, winning him three prizes. His primary goal with his studies was to become a physician, instead, by the providence of God, he became a minister of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

One day in Cornwall, a fellow clergyman who was on his deathbed, requested that Lyte would come and give him some spiritual comfort. “To their mutual grief, they found themselves [both] groping for the light, veritable blind guides”. As they searched for truth and assurance of salvation, they fixed their faith on Christ, and Lyte came away from that sickroom a changed man, never to be the same again. It is said that it was his encounter with God at the bedside of that dying man that prompted Lyte’s noble hymn, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.” In the year 1823, Henry F. Lyte took charge of a seashore parish, Lower Brixham, in Devonshire, England. It was at that place where he spent the last 23 years of his life toiling as a pastor for the spiritual good of the poor fishing people and the rough seafaring men of that region until his death in the fall of 1847. For all of Henry’s dedication and labor, he received a reward: having a Sunday school of several hundred scholars, as well as “a splendid company of seventy or eighty teachers, personally trained by him.”

Throughout his lifetime, his health was continually threatened by asthma and tuberculosis. Notwithstanding his physical frailties, he worked tirelessly with an established reputation as a poet, musician, and minister. Wherever he went, he was greatly loved and admired by his people. Toward the end of these later years, his health became gradually worse. So it was that during the winter months, he felt compelled to seek a warmer climate in Italy, which is a part of southern Europe.

Though he was greatly weakened by his sickness, on September 4, 1847, as Lyte was about to leave to head southward, he was arrested by an “irresistible desire” to preach once more to his congregation. He dearly loved these people and he had labored among them for so many years. “Against the protest of his amazed friends, he accomplished this purpose, and it is recorded that Lyte nearly had to crawl to the pulpit and his message came as from a dying man.” “O brethren,” he said, as he entered the familiar pulpit for the last time, “I stand here among you today, as alive from the dead, if I may hope to impress it upon you, and induce you to prepare for that solemn hour which must come to all, by a timely appreciation and dependance on the death of Christ.” These final words made a deep impact upon his congregation, after which he closed the service by administering the Lord’s Supper to his weeping people. Later that evening, after the service, he was inspired to “poetical composition” and wrote the eight stanzas of his last and greatest hymn:

Abide with me: fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide:
when other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

Swift to its close ebbs out life’s little day;
Earth’s joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But, as Thou dwell’st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free,
Come, not to sojourn, but abide, with me.

Come not in terrors, as the King of kings;
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings;
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea;
Come, Friend of sinners, and thus ‘bide with me.

Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though rebellious and perverse meanwhile,
thou hast not left me, oft as I left thee:
On to the close, O Lord, abide with me.

I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, O abide with me.

I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless:
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death’s sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom, and point me to the skies;
Heaven’s morning breaks, and earth’s vain shadows flee:
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

This hymn he gave to one of the family members that very night. Leaving the following day, he began his trek to Rome, Italy, hoping to gain some relief from his sickness. Lyte make it as far as Nice, France where his sickness prevented his further travel. He passed away soon after the age of 55, on November 20, 1847. His last words were “Joy! Peace!”

The scene behind this hymn is that of the resurrected Christ Jesus walking on the road to Emmaus with two of His somewhat sad and discouraged disciples. As they neared the end of their seven-mile walk and approached the village where they were going, Jesus …made as though he would have gone further. But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them –Luke 24:28-29.

We can draw a parallel between that scene and Henry F. Lyte’s own experience of drawing toward the close of his earthly journey. Thus, as the disciples besought the risen Lord to abide with them in the close of that ancient day, so was the meaning of this song written in the “shadows of death” to the hymn writer.

Lyte himself composed a tune for this hymn on the same evening that he wrote it, but it never became widely used. However, the tune universally used was written fourteen years later by William Henry Monk, a noted London musician, and editor of the well-known Anglican hymnal, Hymns Ancient and Modern. He included this song in his first edition, which was published in 1861.

In all, William H. Monk composed 50 tunes for the hymnal. It is said that Monk, being “inspired by the beauty of a glorious sunset while yet experiencing a deep personal sorrow,” composed (in only 10 minutes) the tune, Eventide, for the song, “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk also wrote the music for other familiar hymns such as “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious”, and “The Strife Is O’er”.

To summarize, Henry Lyte experienced many sorrows during his lifetime. Both of his parents died at an early age leaving him an orphan. And his own sickness and frailty caused him to be in ongoing danger of asthma and tuberculosis. Yet, in spite of all his trials, we find in him a resilient spirit to reach out to others; to touch and minister the Gospel to those poor people among whom he lived. “In no other writer,” says Dr. Breed (in the Treasury of Hymn Stories), “are poetry and religion more exquisitely united.”

Este hino é geralmente considerado um dos maiores hinos já escritos e encontra-se em quase todos os hinários ou livros de hinos publicados hoje. Foi escrito por um homem frágil no corpo, mas forte no espírito. Foi ele quem cunhou a frase: “É melhor gastar-se do que enferrujar.” Vamos agora lançar um olhar sobre a vida desse servo de Deus.

Henry Francis Lyte, o autor deste grande e notável hino, nasceu em 1º de junho de 1793, em Ednam, perto de Kelso, na Escócia. Ainda jovem, ficou órfão e viveu em relativa pobreza. Foi educado no Trinity College, em Dublin, Irlanda. Foi ali que seu dom para a poesia começou a surgir, rendendo-lhe três prêmios. Seu objetivo principal com os estudos era tornar-se médico; entretanto, pela providência de Deus, tornou-se ministro do evangelho de Jesus Cristo.

Um dia, na Cornualha, um colega clérigo que estava à beira da morte pediu que Lyte viesse dar-lhe algum consolo espiritual. “Para o pesar mútuo, encontraram-se [ambos] tateando pela luz, verdadeiros guias cegos”. Enquanto buscavam a verdade e a certeza da salvação, fixaram sua fé em Cristo, e Lyte saiu daquele leito de doente transformado, nunca mais o mesmo. Diz-se que foi seu encontro com Deus ao lado de cama daquele moribundo que motivou o nobre hino de Lyte, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.” No ano de 1823, Henry F. Lyte assumiu a responsabilidade de uma paróquia à beira-mar, Lower Brixham, em Devonshire, Inglaterra. Foi nesse lugar que passou os últimos 23 anos de sua vida trabalhando como pastor para o bem espiritual dos pobres pescadores e dos ásperos marinheiros daquela região até sua morte no outono de 1847. Por toda a dedicação e trabalho de Henry, ele recebeu uma recompensa: ter uma escola dominical com várias centenas de alunos, bem como “uma esplêndida companhia de setenta ou oitenta professores, pessoalmente formados por ele.”

Ao longo de sua vida, sua saúde esteve continuamente ameaçada por asma e tuberculose. Não obstante suas fraquezas físicas, trabalhou incansavelmente com reputação consolidada como poeta, músico e ministro. Onde quer que fosse, era muito amado e admirado por seu povo. Já nos últimos anos, sua saúde foi-se tornando gradualmente pior. Assim, durante os meses de inverno, sentiu-se compelido a buscar um clima mais quente na Itália, que fica no sul da Europa.

Embora estivesse muito enfraquecido pela doença, em 4 de setembro de 1847, quando Lyte estava prestes a partir para o sul, foi detido por um “desejo irresistível” de pregar mais uma vez à sua congregação. Amava profundamente aquelas pessoas e havia trabalhado entre elas por tantos anos. “Contra o protesto de seus amigos espantados, realizou esse propósito, e está registrado que Lyte quase teve de rastejar até o púlpito e sua mensagem soou como a de um homem moribundo.” “Ó irmãos,” disse ele, ao subir no púlpito familiar pela última vez, “estou aqui diante de vós hoje, como alguém que voltou da morte, se posso esperar impressionar-vos com isso e induzi-vos a preparar-vos para aquela hora solene que virá para todos, por uma apreciação e dependência oportunas na morte de Cristo.” Essas últimas palavras causaram profundo impacto em sua congregação, após as quais ele encerrou o culto administrando a Ceia do Senhor ao seu povo em lágrimas. Mais tarde naquela noite, depois do culto, foi inspirado à “composição poética” e escreveu as oito estrofes de seu último e maior hino:

Fica comigo: depressa cai o entardecer;
A escuridão se aprofunda; Senhor, fica comigo:
quando outros socorros falham, e os consolos fogem,
Socorro dos desamparados, ó fica comigo.

Veloz ao fim escoa o pequeno dia da vida;
As alegrias da terra se obscurecem, suas glórias passam;
Mudança e decadência em tudo ao redor vejo;
Ó Tu que não mudas, fica comigo.

Não peço um olhar breve, uma palavra passageira;
Mas, como Tu habitavas com Teus discípulos, Senhor,
Familiar, condescendente, paciente, livre,
Vem, não para pernoitar, mas permanece, comigo.

Não venhas em terrores, como o Rei dos reis;
Mas gentil e bom, com cura em Tuas asas;
Lágrimas por todas as dores, um coração para cada súplica;
Vem, Amigo dos pecadores, e assim fica comigo.

Sobre minha cabeça na juventude cedo Tu sorriste;
E, embora rebelde e pervertido entretanto,
não me deixaste, tantas vezes quanto eu Te deixei:
Até ao fim, ó Senhor, fica comigo.

Preciso de Tua presença a cada hora que passa;
O que senão Tua graça pode frustrar o poder do tentador?
Quem, como Tu mesmo, pode ser meu guia e sustentáculo?
Por entre nuvens e sol, ó fica comigo.

Não temo inimigo, Contigo por perto para abençoar:
Maldades não têm peso, e lágrimas nenhuma amargura.
Onde está o ferrão da morte? Onde, túmulo, tua vitória?
Eu triunfo ainda, se Tu ficares comigo.

Toma Tu a cruz diante dos meus olhos que se fecham;
Brilha através da escuridão, e aponta-me para os céus;
A manhã do céu irrompe, e as vãs sombras da terra fogem:
Na vida, na morte, ó Senhor, fica comigo.

Esse hino ele entregou a um dos membros da família naquela mesma noite. Partindo no dia seguinte, iniciou sua jornada rumo a Roma, Itália, esperando obter algum alívio da enfermidade. Lyte chegou até Nice, na França, onde a doença impediu-lhe continuar a viagem. Faleceu pouco depois, aos 55 anos, em 20 de novembro de 1847. Suas últimas palavras foram “Alegria! Paz!”

A cena por trás deste hino é a do Cristo ressuscitado caminhando na estrada de Emaús com dois de Seus discípulos algo tristes e desanimados. Quando se aproximavam do fim dos sete quilômetros de caminhada e chegavam à aldeia aonde iam, Jesus …fez como que havia de passar adiante. Mas eles o constrangeram, dizendo: Fica conosco, porque já é tarde, e o dia está quase acabado. E ele entrou para ficar com eles –Lucas 24:28-29.

Podemos traçar um paralelo entre essa cena e a própria experiência de Henry F. Lyte ao aproximar-se do final de sua jornada terrena. Assim como os discípulos imploraram ao Senhor ressuscitado que ficasse com eles no final daquele antigo dia, assim foi o sentido desta canção escrita nas “sombras da morte” para o autor do hino.

O próprio Lyte compôs uma melodia para este hino na mesma noite em que o escreveu, mas ela nunca se tornou amplamente usada. Todavia, a melodia universalmente usada foi composta quatorze anos depois por William Henry Monk, um notável músico londrino e editor do conhecido hinário anglicano Hymns Ancient and Modern. Ele incluiu essa canção em sua primeira edição, publicada em 1861.

No total, William H. Monk compôs 50 melodias para o hinário. Diz-se que Monk, inspirado “pela beleza de um glorioso pôr do sol enquanto ainda vivia uma profunda tristeza pessoal”, compôs (em apenas 10 minutos) a melodia Eventide para a canção “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk também escreveu a música para outros hinos familiares como “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious”, e “The Strife Is O’er”.

Para resumir, Henry Lyte viveu muitas tristezas ao longo da vida. Ambos os pais morreram quando ele era jovem, deixando-o órfão. E sua própria enfermidade e fraqueza o colocaram em perigo constante de asma e tuberculose. Ainda assim, apesar de todas as suas provações, encontramos nele um espírito resiliente para estender a mão aos outros; para tocar e ministrar o Evangelho àquelas pessoas pobres entre as quais viveu. “Em nenhum outro autor,” diz o Dr. Breed (no Treasury of Hymn Stories), “poesia e religião se unem de modo mais requintado.”

And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus –Matthew 14:28-29.

Men who follow Jesus are men of faith. Discipleship is not for cowards or the faint of heart, nor is it for those who demand a rationale for acts of obedience. The disciples had spent the day with Jesus. After the feeding of the five thousand Matthew writes that …straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away –Matthew 14:22.

If there was anything that the disciples were familiar with and skilled in, it was sailing the waters of Galilee. This was their territory. Peter and John had fished these waters with their father from their earliest remembrance. But tonight, they were making little headway… the wind was contrary.

And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid –Matthew 14:25-27.

Peter then made this bold appeal …Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water –Matthew 14:28. What was Peter thinking? He had never walked on water. Jesus was not asking him to walk on water. It was not logical. It defied the laws of nature… yet when Jesus said “come”. Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water to go to Jesus. That’s right! He was treading on water.

Peter was responding to a clear call from Jesus. Jesus said “come”. It is important that we understand that faith is our response to the clear call of God on our lives. Too often in our ambition to be useful we choose our path and call our ambition “faith” when God may not be in it at all.

If you want to be a man of faith, open your Bible and pray. Ask God to reveal His plan for your life. The Bible contains many commandments that can provide practical direction for our lives. Take God at His Word. Step out in faith and obedience then you will experience the miracle of God’s power in your life.

Peter’s boat was his security. He and his boat had a long relationship. It had served him well for many years. Peter felt right at home in his old bark, although tonight she did not seem to respond well to his masterful seamanship. He had drawn many a draught of fish over her gunwales. Now as he stands on her deck watching Jesus approach, “walking on the water”, he was overcome with a desire to go to Jesus. In reckless abandonment he stepped off her deck …and a miracle happened.

A walk of faith often calls us away from that which is familiar and secure. If we make safety and security our priority—if we limit our actions to carefully calculated risks (limited to that which we can manage and control)—we limit the power of God working in and through us.

Our forefathers in Europe knew that if they embraced the journey of unreserved discipleship, it could be costly. They risked the seizure of their property; many of them lost all that they owned. Since they willingly faced imprisonment and death, we refer to them as heroes of the faith. These were men who were willing to abandon all for the sake of the gospel. Because of their faith we receive the benefits of a godly heritage.

I commend our younger generation of Anabaptist youth for their willingness to make following Jesus a priority. In the past our priority has been to build our security base, be it our farm or business, and then consider mission work as a possibility. That was never Jesus’ model for service. When Jesus sent out his disciples he said. And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece –Luke 9:3.

Later, after they had returned, Jesus asked them, And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing –Luke 22:35.

You do not need to go into foreign missions to experience the power of God released in your life. Every act of radical obedience is an act of faith. There are men in our Anabaptist communities who are experiencing moral defeat. If we are going to succumb to a victim mentality (“I can’t help it”), and define moral failure as an addiction, we set ourselves up for ongoing defeat. Men of faith are men of action who take measurable steps of obedience which will lead them to ultimate victory. Moral failure begins with small compromises that end in crushing defeat.

Peter’s actions were not logical. If Peter would have processed his decision using the scientific method, he would not have taken such a risk. Many of the simple commands of Christ have no apparent scientific reasoning. From baptism, to communion, to foot washing, to anointing with oil, these are all acts of faith. The significance and the power of each lies in the doing of it with a heart of obedient faith, not in the thing itself.

So it is with many aspects of the Christian experience. We can analyze a thing endlessly, ultimately resulting in its demise. This happens in many churches. We reason away the woman’s head covering. We reason away the nonconformed lifestyle. We reason away the permanence of marriage. We reason away brotherhood accountability. What we have left has no resemblance to the simple teachings of Jesus. Discipleship calls us to faithful obedience. Jesus and the apostles taught it, so we do it. The blessing and the power lie in the doing of it.

That is what Peter discovered. He walked on water! He did not dip a toe to test the water first. I like to think he leaped from the boat and hit the water with both feet. That would be faith and Peter had faith.

But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:30-32.

Peter had faith to walk on water until he began to look around and began to process his situation using the scientific method. This is not to invalidate the scientific method. The scientific method proves the order of creation and the evidence of a creator.

In Hebrews 11 we read that …faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen –Hebrews 11:1.

It is our faith that is the substance and our faith that is the evidence of spiritual realities. Just as the scientific method proves the realities of the created world, so our faith proves spiritual realities.

Boisterous wind and crashing waves produced a fearful, sinking Peter. We sometimes criticize Peter for taking his eyes off of Jesus and sinking into the waves; however, Peter walked on water, I know of no one else who walked on water. When we transition from obedient faith to carnal rationalization, we lose power with God.

Are we suggesting that faith is irrational? No, not at all. As a matter of fact, the first act of faith is to believe that Jesus is the logos. John wrote, In the beginning was the Word [Logos], and the Word [Logos], was with God, and the Word [Logos], was God –John 1:1. It is from the Greek word Logos that we get our English word logic.

Just as there are laws in nature that make the scientific method durable and replicable, so there are spiritual laws that give order and cohesion to our inner man. Jesus is the embodiment of these truths. His teachings are the revelation of these truths and through his death and resurrection these truths have become accessible to all. Jesus promised, Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth… –John 16:13.

Men of faith are men who have eyes to see these spiritual realities. Their vision is not limited to the natural world. They understand that there are spiritual realities that have “cause and effect” in our lives that are every bit as powerful as the “cause and effect” that we see about us in the natural world every day.

These realities are only visible to men of faith. Paul wrote, But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned –1 Corinthians 2:14. Men of faith, are men whose lives are governed by spiritual realities that are incomprehensible to the natural man. If you will be a man of faith, expect to be misunderstood. You are embarking on a journey that will run counter to the world view of many.

As Peter began to sink into the waves he cried out, “Lord, save me”. His plaintive cry revealed an absolute trust in his Lord. Jesus reached out His hand and rescued him. Jesus next words continue to challenge us. He said to Peter, …O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? Matthew 14:31. Peter had just walked on water—a feat no man had accomplished before or since, yet Jesus called it “little faith” and asked, “why did you doubt?”.

Jesus said at another time, …If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20.

If Peter’s “little faith” empowered him to walk on water, and if faith as tiny as a grain of mustard seed can remove mountains what does that say of your and my faith?

Perhaps it is evidence that our faith is littler than Peter’s “little faith” and tinier than the tiny grain of mustard seed?! It is also evidence that God honors little faith. What he does not honor is no faith. According to your faith be it unto you. Little faith…walk on water! No faith…sink beneath the waves!

Since Jesus is the “Logos”, He is the master of the natural world and the spirit world. He proved himself to be the Master of the wind and the waves—and when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:32. And He proved Himself to be the Master of the spirit world—then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God –Matthew 14:33.

We, in our western world, have become so satiated with materialism that we can easily be led to believe that natural realities are the most powerful realities. This materialism assaults us, not just with the abundance of material things, but also with a bombardment of humanistic philosophy. Humanistic philosophy is thinking that is devoid of spiritual reality… that is devoid of faith.

If you, as a man, find yourself sinking in waves of despair… be it financial struggles… be it relational difficulties… moral failure or maybe you find yourself being your own worst critic…may I challenge you to lift your eyes to the one who is Logos. Jesus is the one who is master of your circumstances and the one who would be Lord of your soul. To allow Jesus to be Lord of your soul is to live in faith obedience to the radical teachings of Jesus.

To live in harmony with the natural world we honor the laws of nature. When we are replacing a roof, we respect the law of gravity. When driving a vehicle, we slow down for turns out of respect for the law of inertia. Defy the natural laws and someone gets hurt.

To live in harmony with the spiritual world, we honor the law of Christ. We love our neighbor. We forgive our brother. We keep our marriage vows. We bear …one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2.

Men of faith are men who are attune to these spiritual realities and order their lives accordingly.

Och Petrus svarade honom och sade: Herre, är det du, befall mig då att komma till dig över vattnet. Och han sade: Kom. Då steg Petrus ur båten och gick på vattnet för att gå till Jesus – Matteus 14:28–29.

Män som följer Jesus är män av tro. Lärjungaskap är inte för fegisar eller för dem som har ett svagt hjärta, och det är inte för dem som kräver en rationell förklaring för lydnadshandlingar. Lärjungarna hade tillbringat dagen med Jesus. Efter mättandet av de fem tusen skriver Matteus att …omedelbart tvingade Jesus sina lärjungar att gå ombord i båten och åka före honom till andra sidan, medan han sände folket bort – Matteus 14:22.

Om det var något lärjungarna var vana vid och skickliga i, så var det att segla på Genesarets sjö. Det var deras territorium. Petrus och Johannes hade fiskat dessa vatten med sin far så länge de kunde minnas. Men den här kvällen gjorde de liten framgång… vinden var emot dem.

Och i den fjärde nattvakten gick Jesus ut till dem, gående på sjön. När lärjungarna såg honom gå på sjön blev de oroliga och sade: Det är en vålnad; och de skrek av rädsla. Men omedelbart talade Jesus till dem och sade: Var lugna; det är jag; frukta inte – Matteus 14:25–27.

Petrus gjorde då denna djärva vädjan: …Herre, är det du, befall mig då att komma till dig över vattnet – Matteus 14:28. Vad tänkte Petrus? Han hade aldrig gått på vatten. Jesus bad honom inte att gå på vatten. Det var inte logiskt. Det trotsade naturens lagar… men när Jesus sade ”kom”. Steg Petrus ur båten och gick på vattnet för att gå till Jesus. Rätt så! Han gick på vatten.

Petrus svarade på ett tydligt kall från Jesus. Jesus sade ”kom”. Det är viktigt att vi förstår att tro är vårt svar på Guds tydliga kall i våra liv. Alltför ofta i vår iver att vara nyttiga väljer vi vår egen väg och kallar vår ambition för ”tro” när Gud kanske inte är i det alls.

Vill du vara en man av tro, öppna din Bibel och be. Be Gud uppenbara sin plan för ditt liv. Bibeln innehåller många bud som kan ge praktisk vägledning för våra liv. Ta Gud på hans ord. Steg ut i tro och lydnad så kommer du att uppleva Guds krafts mirakel i ditt liv.

Petrus båt var hans trygghet. Han och hans båt hade en lång relation. Den hade tjänat honom väl i många år. Petrus kände sig som hemma i sin gamla farkost, även om hon denna kväll inte verkade svara väl på hans mästerliga sjömanskap. Han hade dragit många fångster över dess relingskant. Nu stod han på däcket och såg Jesus komma, ”gående på vattnet”, och han övermannades av en önskan att gå till Jesus. I vårdslös uppgivenhet steg han ner från däcket …och ett mirakel hände.

En troendes vandring innebär ofta att vi kallas bort från det som är välbekant och säkert. Om vi sätter säkerhet och trygghet först—om vi begränsar våra handlingar till noggrant beräknade risker (begränsade till det vi kan hantera och kontrollera)—så begränsar vi Guds kraft som verkar i och genom oss.

Våra föregångare i Europa visste att om de omfamnade resan med ovillkorligt lärjungaskap kunde det bli kostsamt. De riskerade att deras egendom skulle beslagtas; många förlorade allt de ägde. Eftersom de villigt mötte fängelse och död, kallar vi dem troshjältar. Det var män som var villiga att överge allt för evangeliets skull. På grund av deras tro får vi ett fromt arv.

Jag berömmer vår yngre generation av anabaptistiska ungdomar för deras villighet att göra följandet av Jesus till en prioritet. Tidigare har vår prioritet varit att bygga vår trygghetsbas, vare sig det var vår gård eller verksamhet, och sedan betrakta missionsarbete som en möjlighet. Det var aldrig Jesu modell för tjänst. När Jesus sände ut sina lärjungar sade han: Och han sade till dem: Tag ingenting med er på vägen, varken stavar, säck eller bröd, och inte pengar i bältet; och ha inte två kläder var – Lukas 9:3.

Senare, när de återkom, frågade han dem: Då sade han till dem: När jag sände er utan penningpung, säck och sandaler, saknade ni något? De svarade: Ingenting – Lukas 22:35.

Du behöver inte åka ut i utländsk mission för att uppleva den kraft Gud frigör i ditt liv. Varje handling av radikal lydnad är en troshandling. Det finns män i våra anabaptistiska församlingar som upplever moralisk nederlag. Om vi kommer att ge efter för en offermentalitet (”jag kan inte rå för det”) och definiera moralisk fall som en beroendeproblematik, sätter vi oss upp för fortsatt nederlag. Män av tro är handlande män som tar mätbara steg i lydnad som leder dem till slutlig seger. Moralisk fall börjar med små kompromisser som slutar i krossande nederlag.

Petrus handlingar var inte logiska. Om Petrus hade bearbetat sitt beslut med den vetenskapliga metoden skulle han inte ha tagit en sådan risk. Många av Kristi enkla bud verkar sakna vetenskaplig förklaring. Från dopet, till nattvarden, till fotvätt, till smörjelse med olja, är detta alla troshandlingar. Betydelsen och kraften i var och en ligger i att utföra dem med ett lydigt hjärta i tro, inte i handlingen i sig.

Så är det med många aspekter av den kristna erfarenheten. Vi kan analysera något oändligt, vilket i slutändan leder till dess undergång. Detta händer i många kyrkor. Vi förklarar bort kvinnans huvudbonad. Vi förklarar bort icke-anpassad livsstil. Vi förklarar bort äktenskapets beständighet. Vi förklarar bort broderligt ansvar. Vad som återstår liknar inte Jesu enkla lära. Lärjungaskap kallar oss till trogen lydnad. Jesus och apostlarna undervisade det, så gör vi det. Välsignelsen och kraften ligger i att göra det.

Det var vad Petrus upptäckte. Han gick på vattnet! Han doppade inte en tå för att pröva först. Jag vill gärna tro att han hoppade från båten och träffade vattnet med båda fötterna. Det skulle vara tro, och Petrus hade tro.

Men när han såg hur vinden var stark, blev han förskräckt; och när han började sjunka ropade han: Herre, hjälp mig! Då sträckte Jesus genast ut sin hand, höll honom och sade till honom: Du som har litet förtroende, varför tvivlade du? När de nu kom in i båten tystnade vinden – Matteus 14:30–32.

Petrus hade tro att gå på vattnet tills han började se sig omkring och började bearbeta situationen med den vetenskapliga metoden. Detta innebär inte att ogiltigförklara den vetenskapliga metoden. Den vetenskapliga metoden visar skapelsens ordning och beviset för en Skapare.

I Hebreerbrevet 11 läser vi att …tro är övertygelsen om det hoppade, en visshet om ting som man inte ser – Hebreerbrevet 11:1.

Det är vår tro som är övertygelsen och vår tro som är beviset för andliga realiteter. Liksom den vetenskapliga metoden bevisar verkligheterna i den skapade världen, så bevisar vår tro andliga verkligheter.

Vågornas dån och starka vind frambringade en rädd, sjunkande Petrus. Vi kritiserar ibland Petrus för att han tog blicken från Jesus och sjönk ner i vågorna; men Petrus gick på vattnet, och jag känner ingen annan som gick på vattnet. När vi övergår från lydig tro till köttslig rationalisering förlorar vi makt hos Gud.

Säger vi då att tro är irrationell? Nej, inte alls. Faktum är att den första handlingen av tro är att tro att Jesus är Logos. Johannes skrev: I begynnelsen var Ordet [Logos], och Ordet var hos Gud, och Ordet var Gud – Johannes 1:1. Det är från det grekiska ordet Logos som vi får vårt svenska ord logik.

Liksom det finns lagar i naturen som gör den vetenskapliga metoden hållbar och reproducerbar, så finns det andliga lagar som ger ordning och sammanhang åt vår inre människa. Jesus är kroppsliggörandet av dessa sanningar. Hans lära är uppenbarelsen av dessa sanningar och genom hans död och uppståndelse har dessa sanningar blivit tillgängliga för alla. Jesus lovade: När han, sanningen Andes, kommer skall han föra er in i hela sanningen… – Johannes 16:13.

Män av tro är män som har ögon att se dessa andliga realiteter. Deras syn är inte begränsad till den naturliga världen. De förstår att det finns andliga realiteter som har ”orsak och verkan” i våra liv som är minst lika kraftfulla som den ”orsak och verkan” vi ser i den naturliga världen varje dag.

Dessa realiteter är endast synliga för människor av tro. Paulus skrev: Men den naturlige mänskan tar inte emot det som hör Guds Ande till; ty det är dårskap för honom, och han kan inte förstå det, därför att det andligen bedöms – 1 Korintierbrevet 2:14. Män av tro är män vars liv styrs av andliga realiteter som den naturlige mannen inte förstår. Om du vill bli en man av tro, räkna med att bli missförstådd. Du ger dig ut på en väg som kommer att gå emot mångas världssyn.

När Petrus började sjunka i vågorna ropade han: ”Herre, hjälp mig”. Hans klagande rop visade ett absolut förtröstande på sin Herre. Jesus räckte ut sin hand och räddade honom. Jesu nästa ord fortsätter att utmana oss. Han sade till Petrus: …Du som har litet förtroende, varför tvivlade du? – Matteus 14:31. Petrus hade just gått på vattnet—en bedrift ingen annan uppnått före eller efter honom—ändå kallade Jesus det för ”liten tro” och frågade: ”varför tvivlade du?”.

Jesus sade vid ett annat tillfälle: …Om ni har tro som ett senapskorn skall ni säga till detta berg: Flytta härifrån dit — och det skall flytta; och ingenting skall vara omöjligt för er – Matteus 17:20.

Om Petrus ”lilla tro” gav honom kraft att gå på vattnet, och om tro så liten som ett senapskorn kan flytta berg, vad säger det då om din och min tro?

Kanske är det ett bevis på att vår tro är ännu mindre än Petrus ”lilla tro” och ännu mindre än det lilla senapskornet?! Det är också bevis på att Gud hedrar liten tro. Det han inte hedrar är ingen tro. Efter din tro må det ske för dig. Liten tro… gå på vattnet! Ingen tro… sjunk under vågorna!

Då Jesus är ”Logos” är han Herre över naturens värld och andevärlden. Han visade sig vara Herre över vind och vågor—och när de kom in i båten upphörde vinden – Matteus 14:32. Och han visade sig vara Herre över andevärlden—då kom de i båten och tillbad honom och sade: Du är verkligen Guds Son – Matteus 14:33.

Vi i vår västerländska värld har blivit så mätta på materialism att vi lätt kan ledas att tro att naturliga realiteter är de mest kraftfulla realiteterna. Denna materialism angriper oss inte bara med överflöd av materiella ting, utan också med en bombarderande humanistisk filosofi. Humanistisk filosofi är ett tänkande tömt på andlig verklighet… som saknar tro.

Om du som man finner dig sjunka i förtvivlans vågor… vare sig det är ekonomiska svårigheter… relationsproblem… moralisk fall eller kanske att du är din egen värsta kritiker… må jag utmana dig att lyfta blicken till honom som är Logos. Jesus är han som är mästare över dina omständigheter och han som vill vara Herre över din själ. Att låta Jesus vara Herre över din själ är att leva i trogen lydnad mot Jesu radikala lära.

För att leva i samklang med naturen hedrar vi naturens lagar. När vi byter tak respekterar vi tyngdlagen. När vi kör ett fordon saktar vi ner i kurvor av respekt för tröghetslagen. Trotsar vi naturens lagar blir någon skadad.

För att leva i samklang med andevärlden hedrar vi Kristi lag. Vi älskar vår nästa. Vi förlåter vår broder. Vi håller våra äktenskapslöften. Vi bär …varandras bördor, och så uppfyller ni Kristi lag – Galaterbrevet 6:2.

Män av tro är män som är inställda på dessa andliga realiteter och ordnar sina liv därefter.

Glancing up at the sun, Beto (a made-up name) quickened his already hurried pace as he approached the forest. He knew that he would need to hurry if he wanted to make it through the forest before dark. Large wildcats were known to roam in the surrounding mountains, and many were the terrifying stories of these cats attacking people in this very forest!

Entering the cool shade of the forest, Beto paused just long enough for a refreshing drink of water from the creek that meandered across the footpath.

Several hours later, as he pushed wearily onward, Beto rounded a bend in the trail and, thinking he saw a movement in the bushes ahead, stopped abruptly. In the gathering darkness Beto watched as, not thirty paces before him, the dreaded beast he so tremendously feared crept out of the bushes and turned to face him! Turning, Beto fled for his life! Hearing the padding of the wildcat’s enormous paws on the forest floor behind him, Beto tried to pump his tired legs even faster. Suddenly, not being able to see the path clearly in the darkness of the forest, Beto tripped on a vine and sprawled helplessly onto the ground. Weeping bitterly, Beto concluded that it was useless to continue trying, so he lay on the ground, waiting for the inevitable. As he waited, he imagined that he could hear the sound of the wildcat moving in closer, closer, closer…

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Are you feeling a bit like Beto? Is there a big “something” inflicting pain in your life and you’re trying to get away from it? Maybe your friends have forsaken you or a brother or sister has slandered you. Maybe someone you highly respected has trampled over you or you are experiencing difficult situations in your family. Maybe you are experiencing something painful that no one else knows about and all that others see is your “smiling” exterior, never realizing the pain you’re feeling inside. Whatever it is that you’re dealing with, have you, like Beto, concluded that it’s useless to keep trying?

At times we experience painful situations that cause us to feel like giving up. We naturally hate pain and do our best to avoid it. Still, we meet up with some of those hard things of life. We don’t want to nurse an attitude of self-pity, going through life with an “I am a victim” mentality. It would be foolish, however, to assume that there is no such thing as a victim. Sometimes people commit sins against each other. There are times when we find ourselves victims of circumstances over which we have no control.

Situations like this are painful and confusing, sometimes causing us to feel like just throwing up our hands in despair. How do we go from feeling like poor victims to being …more than conquerors through him that loved us –Romans 8:37?

Let’s take a look at a few things that we must understand if we are to overcome these battles and continue to thrive spiritually…

…Unreserved surrender

We must understand the importance of unreserved surrender to the Lord Jesus Christ. This means that we are willing to serve Him for the rest of our life, no matter what the cost. We need to be aware that we will face difficulties in life (1 Peter 4:12,13). Being Christians does not give us a trial-free life. Living the life of a Christian does in fact, often bring hardships of its own. Why, then, does Jesus teach that His yoke is easy and His burden light?—…For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light –Matthew 11:28-30. The answer… Because He is willing to help us bear our burdens, we don’t need to do it alone! If we are willing to serve the Lord only in good times, then we will soon feel like giving up when we meet hardship.

…Forgiveness

Usually, when we experience a difficult situation, other people are involved in some way. Sometimes hot words are exchanged, or evil action is taken, and people end up hurting each other. When we’ve been wronged, we know that we should forgive the person who wronged us, yet we hesitate, because we’d really like to see justice carried out. We fear that if we forgive the other person, then we will set him or her free before they realize how wrong they were, so we choose unforgiveness!

Unforgiveness always leads to bitterness; bitterness always shackles us. Always! Bitterness often brings with it a host of other sins and causes much trouble for us and for others. (Hebrews 12:14-17) However, when we choose to forgive others, God will also forgive us (Mark 11:25,26), setting us free from the awful mess that bitterness creates in our lives. We no longer need to worry about holding the offender captive. After all, he or she is not in bondage to us. We cannot choose whether or not they will be set free. Only the Lord has the power to set someone free.

We must understand what forgiveness is or else we will find ourselves wondering whether or not we have forgiven. Following are three points that will help us understand what it really means to forgive:

1. Accept it

Sometimes we face difficulties as the result of our own choices and sometimes as the result of other people’s choices. When other people make choices that cause pain in our life we have a hard time accepting it. We may try to fight this pain in an effort to remove it from our life, or we may try to run away from it in an effort to escape its dreadful reality. We may put up a “tough” facade to try to make others believe it’s really not so bad when in reality it just plain hurts! While these reactions come naturally, we won’t find relief until we’ve come to a place of acceptance. To accept it doesn’t mean to do nothing about it but, rather, to realize that sometimes God allows painful situations in life to help us grow. (James 1:2-4) It means to trust the Lord instead of trying to figure things out on our own. (Proverbs 3:4,5) It also means to admit that we’ve been hurt and that we need God to help us heal.

2. Let it go

What’s the quickest way to get rid of something you no longer want? Give it away! That’s exactly what we must do with those painful burdens we sometimes find ourselves carrying. Give them to God. (1 Peter 5:6,7) It is very important, when we give our burdens to God, that we leave them there. We would feel very foolish taking a load of garbage to the local landfill, and then turning around and taking it all back home without dumping it! None of us would even consider doing such a thing. Yet, when we bring a burden to the Lord, we sometimes go through a formal ritual of telling God about it but never letting it go.

How do you let go of something that has become so much a part of you and is so painful that you can think of little else? A good place to start is to find a stable believer with whom you can comfortably converse and talk with about it. Even more importantly, talk with God about it. (Hebrews 4:14-16) It doesn’t matter if you find a place to be alone with God or if you find someone to pray with you. What really matters is to find a place where you can get on your knees and tell the Lord exactly how you are feeling. You can tell Him that you feel you were treated unjustly. You can tell Him all about the pain, the confusion and the feelings of hatred and revenge that you are feeling. Make a point of telling God that you choose to forgive the offender. Be specific, mentioning the name of the offender and specific situations. This can be very painful because it brings fresh memories of difficult situations. It is a time of soul searching, forgiving, and letting go. Stay on your knees until you are at peace about the situation. It doesn’t matter how long it takes as long as you get rid of that awful burden—try to not be mindful of the time. Be assured that God never ignores a plea for help! (1Peter 3:12)

3. Love your enemies

Jesus commands us to love our enemies. (Matthew 5:43-48) When we have forgiven, we will genuinely love the offender the way that God loves them. According to human reasoning, this isn’t possible. It’s the miracle of a changed heart that causes us to love someone we once hated.

…Worship the Lord

Often, we don’t feel like worshiping the Lord in the middle of a trial but why should we quit worshiping Him when we need Him the most? (Philippians 4:4-7) We ought to at least think of some things for which to be thankful, then thank God for them. In Acts 16, we read an account of Paul and Silas preaching in Philippi. After they had healed a demon-possessed girl they were severely beaten by the local authorities, secured in stocks, and locked in prison. Their situation must surely have felt hopeless. They were in pain, they couldn’t move, and it was night. It probably felt like a dark time in their lives. In spite of all this, they prayed and sang praises to God! They were living lives of unreserved surrender to a God Whom they loved and trusted. In the end, God chose to miraculously deliver them.

Praising God in the middle of trials is only possible when Christ is reigning in our lives.

…Move forward

When we experience difficulties there are always things we can learn. We learn the importance of complete dependence on and unconditional surrender to the Lord. We experience, at a personal level, the comfort of God and we are called to reach out to other troubled souls with this comfort. (2 Corinthians 1:1-7)

Dear friends, remember, the next time the cares of life make you feel like giving up, bring your burden to the Lord, put it all in His hands, and let it go!

Alzando lo sguardo verso il sole, Beto (un nome inventato) accelerò il già rapido passo mentre si avvicinava alla foresta. Sapeva che avrebbe dovuto affrettarsi se voleva attraversare la foresta prima del buio. Si sapeva che grandi felini selvatici vagavano per le montagne circostanti, e molte erano le storie terrificanti di questi felini che attaccavano persone proprio in questa foresta!

Entrando nell'ombra fresca della foresta, Beto si fermò giusto il tempo per una bevuta rinfrescante d'acqua dal ruscello che serpeggiava lungo il sentiero.

Alcune ore più tardi, mentre proseguiva stancamente, Beto svoltò una curva del sentiero e, pensando di aver visto un movimento nei cespugli avanti, si fermò di colpo. Nella crescente oscurità Beto osservò come, a non più di trenta passi da lui, la temuta bestia che tanto temeva sbucò dai cespugli e si voltò a guardarlo! Voltatosi, Beto fuggì per salvarsi la vita! Sentendo il tacchettio delle enormi zampe del felino sulla terra della foresta alle sue spalle, Beto cercò di spingere le sue gambe stanche ancora più veloce. Improvvisamente, non riuscendo a vedere chiaramente il sentiero nell'oscurità della foresta, Beto inciampò in una liana e si rovesciò impotente a terra. Piangendo amaramente, Beto concluse che era inutile continuare a lottare, così rimase sdraiato a terra, aspettando l'inevitabile. Mentre aspettava, si immaginò di poter sentire il suono del felino che si avvicinava, sempre più vicino, sempre più vicino…

* * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * * *

Ti senti un po' come Beto? C'è un grande “qualcosa” che ti infligge dolore nella vita e stai cercando di allontanartene? Forse i tuoi amici ti hanno abbandonato o un fratello o una sorella ti ha diffamato. Forse qualcuno che stimavi molto ti ha calpestato o stai vivendo situazioni difficili in famiglia. Forse stai attraversando qualcosa di doloroso che nessun altro conosce e tutto ciò che gli altri vedono è il tuo esteriore “sorridente”, senza rendersi conto del dolore che provi dentro. Qualunque cosa tu stia affrontando, hai, come Beto, concluso che è inutile continuare a provarci?

A volte viviamo situazioni dolorose che ci fanno venire voglia di arrenderci. Naturalmente odiamo il dolore e facciamo del nostro meglio per evitarlo. Eppure, ci imbattiamo in alcune di quelle difficoltà della vita. Non vogliamo coltivare un atteggiamento di pietà verso noi stessi, vivendo con una mentalità da “vittima”. Sarebbe però sciocco presumere che non esista la vittima. A volte le persone commettono peccati l'una contro l'altra. Ci sono momenti in cui ci troviamo vittime di circostanze su cui non abbiamo alcun controllo.

Situzioni come questa sono dolorose e sconcertanti, talvolta facendoci venir voglia di gettare semplicemente le armi e disperare. Come passiamo dal sentirci povere vittime all'essere …più che vincitori per mezzo di colui che ci ha amati — Romani 8:37?

Diamo uno sguardo ad alcune cose che dobbiamo comprendere se vogliamo vincere queste battaglie e continuare a prosperare spiritualmente…

…resa senza riserve

Dobbiamo comprendere l'importanza della resa senza riserve al Signore Gesù Cristo. Questo significa che siamo disposti a servirlo per il resto della nostra vita, a qualunque costo. Dobbiamo essere consapevoli che affronteremo difficoltà nella vita (1 Pietro 4:12,13). Essere cristiani non ci garantisce una vita senza prove. Vivere la vita cristiana, infatti, spesso comporta difficoltà proprie. Perché, allora, Gesù insegna che il suo giogo è facile e il suo fardello leggero?—…Perché il mio giogo è dolce e il mio carico è leggero — Matteo 11:28-30. La risposta… Perché egli è disposto ad aiutarci a portare i nostri pesi, non dobbiamo farlo da soli! Se siamo disposti a servire il Signore solo nei momenti buoni, presto ci sentiremo pronti ad arrenderci quando incontreremo difficoltà.

…perdono

Di solito, quando viviamo una situazione difficile, altre persone sono in qualche modo coinvolte. A volte si scambiano parole accese o si compiono azioni malvagie, e le persone finiscono per ferirsi a vicenda. Quando siamo stati offesi, sappiamo che dovremmo perdonare chi ci ha fatto del male, eppure esitiamo, perché vorremmo davvero che la giustizia fosse fatta. Temiamo che se perdoniamo l'altra persona, la libereremo prima che si renda conto di quanto ha sbagliato, così scegliamo l'accanimento del non-perdono!

L'imperdonanza porta sempre all'amarezza; l'amarezza sempre ci incatena. Sempre! L'amarezza spesso porta con sé una serie di altri peccati e causa molti guai a noi e agli altri. (Ebrei 12:14-17) Tuttavia, quando scegliamo di perdonare gli altri, Dio ci perdonerà anche noi (Marco 11:25,26), liberandoci dall'orribile pasticcio che l'amarezza crea nelle nostre vite. Non dobbiamo più preoccuparci di tenere il colpevole prigioniero. Dopotutto, lui o lei non è in schiavitù a noi. Non possiamo decidere se verranno liberati o meno. Solo il Signore ha il potere di liberare qualcuno.

Dobbiamo comprendere che cos'è il perdono, altrimenti ci troveremo a chiederci se abbiamo davvero perdonato o no. Seguono tre punti che ci aiuteranno a capire cosa significa veramente perdonare:

1. Accettalo

Talvolta affrontiamo difficoltà a causa delle nostre scelte e talvolta a causa delle scelte altrui. Quando altre persone compiono scelte che causano dolore nella nostra vita, abbiamo difficoltà ad accettarlo. Potremmo cercare di combattere questo dolore nel tentativo di eliminarlo dalla nostra vita, oppure potremmo cercare di scappare da esso per sfuggire alla sua terribile realtà. Potremmo mettere su una facciata “dura” per cercare di far credere agli altri che non sia così grave quando in realtà fa malissimo! Sebbene queste reazioni siano naturali, non troveremo sollievo finché non arriveremo a un luogo di accettazione. Accettarlo non significa non fare nulla al riguardo, ma piuttosto rendersi conto che a volte Dio permette situazioni dolorose nella vita per aiutarci a crescere. (Giacomo 1:2-4) Significa confidare nel Signore invece di cercare di risolvere tutto da soli. (Proverbi 3:4,5) Significa anche ammettere di essere stati feriti e che abbiamo bisogno che Dio ci aiuti a guarire.

2. Lascialo andare

Qual è il modo più rapido per liberarsi di qualcosa che non vuoi più? Dallo via! Questo è esattamente ciò che dobbiamo fare con quei fardelli dolorosi che a volte ci ritroviamo a portare. Dallì a Dio. (1 Pietro 5:6,7) È molto importante, quando consegniamo i nostri pesi a Dio, lasciarli lì. Ci sentiremmo molto sciocchi a portare un carico di immondizia alla discarica locale e poi torcerci indietro a prenderlo tutto senza scaricarlo! Nessuno di noi considererebbe neppure di fare una cosa simile. Eppure, quando portiamo un peso al Signore, a volte procediamo con un rituale formale di raccontarglielo ma senza mai lasciarlo andare.

Come lasci andare qualcosa che è diventato così parte di te e che è così doloroso che riesci a pensare a poco altro? Un buon punto di partenza è trovare un credente stabile con cui puoi conversare comodamente e parlarne. Ancora più importante, parlane con Dio. (Ebrei 4:14-16) Non importa se trovi un luogo per rimanere solo con Dio o se trovi qualcuno con cui pregare. Ciò che conta davvero è trovare un luogo dove puoi inginocchiarti e dire al Signore esattamente come ti senti. Puoi dirgli che senti di essere stato trattato ingiustamente. Puoi raccontargli tutto del dolore, della confusione e dei sentimenti di odio e vendetta che provi. Impegnati a dire a Dio che scegli di perdonare l'offensore. Sii specifico, menzionando il nome dell'offensore e situazioni specifiche. Questo può essere molto doloroso perché porta alla luce ricordi freschi di situazioni difficili. È un tempo di esame dell'anima, di perdono e di lasciar andare. Rimani in ginocchio finché non sei in pace riguardo alla situazione. Non importa quanto tempo ci vuole purché ti liberi di quel terribile fardello—cerca di non pensare al tempo. Sii certo che Dio non ignora mai una richiesta di aiuto! (1 Pietro 3:12)

3. Ama i tuoi nemici

Gesù ci comanda di amare i nostri nemici. (Matteo 5:43-48) Quando abbiamo perdonato, ameremo sinceramente l'offensore come Dio lo ama. Secondo la ragione umana, questo non è possibile. È il miracolo di un cuore trasformato che ci porta ad amare qualcuno che un tempo odiavamo.

…Adora il Signore

Spesso non abbiamo voglia di adorare il Signore in mezzo a una prova, ma perché dovremmo smettere di adorarlo proprio quando ne abbiamo più bisogno? (Filippesi 4:4-7) Dovremmo almeno pensare ad alcune cose per cui essere grati, e poi ringraziare Dio per esse. In Atti 16 leggiamo il racconto di Paolo e Sila che predicavano a Filippi. Dopo aver liberato una ragazza posseduta da uno spirito maligno, furono duramente picchiati dalle autorità locali, messi in ceppi e rinchiusi in prigione. La loro situazione doveva senz'altro sembrare senza speranza. Erano nel dolore, non potevano muoversi ed era notte. Probabilmente sembrava un momento oscuro nelle loro vite. Nonostante tutto questo, pregarono e cantavano inni a Dio! Vivevano vite di resa senza riserve a un Dio che amavano e in cui confidavano. Alla fine, Dio scelse di liberarle miracolosamente.

Lodare Dio in mezzo alle prove è possibile solo quando Cristo regna nelle nostre vite.

…Avanza

Quando sperimentiamo difficoltà ci sono sempre cose che possiamo imparare. Impariamo l'importanza della dipendenza completa e della resa incondizionata al Signore. Sperimenti, a livello personale, il conforto di Dio e siamo chiamati a tendere la mano ad altre anime travagliate con questo conforto. (2 Corinzi 1:1-7)

Cari amici, ricordate, la prossima volta che i pesi della vita vi fanno venir voglia di arrendervi, portate il vostro fardello al Signore, mettetelo tutto nelle Sue mani e lasciatelo andare!

As a child, you might think you can’t make a difference in the lives of people around you, but that is not true! Your little acts of kindness will not soon be forgotten. Being a true friend to someone who is hurting can change that person’s life forever.

This is the true story of “Hadassah” (not her real name) a young girl who was very much looking forward to starting school. Once she started first grade, what a disappointment it was to find that the second-grade girls were ready for someone to be mean to, or so it seemed. Maybe it would have been better if Hadassah had stood up to them, but she didn’t. Instead, she chose to act as if it didn’t hurt and tried to ignore them. Some days were better than others, but sadly this went on for three or four years.

Sure, there were good times too, but many evenings she walked home from school, crying most of the way and wishing that she wouldn’t need to go back to school the next day!

One day, one of the girls lost her pen. She was sure that Hadassah had stolen it. This was very disturbing to a very conscientious Hadassah. At the next recess she was blamed for cheating on her flash cards. Many other made-up stories were also passed around among the girls.

However, there was one little girl in that second-grade group of girls whose name we’ll say was “Esther”. She was Hadassah’s best friend and supported her all through those difficult years.

Esther was a very gentle, sweet girl, which is mostly what Hadassah remembered her for. Esther had cystic fibrosis and in the 1970s they didn’t have as many treatment options available for that disease as they do now, so those patients usually died very young. As Esther’s sickness became worse, the days that she felt well enough to be in school were rare. Since Esther was well-liked, the days when she was in school were special to everyone. Perhaps Esther realized she would be in heaven before the other girls—we don’t know for sure. But she taught the girls a song, “How Far Is Heaven”, which Hadassah still likes to sing today!

Hadassah still remembers seeing the emergency squad go past her house when they took Esther to the hospital for the last time. It was a very sad group of schoolgirls when Esther died at the age of 13. Esther had touched the hearts of many people in her short life, including the nurses who had cared for her during her stay in the hospital. Hadassah still remembers seeing some of the nurses crying at Esther’s funeral. Do you think Hadassah will ever forget Esther? Never!

Besides being her best friend, another bright spot for Hadassah was that when Esther was in school the other girls weren’t as mean to her (Hadassah). It so happened that in about the fourth grade, Esther was in school more often. One day she went home and told her parents what she was witnessing in school—how the other girls were against Hadassah and were being so mean to her. Esther’s father brought this problem up in the next parent/teacher meeting. What a night and day change started the very next day! One of the girls even came to Hadassah and apologized. Finally, they could all be friends and today those girls are Hadassah’s “old school friends”.

It’s worth it to stand beside someone who is being treated unkindly. Your support may be what God uses to help your friend to go through their hard times in a good way! And share it with your parents, they can help find a way to change the problem.

Ukitoka utotoni, unaweza kudhani hauwezi kuleta tofauti katika maisha ya watu waliokuzunguka, lakini hiyo si kweli! Matendo yako madogo ya wema hayatapitwa na wakati haraka. Kuwa rafiki wa kweli kwa mtu anayehangaika kunaweza kumabadilisha maisha yake milele.

Hii ni hadithi halisi ya “Hadassah” (sio jina lake halisi), msichana mdogo aliyekuwa akisubiri kwa hamu kuanza shule. Alipopata nafasi ya kuingia darasa la kwanza, alishangazwa na kufadhaika alipogundua kwamba wasichana wa darasa la pili walikuwa tayari kumchukulia mtu wa kuwa mkasiriwa, au hivyo ilionekana. Labda ingekuwa bora kama Hadassah angehimili na kuwakananisha, lakini hakufanya hivyo. Badala yake, aliamua kuonyesha kama haikuumiza na alijaribu kuwasahau. Siku fulani zilikuwa nzuri kuliko nyingine, lakini kwa masikitiko hili liliendelea kwa miaka mitatu au minne.

Ndio, kulikuwepo na wakati mzuri pia, lakini usiku wengi alitembea nyumbani kutoka shuleni akilia sehemu kubwa ya safari na akitamani asingehitaji kurudi shuleni siku iliyofuata!

Siku moja, mmoja wa wasichana alipoteza kalamu yake. Alikuwa na hakika Hadassah alimwindikia. Hii ilimkera sana Hadassah ambaye alikuwa mwangalifu sana. Wakati wa mapumziko uliofuata alishtakiwa kwa kuibiwa kwa karatasi zake za kufundishia. Hadithi nyingi nyingine za kubuni pia zilienea miongoni mwa wasichana.

Hata hivyo, kulikuwa na msichana mdogo kati ya kundi hilo la darasa la pili ambaye tutamwita “Esther”. Alikuwa rafiki wa karibu wa Hadassah na alimtia moyo katika miaka hiyo yote ngumu.

Esther alikuwa msichana mlevi sana na mtamu, ndivyo ambavyo Hadassah alikumbuka zaidi kumhusu. Esther alikuwa na ugonjwa wa cystic fibrosis na miaka ya 1970 hawakuwa na chaguzi nyingi za matibabu kwa ugonjwa huo kama zilivyo sasa, kwa hivyo wagonjwa hao kwa kawaida walifariki wakiwa wadogo. Ugonjwa wa Esther ulipozidi, siku alizokuwa na afya ya kutosha kuwa shuleni zilikuwa nadra. Kwa kuwa Esther alipendwa, siku ambapo alikuwa shuleni zilikuwa maalum kwa kila mtu. Huenda Esther alitambua atakuwa mbinguni kabla ya wasichana wengine—hatujui kwa hakika. Lakini alimfundisha kundi wimbo, “How Far Is Heaven”, ambao Hadassah bado anapenda kuimba hadi leo!

Hadassah bado anakumbuka kuona gari la dharura likipita karibu na nyumba yao walipokuwa wakipeleka Esther hospitalini mara ya mwisho. Walikuwa kundi la wasichana waliotia huzuni walipomuaga Esther akiwa na umri wa miaka 13. Esther alikuwa ameigusa mioyo ya watu wengi katika maisha yake mafupi, wakiwemo wauguzi waliomtunza wakati wa kukaa kwake hospitalini. Hadassah bado anakumbuka kuona baadhi ya wauguzi wakilia katika mazishi ya Esther. Je, unaona Hadassah atamsahau Esther? Kamwe!

Mbali na kuwa rafiki yake wa karibu, jambo jingine lililokuwa muhimili kwa Hadassah ni kuwa alipokuwa Esther shuleni wasichana wengine hawakuwa wakiwa mkali kwake (Hadassah). Ilikuwa hivyo hadi takriban darasa la nne, Esther alianza kuwa shuleni mara kwa mara. Siku moja alirudi nyumbani na kumuambia wazazi wake yale aliyoyaona shuleni—jinsi wasichana walivyokuwa dhidi ya Hadassah na walivyokuwa wakimdhulumu. Baba wa Esther alileta tatizo hili kwenye mkutano ufuatao wa wazazi/walimu. Ni mabadiliko gani ghafla yaliyoanza siku iliyofuata! Mmoja wa wasichana hata alimjia Hadassah na kumwomba msamaha. Hatimaye, wote waliweza kuwa marafiki na leo hao wasichana ni “marafiki zake wa zamani wa shule” wa Hadassah.

Inafaa kusimama kando ya mtu anayetiwa mnyanyaso. Msaada wako unaweza kuwa kile ambacho Mungu atakitumia kumsaidia rafiki yako kupitia nyakati ngumu kwa njia nzuri! Na shiriki hilo na wazazi wako, wao wanaweza kusaidia kutafuta njia ya kubadilisha tatizo.
