Katika miaka michache iliyopita, jambo ambalo Mungu amekuwa akilifanya moyoni mwangu ni eneo la utii. Sitaki kuangalia nyuma kwa njia isiyo sahihi, lakini ninaona mahali nilikoshindwa kwa mume wangu katika nafasi ambayo Mungu amenipa niliweze kufanya kama msaidizi wake, anayemfaa. Nikiwa nimekuwa nikitafakari juu ya maisha yangu mwenyewe, nimegundua jinsi jukumu letu lilivyo muhimu sisi wanawake Wakristo, katika nyumbani kwetu na katika maisha ya watoto wetu.

Ninaelewa kwamba watoto wetu watahitaji kufanya uamuzi wao wenyewe linapokuja suala la kuwa mwanafuasi wa Kristo, lakini tamaa yangu ni kwamba mimi siwe sababu watoto wetu wakatwike dhidi ya Neno la Mungu. Tunapomheshimu waume zetu kwa namna ambayo Mungu ameifundisha katika Neno lake, mfano wa maisha yetu utawavuta wasiokuwa waaminifu kwa Kristo. Kwa mwili, hatutaweza kumheshimu mume wetu kwa njia itakayompa utukufu Mungu, lakini kwa Kristo tunaweza kufanya mambo yote kulingana na mapenzi Yake.

Nina uchungu kuhusu hili kwa sababu katika miezi michache iliyopita nimegundua jinsi nyumba zetu zilivyo chini ya shambulio la mara kwa mara kutoka kwa adui wa nafsi zetu, anapojaribu kutumia nafsi zetu na dunia. Ninapoandika hili, sijisikii kwamba nitamfanya haki ipatikane kwa uandishi huu, hivyo nitaandika tu baadhi ya mawazo yangu na kuomba kwamba wote watakaosoma makala hii wategemekewe katika ndoa zao kuheshimu, kuwatambua, na kuwapenda waume zao.

  • Nevertheless let … the wife see that she reverence her husband –Ephesians 5:33.
  • Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands… –1 Peter 3:1.
  • Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are… –1 Peter 3:6.
  • Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord –Ephesians 5:22.
  • But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God –1 Corinthians 11:3.
  • Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence. For Adam was first formed, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression –1 Timothy 2:11-14.
  • Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be [subject] to their own husbands in every thing –Ephesians 5:24.
  • Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law –1 Corinthians 14:34.

Haya Maandiko si yangu mimi mwenyewe, bali ya Mungu. Anatupa Neno Lake tusome na kuishi kwa maana hiyo ndiyo njia pekee tutakapoweza kuwa na amani na muafaka katika nyumba zetu. Zaidi ya hayo, njia PEKEYE tunayoweza kuwa na dhamiri safi mbele za Mungu ni tunapokuwa katikati ya mapenzi Yake.

Tunapofikiri juu ya utii, nini kinakuja akilini? Je, tunafikiri kwamba tukitiifu, tutadhulumiwa? Je, tunafikiri kwamba sisi ni wenye busara kuliko waume zetu? Najua kwa mwili hili linaweza kuonekana kigumu, lakini kama tungeweza kutambua tu kwamba tukimzuia mume wetu kuongoza na kufanya maamuzi, tunamlemaza tu. Ukweli ni kwamba ikiwa waume zetu watatenda makosa, sawa kwa sababu sisi pia tunajitenda makosa. Pia, kama tumezaliwa upya, na tunatembea na Mungu, lakini waume zetu hawako, Mungu bado atatutunza. Maandiko yanafundisha kwamba ikiwa mume wako sio katika nafasi yake, basi kupitia mke kutembea kulingana na mafundisho wazi ambayo Mungu amempa katika Neno Lake, mume anaweza kushindaniwa kupitia mazungumzo yake (au kwa jinsi anavyoendesha maisha yake).

Tunahitaji kumtumaini Mungu kwa maisha yetu yote, hata katika eneo la ndoa yetu. Mungu ni Mungu wa utaratibu. Fikiria jinsi Mungu anavyotaka watoto waheshimu wazazi na wazazi wasiwachochee watoto wao kuwa hasira; si tofauti katika uhusiano wa mume na mke. Mume anapaswa kumpenda mke wake kama Kristo anavyopenda kanisa, na mke anapaswa kumheshimu mume wake.

Mwanzo, Mungu aliumba mwanaume na mwanamke. Aliumba Adamu na akasema kwamba sivyo vya heri mwanaume kuwa pekee; kisha Aliumba mwanamke kutoka kwa mfupa wa kando ya Adamu. Moyo wa Mungu mwanzoni ulikuwa kwamba mwanaume na mwanamke wangekuwa wamoja, na pamoja wangekutana na Mungu na kumtukuzisha. Kisha kupitia Adamu na Eva kukubali kujaribiwa, dhambi ilileta duniani. Kila tunapopambana katika ndoa zetu, ninakumbushwa jinsi ilivyokuwa Eva ndiye aliyekubali kwanza jaribio la tundu. Tuwe sisi wanawake haraka kuchunguza mioyo yetu ili kuwa na uhakika kwamba tuko katika nafasi yetu. Wakati hali zinaibuka, mara ngapi sisi wanawake tunajaribiwa kufikiri kwamba tunajua vyema na tunaweza kushughulikia hali hiyo vyema kuliko waume zetu.

Mungu ameunda waume zetu kuwa walinzi wetu ikiwa tutaendelea kuwa chini yao. Nafahamu kwamba sisi sio kamilifu, na hilo linafanya iwe changamoto zaidi kuwasaliti waume zetu. Hata hivyo, ninaamini kwamba tunapo zaliwa upya kwa Roho wa Mungu, upendo wake ndani yetu unatuwezesha kumtii waume zetu. Pia ninaelewa kuwa kuna nyumba nyingi zilizo broken. Usisimke wangu kwa yeyote aliyepo katika hali isiyo nzuri kabisa ni kuomba kwa dhati… kwanza kwa ajili yako mwenyewe ili uweze kutembea kwa njia isiyo na lawama na pia kwa mume wako kwamba awe kile Mungu alimuumba kuwa—si kile unachodhani anapaswa kuwa. Mara nyingi, tunachanganyikiwa kuhusu hili na inatusababisha kuwa na mawazo mabaya kuhusu waume zetu.

Tito unatupatia sisi ndugu mwelekeo wazi kutoka kwa Mungu. The aged women likewise, that they be … teachers of good things; That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed –Titus 2:3-5.

Jitihada nyingine ambayo sisi wanawake tunakutana nayo ni kulinganisha waume zetu na wanaume wengine. Labda tungaambia waume zetu kwamba huyu mwanamume hange fanya hivi na hivyo kwa namna unayofanya, au njia anavyo fanya jambo ni bora kuliko yako. Labda hata hatusemi maneno haya, lakini matendo yetu yanaweza kumwambia mume wako mengi. Neno la Mungu linatufundisha kuwa walewale watii waume zao wenyewe, si waume wengine. Kila mume amepewa kipawa kwa njia tofauti, na ndiyo sababu kila mke amefaa hasa kwa mume wake. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help [helper, aid, supporter] meet [suitable, appropriate, complementary] for him –Genesis 2:18.

That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children –Titus 2:4. Neno “love,” katika to love their husbands linamaanisha “kuwa na mapenzi ya kimoyo kwa mume wao” ikilinganishwa na neno “love” katika to love their children ambalo linamaanisha “kuwa na upendo wa uzazi kwa watoto wao”. Ni aina gani ya upendo tunayomwonyesha waume wetu? Je, waume wetu wanaweza kutuamini kwamba tuna tu mema yao akilini, au tunadhihirisha upendo kwa ajili ya kupata kitu kwa kurudisha? Upendo wa kweli utasamehe licha ya kushindwa, hata wakati tunafikiri maumivu ni makubwa mno kuvumilia. Upendo wa kweli utatufanya tuombe kwa ajili yetu na waume zetu tunapokuwepo tofauti kuhusu jambo fulani kuliko wao. Upendo wa kweli hautatusababishii kukata tamaa, bali utatufanya tumtazame Mungu zaidi.

Tunapojaribiwa kuzungumza kuhusu dosari za waume zetu kwa wengine, tusikubali jaribio hilo bali tuombe kwa ajili yao. Je, tungefahamu waume wetu wakizungumza kuhusu dosari zetu kwa watu wengine? Pia, ombeni uelewa wa kujua ikiwa, na lini, kusema na mtu kuhusu dhambi ambayo mume wako anaweza kuwa amejihusisha nayo. Tusilaumu au kuudhiwa waume wetu wakati matatizo yanapotokea. Badala yake, tuombe Mungu afanye kazi ndani ya maisha yetu na tumgeukie Yeye na kuacha tatizo kwa Yeye. Waume zetu ni wanadamu tu, kama sisi tulivyo. Tukishindwa wakati mwingine, basi tusishangaze kwamba wao pia wanaweza kushindwa wakati mwingine. Nafikiri kinachofanya ndoa zetu kuwa kamilifu ni kwamba tunajifunza kusamehe kila mmoja na kusonga mbele kuwa wamoja.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation [conduct] of the wives; While they behold your chaste [modest, innocent, perfect, pure] conversation coupled with fear. Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement [terror]. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-2 & 3:6-7.

Mojawapo ya mara za kwanza wakati aya hii ilitufikia kwa dhati ilikuwa wakati mtoto wetu wa kwanza alikuwa takriban miezi mitano. Tulikuwa umbali fulani na nyumbani na alianza kulia kwa maumivu mengi. Tulisali kwa ajili yake, lakini bado alilia. Hatuwezi kuelewa kilichokuwa kosa, hivyo tumpeleka Idara ya Dharura. Walituambia alikuwa na maambukizi ya sikio na wakatupatia dawa. Hata hivyo, bado alilia. Tulikuwa na safari ya saa kumi kwenda nyumbani, na alilia yote wakati wa safari. Baada tulipofika nyumbani, mume wangu na mimi tukagundua kwamba kulikuwa na mambo yaliyorukwa baina yetu. Baada ya kutubu makosa yetu kwa kila mmoja na kwa Mungu, tulimsali tena kwa ajili ya mtoto wetu. Mara baada ya kusali, mtoto wetu alisitisha kulia. Sijui kila hali inaisha kama hii, lakini Mungu alitufundisha kwamba tunapaswa kuwa wazi kwa kila mmoja bila dhambi iliyofichika, ili sala zetu zisizuilike.

Maswali kadhaa ambayo yanaweza kuulizwa ni: Watoto wetu wanaona nini katika nyumba zetu? Je, wanaona Mama akimuheshimu baba kwa furaha au kwa hofu? Je, wanaona Mama akiwa muwivu kwa mume wake kwa njia inayofaa, kama kupitia maneno ya wema, kutaka kupenda vitu anavyovipenda, kushikilia mikono, nk. (Nimejifunza kwamba ni vigumu kushikilia mikono na mume wangu ikiwa kuna kitu kati yetu.) Je, Mama huhoji, kupinga, au kumkosoa Baba kwa anachofanya?

Wakati watoto wetu wenyewe wanakua na kuingia katika miaka ya ujana, ninaona jinsi nguvu zake ni muhimu kwamba kanuni hizi ziishiwe katika nyumba zetu. Ikiwa tukihoji wazi mamlaka ya mume wetu, naamini tunapanda mbegu kwa watoto wetu kwamba nao watashusha shaka mamlaka ya baba yao. Mwishowe, katika wakati tunaouishi, tunaona kizazi kinachouliza kila kitu kinachohusu utaratibu wa Mungu wa uumbaji—kuna vurugu za jinsia, nadharia ya uumbaji kwa mageuzi, na uasi dhidi ya mamlaka kwa ujumla. Mara nyingi nimejiuliza ikiwa labda sababu ya kuona uasi mwingi katika makanisa yetu ya kawaida ni kwa sababu utaratibu wa Mungu hauishiwi ndani ya nyumba zetu.

Kulikuwa na rafiki yetu aliyetuambia kwamba kama kungekuwa na kanuni moja ya Kikristo aliyedhani itakuwa na athari kubwa zaidi kwa nyumbani, ingekuwa kanuni ya utaratibu wa uongozi. Tuna rafiki mpendwa ambaye alikuwa amekuwa Mkristo kabla ya mume wake. Alipitia nyakati nyingi za shida, lakini aliendelea kumpenda na kumheshimu mume wake. Alifunga na kuomba kwa miaka mingi kwa ajili ya mume wake. Leo mume wake atashuhudia kwamba ilikuwa kwa sababu ya mwenendo wa mke wake wa kumtumika Mungu uliomvutia kwa toba na imani kwa Kristo.

Mfano mwingine wenye matokeo tofauti… Ninamjua jozi ambayo hawakuwa na ndoa imara. Mume hakukuwa katika nafasi yake na mke akawa mwenye chuki, chuki kiasi kwamba alisema kwamba anapotoka kwa kaburi, hataki kuzikwa pembeni ya mume wake. Chuki hiyo mwingi imekuwa na athari mbaya kwa watoto wao. Nilijiuliza kama hakuwa amekuwa mwepesi, angeweza angalau kumwachia watoto wake kutoka kwa maumivu mengi ambayo wamepata.

Ninajua pia wa jozi nyingine ambako wote wawili walitendewa vibaya sana na familia karibu, lakini walichagua kutokuwa wenye chuki. Walikua karibu zaidi na Mungu na kwa kila mmoja kupitia vilima hivyo na wanavuna matokeo ya matunda ya chaguo lao hadi leo.

Hata karibu nyumbani… Niliokulia katika nyumba ambayo haikuwa nyumba ya Kikristo. Wazazi wangu hawakuwa wametangazwa kuwa wapya. Walipoanza kumruhusu Mungu afanye kazi moyoni mwao, ningeweza kuona. Ningeenda nyumbani kutoka mikutano na kumuona baba yangu akisombwa macho alipoisoma Biblia yake. Pia, siku moja nilirudi nyumbani na kuona wazazi wangu wamekaa mezani wakiena pamoja. Nitasema kwamba hili lilikuwa na athari kubwa maishani mwangu. Ningeweza pia kuona mama yangu akikazia kuwa katika nafasi yake kama Mungu alivyomuumba kuwa. Tunapotoka katika maisha haya, familia yetu watasema nini kuhusu sisi? Je, watashuhudia kwamba upendo wa Mungu ulikuwa miteremko katika miili yetu ya mtu?

Kwa upande wa vitendo, niliona nitataja njia chache ambazo tunaweza kuonyesha kwamba tunawapenda waume wetu kwa vitendo na sio kwa maneno tu.

  • Kuwaona kwa ushauri (si tu kupambana na kile tunachodhani)
  • Kutengeneza vyakula wanavyopenda
  • Kuweka nyumba katika utaratibu na usafi
  • Kuwa tayari na kupenda kuacha mipango yetu kusaidia waume zetu na chochote wanachohitaji
  • Kuwakaribisha mlango kwa tabasamu (bila kujali jinsi siku ilivyokuwa mbaya)
  • Kuweka nyumba kimya, hata na watoto wadogo, anapojaribu kupumzika au kusoma
  • Kuwafundisha watoto wetu adabu sahihi katika kuhusiana na kila mmoja nyumbani
  • Kuwafundisha watoto wetu kumpenda na kumheshimu baba yao, hata kama si kila wakati amekuwa mkamilifu

Changamoto nyingine ninayotaka kuwapa kila dada mliyooa ni kufikiria kitu ambacho unaweza kumuambia mume wako kwamba umebarikiwa naye; jaribu kufanya hivi kila siku kwa wiki mbili. Ni ajabu jinsi wema unaweza kuleta athari kwa ndoa. Labda kwa wengine hili litaonekana kazi ngumu, lakini si hivyo. Ninashangazwa kwamba tunapokomaa, tunafikiri mengi kwa namna ileile, mara nyingine tukikamilisha hata sentensi za kila mmoja. Ninatambua kuna mengi zaidi yangekuwa yameandikwa. Nina tumaini kwamba Mungu ataendelea kutufungulia Neno Lake tukiomtazama Yeye.

Editor’s Note:

Mimi nilikuwa mmoja aliyepambana sana kwa miaka mingi bila kujua jinsi ya kuwasaliti na bado kutaka kufanya hivyo. Hapa chini ni jaribangu la kushiriki kile Mungu amenifundisha.

Mojawapo ya sababu kuu nyingi watu wanapambana na “utii” ni kwamba hawafahamu hasa Mungu anamaanisha nini kuhusu somo hilo—hawafahamu uhalisia wa utii wa kibiblia. Kwa kawaida, mtu anajua anachomwamini kuhusu somo fulani, hivyo akidhani anapoulizwa “kuwasaliti” katika suala hilo, wanafikiri wanajiulizwa kukubali imani yao ya kibinafsi—au kuasi dhana yao ya dhamiri.

Jibu ni kwa njia mbili.

Kwanza, ikiwa watu wawili wanakubaliana juu ya suala, basi hakuna haja kwa mtu yeyote kuwasaliti. Kwa hiyo, kutilia tusiwi sio lazima kwamba mtu anayewasaliti lazima abadilishe mawazo yake, badala yake wachoose kuunga mkono uamuzi wa mtu mwingine kulingana na ukweli kwamba Mungu anasema mtu huyo ndiye anayeashiria kuwajibika kwa maamuzi ya upande huo—iwe ni wawili, nyumbani, shule, kanisa, nk.

Pili, Mungu alijua kwamba wakati kuna watu zaidi ya mmoja wanajadili uamuzi unaohitajika kufanywa, kwamba itamaanisha kila mara moja atakuwa akimtii mwingine. Hivyo, kutoa uwazi juu ya uwajibikaji, Anakabidhi mwelekeo wazi kuhusu nani anayeona mwenyewe kuwa mtu anayewajibika (mamlaka ya kiroho) katika kila aina ya hali—mume katika ndoa, baba katika familia, mwanaume (kichwa) nyumbani, viongozi walioagizwa kanisani, walimu/mkuu wa shule katika mazingira ya shule, nk. Kwa njia hiyo kila mtu anaweza kujua nani Mungu anamwona yeye kuwa na uwajibikaji kwa makosa yoyote yanayotokea.

Tafakari kwamba ingawa Eva alichukua tunda na kula kwanza, kisha akampa mumewe kuliwa, Mungu anatupa uwazi kuhusu nani anayeachiliwa kuwajibika kwa kushindwa hilo (dhambi). Wherefore, as by one man [not one woman] sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned … Nevertheless death reigned from Adam [not from Eve] to Moses, even over them [Adam’s descendants—all of the human race] that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression… –Romans 5:12-14.

Hivyo, tunaona kwamba Mungu anatoa ulinzi na usalama kwa wote walio chini ya mamlaka ikiwa watalinda chini ya mamlaka hiyo. Yeye ambaye Mungu kwa wazi anasema ndiye kielelezo cha mamlaka katika kila uhusiano ataendelea kuwa ndiye atakayewajibishwa kwa maamuzi yaliyofanywa na kundi hilo la watu. Kama ilivyokuwa katika kuanguka katika Bustani ya Edeni, dhambi za kutokufanya na za kufanya ndani ya kila familia zitaletewa kwa walio kwa hesabu ya baba. Iwe baba alikuwa akitoa mwelekeo mbaya kwa familia au hakutoa mwelekeo kabisa, haijalishi, bado atahesabiwa kwani Mungu anaona mwanaume kuwa kichwa cha nyumbani mwake. (angalia 1 Corinthians 11:3 na Romans 13:12)

In the last couple of years, something that God has been working on in my heart is the area of submission. I don’t want to look back in a wrong way, but I see where I have failed my husband in the role that God has given for me to function as his helper, one that is meet for him. As I have been thinking about my own life, I have come to realize how important our role is as Christian women, in our homes and in the lives of our children.

I realize that our children are going to need to make their own decision when it comes to being a disciple of Christ, but my desire is that I am not the reason that our children rebel against the Word of God. When we honor our husbands the way that God has taught in His Word, the example of our lives will draw the unbelieving to Christ. In the flesh, we will not be able to honor our husbands in a way that will bring glory to God, but with Christ we can do all things according to His will.

I have a burden about this because in the last couple of months I have noticed how much our homes are under constant attack from the enemy of our souls, as he tries to use our flesh and the world. As I write on this, I don’t feel that I will do justice to it, so I will just write some of my thoughts and pray that all who read this article will be encouraged in their marriages to honor, respect, and love their husbands.

  • Nevertheless let … the wife see that she reverence her husband –Ephesians 5:33.
  • Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands… –1 Peter 3:1.
  • Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are… –1 Peter 3:6.
  • Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord –Ephesians 5:22.
  • But I would have you know, that the head of every man is Christ; and the head of the woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God –1 Corinthians 11:3.
  • Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence. For Adam was first formed, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression –1 Timothy 2:11-14.
  • Therefore as the church is subject unto Christ, so let the wives be [subject] to their own husbands in every thing –Ephesians 5:24.
  • Let your women keep silence in the churches: for it is not permitted unto them to speak; but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law –1 Corinthians 14:34.

These Scriptures are not my own, but God’s. He gives us His Word to read and to live by because that is the only way we will be able to have peace and harmony in our homes. Even more importantly, the ONLY way that we can have a clear conscience before God is when we are in the center of His will.

When we think of submission, what comes to mind? Do we think that if we submit, we will be taken advantage of? Do we think that we are wiser than our husbands? I know to the flesh this sounds kind of hard, but if we could only realize that if we don’t allow our husbands to lead out and make decisions, we are only crippling them. The reality is that if our husbands make mistakes, it is okay because we ourselves make mistakes as well. Also, if we are born again, and we are walking with God, but our husbands are not, God will still take care of us. The Scriptures teach that if our husband is not in his place, then through the wife walking according to the clear teaching that God has given her in His Word, the husband can be won through her conversation (or by the way she conducts her life).

We need to trust God with our whole lives, even in the area of our marriage. God is a God of order. Think of how God desires the children to honor the parents and the parents to not provoke their children to anger; it’s no different in the husband-and-wife relationship. The husband is to love his wife as Christ loves the church, and the wife is to reverence her husband.

In the beginning, God created male and female. He created Adam and said that it was not good for man to be alone; then He created woman from the rib of Adam’s side. God’s heart in the beginning was that man and woman would be one, and together they would walk with God and glorify Him. Then through Adam and Eve yielding to temptation, sin was brought into the world. Whenever we are struggling in our marriage, I am reminded how it was Eve that first yielded to the serpent’s temptation. Let us as wives be quick to examine our own hearts to be sure that we are in our place. When situations arise, how often are we as women tempted to think that we know better and could handle the situation better than our husbands.

God has designed our husbands to be our protector if we stay under them. I realize that we are imperfect, and that makes it more challenging to submit to our husbands. However, I believe that when we are born again by the Spirit of God, His love in us enables us to submit to our husbands. I also realize that there are a lot of broken homes. My encouragement to anyone who is in a less than ideal situation is to sincerely pray…first for yourself that you can walk in a blameless way and also for your husband that he would be what God has designed him to be—not what you think he should be. Many times, we get confused about this and it causes us to have bad thoughts about our husbands.

Titus gives us sisters clear direction from God. The aged women likewise, that they be … teachers of good things; That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children, To be discreet, chaste, keepers at home, good, obedient to their own husbands, that the word of God be not blasphemed –Titus 2:3-5.

Another temptation that we women face is to compare our husbands with other men. Perhaps we tell our husbands that this other man wouldn’t do such and such the way you do, or the way he does something is better than the way you do. Maybe we don’t even say these words, but our actions can tell our husbands a lot. God’s Word teaches us to be obedient to our own husbands, and not another. Each husband is gifted in a different way, and that is why each wife is especially suited for their husband. And the LORD God said, It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help [helper, aid, supporter] meet [suitable, appropriate, complementary] for him –Genesis 2:18.

That they may teach the young women to be sober, to love their husbands, to love their children –Titus 2:4. The word “love,” in to love their husbands means “to be affectionately fond of their man” as compared to the word “love” in to love their children which means “to have a maternal fondness for one’s children”. What kind of love are we showing our husbands? Can our husbands trust us that we only have their good in mind, or do we pretend to love in order to get something in return? True love will forgive in spite of failures, even when we think the pain is too great to bear. True love will cause us to pray for ourselves and our husbands when we feel differently about something than they do. True love will not cause us to despair, rather it will cause us to seek God even more.

When we are tempted to speak about our husbands’ faults to others, let us not yield to that temptation but let’s pray for them. Would we appreciate our husbands talking about our faults to other people? Also, pray for discernment to know if, and when, to speak to someone about a sin that your husband may be involved in. Let us not rail on or nag our husbands when difficulties arise. Instead, let us ask God to work in our lives and give the problem to Him and let it there. Our husbands are only too human, just as we are. If we fail at times, then we must not be surprised that they too might fail at times as well. I think what makes our marriages perfect is that we learn to forgive one another and press on to be one together.

Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation [conduct] of the wives; While they behold your chaste [modest, innocent, perfect, pure] conversation coupled with fear. Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement [terror]. Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered –1 Peter 3:1-2 & 3:6-7.

One of the first times that this verse became real to us was when our first child was around five months old. We were quite a ways from home and he started crying with a lot of pain. We prayed for him, but he still cried. We could not figure out what was wrong, so we took him into the ER. They told us that he had an ear infection and gave us medication. However, he still cried. We had a ten-hour journey home, and he cried the whole way. After we had gotten home, my husband and I discovered that there were some unresolved things between us. After we confessed our wrongs to each other and to God, we prayed again for our son. Immediately after we prayed, our son quit crying. I know not every situation turns out like this one did, but God taught us that we need to be open with each other with no hidden sin, that our prayers be not hindered.

Some questions that could be asked are: What are our children seeing in our homes? Do they see Mom reverencing their dad with joy or with fear? Do they see Mom being appropriately affectionate with her husband, such as through kind words, seeking to love the things that he loves, holding hands, etc. (I have come to realize that it is difficult to hold hands with my husband if there is something between us.) Does Mom question, challenge, or criticize what Dad does?

As our own children are growing older and into their youth years, I see how important it is that these principles are lived out in our homes. If we openly question our husband’s authority, I believe we are sowing a seed in our children that they too will question their dad’s authority. Ultimately, in the time that we live, we are seeing a generation that is questioning everything about God’s created order—there is gender confusion, evolution, and rebellion against authority in general. I have often wondered if perhaps the reason that we see so much rebellion in our plain churches is because of God’s order not being lived out in our homes.

There was a friend of ours who told us that if there would be one Christian principle that he thought would have the most impact on the home, it would be the principle of the headship order. We have a dear friend who had become a Christian before her husband. She went through a lot of difficult times, but she continued to love and reverence her husband. She fasted and prayed for many years for her husband. Today her husband will testify that it was because of his wife’s godly conduct that drew him to repentance and faith in Christ.

Another example with a different outcome… I know of a couple that didn’t have a solid marriage. The husband was not in his place and the wife became bitter, so bitter in fact, that she said that when she is buried in the grave, she doesn’t want to be buried beside her husband. This much bitterness has had a terrible effect on their children. I wondered if she had not become bitter, if she could have at least spared her children from the many heartaches that they have suffered.

I also know of another couple where both of them were badly mistreated by close family, but they chose not to become bitter. They drew closer to God and to each other through those valleys and they are reaping the benefits of the fruit of their choices to this day.

Even closer to home… I grew up in a home that was not a Christian home. Neither of my parents were born again. When they began to allow God to work in their hearts, I could see it. I would come home from gatherings and see my dad weeping as he was reading his Bible. Also, on one particular evening I came home and saw my parents sitting at the table and they were singing together. I will testify that this had a tremendous effect on my life. I could also see my own mother desiring to be in her place as God had designed her to be. When we pass from this life, what will our family say about us? Will they testify that the love of God reigned in our mortal bodies?

On a practical note, I thought I would write a few ways that we can show that we love our husbands in deed and not just in word.

  • Asking them for advice (not just going on what we think)
  • Fixing their favorite foods
  • Keeping the house orderly and neat
  • Being ready and willing to drop our plans to help our husbands with whatever they need
  • Meeting them at the door with a smile (no matter how bad of day we may have had)
  • Keeping the house quiet, even with little children, when he’s trying to rest or study
  • Teaching our children proper manners in relating to each other in the home
  • Teaching our children to love and respect their father, even if he isn’t always perfect

Another challenge I wish to give to each married sister is to think of something that you can tell your husband that you are blessed about with him, Try doing this every day for two weeks. It’s amazing what effect kindness can have on a marriage. Maybe to some this would seem like drudgery, but it’s not. I am amazed that as we get older, how much we think alike, even sometimes finishing each other’s sentences. I realize there is so much more that could have been written. I trust that God will continue to open His Word to us as we seek Him.

Editor’s Note:

I was one who struggled majorly and for years with not knowing how to submit and yet wanting to. Following is my attempt to share what God has been teaching me.

One of the main reasons that many people struggle with “submission” is that they don’t really understand what God means with the subject—they don’t understand the reality of biblical submission. Usually, a person knows what they believe on a certain subject, so in their mind when they are being asked to “submit” on that point, they think they are being asked to compromise their personal belief—or sin against their conscience.

The answer is two-fold.

First, if two people agree on an issue, then there is no need for anyone to submit. Thus, to submit does not mean that the person submitting is necessarily changing their mind, rather they are choosing to support the other person’s decision based on the fact that God says that that person is the one He is holding responsible for the decisions of that party—whether it be a couple, the home, a school, a church, etc.

Second, God knew that whenever there would be more than one person discussing a decision that needs to be made, that it would always mean that the one would end up submitting to the other. Therefore, to provide clarity in responsibility, He gives clear direction regarding whom He considers the responsible person (the spiritual authority) in each type of situation—the husband in a marriage, the father in the family, the man (the head) in the home, the ordained leaders in the church, the schoolteachers/principal in the school setting, etc. That way everyone can know who God sees as responsible for any mistakes that are made.

Consider that even though Eve took the fruit and ate it first, and then gave it to her husband to eat, God provides us with clarity regarding who He holds responsible for that failure (sin). Wherefore, as by one man [not one woman] sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned … Nevertheless death reigned from Adam [not from Eve] to Moses, even over them [Adam’s descendants—all of the human race] that had not sinned after the similitude of Adam’s transgression… –Romans 5:12-14.

So, we see that God provides protection and security to all those who are under authority if they stay under that authority. The one who God clearly states as being the authority figure in each relationship will always be the one that God holds responsible for decisions made by that group of people. Just like in the fall in the Garden of Eden, sins of omission and of commission within each family will be primarily held to dad’s account. Whether dad was giving wrong direction to the family or if he was not giving direction at all, it doesn’t matter, he will still be held to account since God sees the man as being the head of his home. (see 1 Corinthians 11:3 and Romans 13:12)

Au cours des deux dernières années, quelque chose sur lequel Dieu a travaillé dans mon cœur concerne la soumission. Je ne veux pas regarder en arrière de manière erronée, mais je vois où j’ai failli envers mon mari dans le rôle que Dieu m’a donné pour fonctionner comme son aide, une aide qui lui convienne. En réfléchissant à ma propre vie, j’ai réalisé combien notre rôle en tant que femmes chrétiennes est important, dans nos foyers et dans la vie de nos enfants.

Je comprends que nos enfants devront prendre leur propre décision quand il s’agira d’être disciple du Christ, mais mon désir est que je ne sois pas la raison pour laquelle nos enfants se rebellent contre la Parole de Dieu. Lorsque nous honorons nos maris comme Dieu l’a enseigné dans Sa Parole, l’exemple de nos vies attirera les incroyants vers Christ. Dans la chair, nous ne pourrons pas honorer nos maris d’une manière qui glorifie Dieu, mais avec Christ nous pouvons faire toutes choses selon Sa volonté.

J’ai une préoccupation à ce sujet parce que, ces derniers mois, j’ai remarqué à quel point nos foyers sont sous attaque constante de l’ennemi de nos âmes, qui essaie d’utiliser notre chair et le monde. En écrivant ceci, je ne pense pas en faire pleinement justice, donc je vais simplement coucher sur le papier quelques-unes de mes pensées et prier que tous ceux qui liront cet article soient encouragés dans leurs mariages à honorer, respecter et aimer leurs maris.

  • Néanmoins que… la femme voie qu’elle craigne son mari – Éphésiens 5:33.
  • Semblablement, vous les femmes, soyez soumises à vos propres maris… – 1 Pierre 3:1.
  • Comme Sara obéissait à Abraham, l’appelant seigneur : vous en êtes les filles… – 1 Pierre 3:6.
  • Femmes, soyez soumises à vos propres maris, comme au Seigneur – Éphésiens 5:22.
  • Je veux cependant que vous sachiez que le chef de tout homme, c’est Christ; et le chef de la femme, c’est l’homme; et le chef de Christ, c’est Dieu – 1 Corinthiens 11:3.
  • Que la femme apprenne dans le silence avec toute soumission. Je ne permets pas à la femme d’enseigner, ni d’avoir autorité sur l’homme, mais d’être dans le silence. Car Adam fut formé le premier, puis Eve. Et Adam ne fut pas séduit, mais la femme, ayant été séduite, fut dans la transgression – 1 Timothée 2:11-14.
  • Comme l’Église est soumise à Christ, que les femmes soient [soumises] à leurs propres maris en toutes choses – Éphésiens 5:24.
  • Que vos femmes se taisent dans les assemblées : car il ne leur est pas permis de parler; mais qu’elles soient soumises, comme le dit aussi la loi – 1 Corinthiens 14:34.

Ces Écritures ne sont pas miennes, mais de Dieu. Il nous donne Sa Parole pour la lire et la vivre car c’est la seule façon d’avoir la paix et l’harmonie dans nos foyers. Plus important encore, la SEULE façon d’avoir une conscience claire devant Dieu est d’être au centre de Sa volonté.

Quand nous pensons à la soumission, qu’est-ce qui nous vient à l’esprit ? Pensons-nous que si nous nous soumettons, on profitera de nous ? Pensons-nous que nous sommes plus sages que nos maris ? Je sais que, dans la chair, cela paraît assez dur, mais si seulement nous pouvions réaliser que si nous n’autorisons pas nos maris à diriger et à prendre des décisions, nous les rendons simplement incapables. La réalité est que si nos maris commettent des erreurs, ce n’est pas grave parce que nous-mêmes faisons aussi des erreurs. De plus, si nous sommes nées de nouveau et que nous marchons avec Dieu, mais que nos maris ne le sont pas, Dieu prendra quand même soin de nous. Les Écritures enseignent que si notre mari n’est pas à sa place, alors par la femme qui marche selon l’enseignement clair que Dieu lui a donné dans Sa Parole, le mari peut être gagné par leur conversation (ou par la manière dont elle conduit sa vie).

Nous devons faire confiance à Dieu pour toute notre vie, même dans le domaine de notre mariage. Dieu est un Dieu d’ordre. Pensez à la façon dont Dieu désire que les enfants honorent les parents et que les parents ne provoquent pas leurs enfants à la colère ; ce n’est pas différent dans la relation mari-femme. Le mari doit aimer sa femme comme Christ aime l’Église, et la femme doit révérer son mari.

Au commencement, Dieu créa l’homme et la femme. Il créa Adam et dit qu’il n’était pas bon que l’homme soit seul ; puis Il créa la femme à partir de la côte d’Adam. Le cœur de Dieu au commencement était que l’homme et la femme seraient un, et ensemble ils marcheraient avec Dieu et Le glorifieraient. Puis, par la capitulation d’Adam et Ève à la tentation, le péché entra dans le monde. Chaque fois que nous avons des difficultés dans notre mariage, je me rappelle qu’Eve fut la première à céder à la tentation du serpent. Soyons, en tant que femmes, promptes à examiner nos propres cœurs pour nous assurer que nous sommes à notre place. Quand des situations surviennent, combien de fois sommes-nous tentées en tant que femmes de penser que nous savons mieux et que nous pourrions gérer la situation mieux que nos maris ?

Dieu a conçu nos maris pour être nos protecteurs si nous restons sous eux. Je reconnais que nous sommes imparfaites, et cela rend plus difficile la soumission à nos maris. Cependant, je crois que lorsque nous sommes nées de nouveau par l’Esprit de Dieu, Son amour en nous nous permet de nous soumettre à nos maris. Je reconnais aussi qu’il y a beaucoup de foyers brisés. Mon encouragement à quiconque se trouve dans une situation moins qu’idéal est de prier sincèrement… d’abord pour vous-même afin que vous puissiez marcher d’une manière irréprochable et aussi pour votre mari afin qu’il devienne ce que Dieu l’a conçu pour être — pas ce que vous pensez qu’il devrait être. Bien des fois, nous sommes confuses à ce sujet et cela nous fait avoir de mauvaises pensées à propos de nos maris.

Tite donne aux sœurs une direction claire de la part de Dieu. Les femmes âgées, de même, doivent être… enseignantes de ce qui est bien; afin qu’elles exhortent les jeunes femmes à être sobres, à aimer leurs maris, à aimer leurs enfants, à être discrètes, chastes, sages ménagères, bonnes, obéissantes à leurs propres maris, afin que la parole de Dieu ne soit pas blasphémée – Tite 2:3-5.

Une autre tentation que nous, femmes, affrontons est de comparer nos maris à d’autres hommes. Peut-être disons-nous à nos maris que cet autre homme ne ferait pas ceci ou cela de la façon dont tu le fais, ou que la façon dont il fait quelque chose est meilleure que la tienne. Peut-être ne prononçons-nous même pas ces mots, mais nos actions peuvent en dire long à nos maris. La Parole de Dieu nous enseigne d’être obéissantes à nos propres maris, et non à un autre. Chaque mari est doté d’un don différent, et c’est pourquoi chaque épouse est particulièrement adaptée à son mari. Et l’Éternel Dieu dit : Il n’est pas bon que l’homme soit seul; je lui ferai une aide [secours, auxiliaire, compagne] qui sera assortie [convenable, appropriée, complémentaire] pour lui – Genèse 2:18.

Qu’elles exhortent les jeunes femmes à être sobres, à aimer leurs maris, à aimer leurs enfants – Tite 2:4. Le mot « aimer », dans aimer leurs maris, signifie « éprouver de l’affection pour son homme » comparé au mot « aimer » dans aimer leurs enfants qui signifie « éprouver l’affection maternelle pour ses enfants ». Quel genre d’amour montrons-nous à nos maris ? Nos maris peuvent-ils nous faire confiance pour savoir que nous ne cherchons que leur bien, ou faisons-nous semblant d’aimer pour obtenir quelque chose en retour ? Le véritable amour pardonne malgré les échecs, même lorsque nous pensons que la douleur est trop grande à supporter. Le véritable amour nous poussera à prier pour nous-mêmes et pour nos maris quand nous pensons différemment de certaines choses. Le véritable amour ne nous fera pas désespérer, mais nous amènera à chercher Dieu encore davantage.

Quand nous sommes tentées de parler des défauts de nos maris à d’autres, ne cédons pas à cette tentation mais prions pour eux. Apprécierions-nous que nos maris parlent de nos défauts à d’autres personnes ? Prions aussi pour avoir le discernement de savoir si, et quand, parler à quelqu’un d’un péché que votre mari pourrait commettre. Ne vouons pas nos maris aux remontrances ou au harcèlement lorsque des difficultés surviennent. Au lieu de cela, demandons à Dieu d’œuvrer dans nos vies et remettons-Lui le problème et laissons-le là. Nos maris sont tout aussi humains que nous. Si nous faillons parfois, nous ne devons pas être surpris qu’eux aussi puissent faillir parfois. Je pense que ce qui rend nos mariages parfaits, c’est que nous apprenons à nous pardonner mutuellement et à persévérer pour être un ensemble.

Semblablement, vous les femmes, soyez soumises à vos propres maris; afin que, si quelqu’un n’obéit pas à la parole, il soit aussi gagné sans parole par la conduite [comportement] des femmes; Pendant qu’ils regardent votre conduite chaste [modeste, innocente, parfaite, pure] accompagnée de crainte. Comme Sara obéissait à Abraham, l’appelant seigneur: vous en êtes les filles, tant que vous faites le bien, et que vous n’êtes pas effrayées par aucun effroi [terreur]. De même, vous les maris, vivez avec elles selon la connaissance, honorant la femme, comme un vase plus faible, et comme étant héritiers ensemble de la grâce de la vie; afin que vos prières ne soient pas empêchées – 1 Pierre 3:1-2 & 3:6-7.

L’un des premiers moments où ce verset est devenu réel pour nous fut quand notre premier enfant avait environ cinq mois. Nous étions assez loin de chez nous et il a commencé à pleurer avec beaucoup de douleur. Nous avons prié pour lui, mais il pleurait encore. Nous ne comprenions pas ce qui n’allait pas, alors nous l’avons emmené aux urgences. Ils nous ont dit qu’il avait une infection de l’oreille et nous ont donné des médicaments. Cependant, il pleurait toujours. Nous avions un trajet de dix heures pour rentrer, et il a pleuré tout le long. Une fois rentrés, mon mari et moi avons découvert qu’il y avait des choses non résolues entre nous. Après nous être confessés nos torts l’un à l’autre et à Dieu, nous avons prié encore pour notre fils. Immédiatement après notre prière, notre fils cessa de pleurer. Je sais que toutes les situations ne se terminent pas ainsi, mais Dieu nous a appris que nous devons être ouverts les uns envers les autres sans péché caché, afin que nos prières ne soient pas empêchées.

Quelques questions qui pourraient être posées : Que voient nos enfants dans nos foyers ? Voient-ils Maman révérer leur père avec joie ou avec peur ? Voient-ils Maman être affectueuse de façon appropriée avec son mari, comme par des paroles aimables, cherchant à aimer les choses qu’il aime, se tenant la main, etc. (J’ai réalisé qu’il est difficile de se tenir la main avec mon mari s’il y a quelque chose entre nous.) Maman remet-elle en question, défie ou critique ce que Papa fait ?

Alors que nos propres enfants grandissent et entrent dans l’adolescence, je vois combien il est important que ces principes soient vécus dans nos foyers. Si nous remettons ouvertement en question l’autorité de notre mari, je crois que nous semons une graine chez nos enfants pour qu’eux aussi remettent en question l’autorité de leur père. Ultimement, à l’époque où nous vivons, nous voyons une génération qui remet tout en question concernant l’ordre créé par Dieu — il y a une confusion des genres, l’évolution, et une rébellion contre l’autorité en général. Je me suis souvent demandé si la raison pour laquelle nous voyons tant de rébellion dans nos églises simples ne viendrait pas du fait que l’ordre de Dieu n’est pas vécu dans nos foyers.

Un ami nous a dit que s’il fallait choisir un principe chrétien qui, selon lui, aurait le plus d’impact sur la famille, ce serait le principe de l’ordre de la tête (la tête). Nous avons une chère amie qui est devenue chrétienne avant son mari. Elle a traversé beaucoup de moments difficiles, mais elle a continué à aimer et à révérer son mari. Elle a jeûné et prié pendant de nombreuses années pour son mari. Aujourd’hui, son mari témoignera que c’est à cause de la conduite pieuse de sa femme qu’il a été amené au repentir et à la foi en Christ.

Un autre exemple avec un résultat différent… Je connais un couple qui n’avait pas un mariage solide. Le mari n’était pas à sa place et la femme devint amère, si amère en fait, qu’elle déclara que lorsqu’elle serait enterrée, elle ne voulait pas être enterrée à côté de son mari. Cette amertume a eu un effet terrible sur leurs enfants. Je me suis demandé si, si elle n’était pas devenue amère, elle aurait au moins pu épargner à ses enfants les nombreuses peines de cœur qu’ils ont subies.

Je connais aussi un autre couple qui avait été gravement maltraité par des membres proches de la famille, mais ils choisirent de ne pas devenir amers. Ils se sont rapprochés de Dieu et l’un de l’autre à travers ces vallées et ils récoltent jusqu’à ce jour les bénéfices du fruit de leurs choix.

Encore plus près de chez moi… J’ai grandi dans un foyer qui n’était pas chrétien. Aucun de mes parents n’était né de nouveau. Quand ils commencèrent à permettre à Dieu d’agir dans leurs cœurs, je pouvais le voir. Je revenais de rassemblements et je voyais mon père en pleurs en train de lire sa Bible. Aussi, un soir en particulier, je suis rentrée et j’ai vu mes parents assis à la table en train de chanter ensemble. Je témoignerai que cela a eu un effet énorme sur ma vie. Je voyais aussi ma propre mère désirer être à sa place comme Dieu l’avait conçue. Quand nous quitterons cette vie, que dira notre famille de nous ? Témoigneront-ils que l’amour de Dieu régnait dans nos corps mortels ?

De façon pratique, j’ai pensé écrire quelques manières par lesquelles nous pouvons montrer que nous aimons nos maris en actes et non seulement en paroles.

  • Leur demander conseil (ne pas uniquement agir selon ce que nous pensons)
  • Préparer leurs plats favoris
  • Garder la maison ordonnée et propre
  • Être prête et disposée à laisser tomber nos plans pour aider nos maris dans ce dont ils ont besoin
  • Les accueillir à la porte avec le sourire (peu importe la mauvaise journée que nous avons eue)
  • Garder la maison calme, même avec de petits enfants, quand il essaie de se reposer ou d’étudier
  • Apprendre à nos enfants les bonnes manières dans leurs relations au foyer
  • Apprendre à nos enfants à aimer et respecter leur père, même s’il n’est pas toujours parfait

Un autre défi que je souhaite lancer à chaque sœur mariée est de penser à quelque chose que vous pouvez dire à votre mari pour lui dire que vous êtes bénie à cause de lui. Essayez de le faire chaque jour pendant deux semaines. C’est incroyable l’effet que la bonté peut avoir sur un mariage. Cela paraîtra peut-être pour certaines comme une corvée, mais ce n’en est pas une. Je suis étonnée de voir qu’à mesure que nous vieillissons, combien nous pensons de la même façon, allant parfois jusqu’à finir les phrases de l’autre. Je réalise qu’il y aurait tellement plus à écrire. Je fais confiance à Dieu pour continuer d’ouvrir Sa Parole pour nous à mesure que nous Le cherchons.

Note de la rédaction :

J’ai été de celles qui ont eu de grandes difficultés pendant des années à ne pas savoir comment se soumettre tout en désirant le faire. Ce qui suit est ma tentative de partager ce que Dieu m’a enseigné.

Une des principales raisons pour lesquelles beaucoup de personnes ont du mal avec la « soumission » est qu’elles ne comprennent pas vraiment ce que Dieu entend par le sujet — elles ne comprennent pas la réalité de la soumission biblique. Généralement, une personne sait ce qu’elle croit sur un certain sujet, donc, dans son esprit, quand on lui demande de « se soumettre » sur ce point, elle pense qu’on lui demande de compromettre sa conviction personnelle — ou de pécher contre sa conscience.

La réponse est double.

Premièrement, si deux personnes sont d’accord sur une question, il n’y a pas besoin que l’une se soumette à l’autre. Ainsi, se soumettre ne signifie pas nécessairement que la personne qui se soumet change d’avis, mais plutôt qu’elle choisit de soutenir la décision de l’autre personne en se basant sur le fait que Dieu dit que cette personne est celle qu’Il tient responsable des décisions de ce groupe — que ce soit un couple, la maison, une école, une église, etc.

Deuxièmement, Dieu savait que chaque fois qu’il y aurait plus d’une personne discutant d’une décision à prendre, cela signifierait toujours que l’une finirait par se soumettre à l’autre. Donc, pour clarifier la responsabilité, Il donne des directives claires concernant qui Il considère comme la personne responsable (l’autorité spirituelle) dans chaque type de situation — le mari dans un mariage, le père dans la famille, l’homme (la tête) dans la maison, les dirigeants ordonnés dans l’église, les enseignants/directeur dans l’école, etc. Ainsi chacun peut savoir qui Dieu considère comme responsable pour les erreurs qui sont commises.

Considérez que même si Ève prit le fruit et le mangea la première, puis le donna à son mari pour qu’il le mange, Dieu nous donne une clarté sur qui Il tient pour responsable de cette défaillance (du péché). C’est pourquoi, de même que par un seul homme [pas par une femme] le péché est entré dans le monde, et la mort par le péché; et ainsi la mort s’est étendue à tous les hommes, parce que tous ont péché … Néanmoins la mort a régné depuis Adam [pas depuis Ève] jusqu’à Moïse, même sur ceux [les descendants d’Adam — toute la race humaine] qui n’avaient pas péché selon la ressemblance de la transgression d’Adam… – Romains 5:12-14.

Ainsi, nous voyons que Dieu fournit protection et sécurité à tous ceux qui sont sous l’autorité s’ils restent sous cette autorité. Celui que Dieu déclare clairement être la figure d’autorité dans chaque relation sera toujours celui que Dieu tiendra responsable des décisions prises par ce groupe de personnes. Tout comme dans la chute dans le jardin d’Éden, les péchés d’omission et de commission au sein de chaque famille seront tenus principalement pour compte du père. Que le père ait donné de mauvaises directions à la famille ou qu’il n’ait donné aucune direction, peu importe, il sera quand même tenu responsable puisque Dieu voit l’homme comme étant la tête de sa maison. (voir 1 Corinthiens 11:3 et Romains 13:12)

And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus –Matthew 14:28-29.

Men who follow Jesus are men of faith. Discipleship is not for cowards or the faint of heart, nor is it for those who demand a rationale for acts of obedience. The disciples had spent the day with Jesus. After the feeding of the five thousand Matthew writes that …straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away –Matthew 14:22.

If there was anything that the disciples were familiar with and skilled in, it was sailing the waters of Galilee. This was their territory. Peter and John had fished these waters with their father from their earliest remembrance. But tonight, they were making little headway… the wind was contrary.

And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid –Matthew 14:25-27.

Peter then made this bold appeal …Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water –Matthew 14:28. What was Peter thinking? He had never walked on water. Jesus was not asking him to walk on water. It was not logical. It defied the laws of nature… yet when Jesus said “come”. Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water to go to Jesus. That’s right! He was treading on water.

Peter was responding to a clear call from Jesus. Jesus said “come”. It is important that we understand that faith is our response to the clear call of God on our lives. Too often in our ambition to be useful we choose our path and call our ambition “faith” when God may not be in it at all.

If you want to be a man of faith, open your Bible and pray. Ask God to reveal His plan for your life. The Bible contains many commandments that can provide practical direction for our lives. Take God at His Word. Step out in faith and obedience then you will experience the miracle of God’s power in your life.

Peter’s boat was his security. He and his boat had a long relationship. It had served him well for many years. Peter felt right at home in his old bark, although tonight she did not seem to respond well to his masterful seamanship. He had drawn many a draught of fish over her gunwales. Now as he stands on her deck watching Jesus approach, “walking on the water”, he was overcome with a desire to go to Jesus. In reckless abandonment he stepped off her deck …and a miracle happened.

A walk of faith often calls us away from that which is familiar and secure. If we make safety and security our priority—if we limit our actions to carefully calculated risks (limited to that which we can manage and control)—we limit the power of God working in and through us.

Our forefathers in Europe knew that if they embraced the journey of unreserved discipleship, it could be costly. They risked the seizure of their property; many of them lost all that they owned. Since they willingly faced imprisonment and death, we refer to them as heroes of the faith. These were men who were willing to abandon all for the sake of the gospel. Because of their faith we receive the benefits of a godly heritage.

I commend our younger generation of Anabaptist youth for their willingness to make following Jesus a priority. In the past our priority has been to build our security base, be it our farm or business, and then consider mission work as a possibility. That was never Jesus’ model for service. When Jesus sent out his disciples he said. And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece –Luke 9:3.

Later, after they had returned, Jesus asked them, And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing –Luke 22:35.

You do not need to go into foreign missions to experience the power of God released in your life. Every act of radical obedience is an act of faith. There are men in our Anabaptist communities who are experiencing moral defeat. If we are going to succumb to a victim mentality (“I can’t help it”), and define moral failure as an addiction, we set ourselves up for ongoing defeat. Men of faith are men of action who take measurable steps of obedience which will lead them to ultimate victory. Moral failure begins with small compromises that end in crushing defeat.

Peter’s actions were not logical. If Peter would have processed his decision using the scientific method, he would not have taken such a risk. Many of the simple commands of Christ have no apparent scientific reasoning. From baptism, to communion, to foot washing, to anointing with oil, these are all acts of faith. The significance and the power of each lies in the doing of it with a heart of obedient faith, not in the thing itself.

So it is with many aspects of the Christian experience. We can analyze a thing endlessly, ultimately resulting in its demise. This happens in many churches. We reason away the woman’s head covering. We reason away the nonconformed lifestyle. We reason away the permanence of marriage. We reason away brotherhood accountability. What we have left has no resemblance to the simple teachings of Jesus. Discipleship calls us to faithful obedience. Jesus and the apostles taught it, so we do it. The blessing and the power lie in the doing of it.

That is what Peter discovered. He walked on water! He did not dip a toe to test the water first. I like to think he leaped from the boat and hit the water with both feet. That would be faith and Peter had faith.

But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:30-32.

Peter had faith to walk on water until he began to look around and began to process his situation using the scientific method. This is not to invalidate the scientific method. The scientific method proves the order of creation and the evidence of a creator.

In Hebrews 11 we read that …faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen –Hebrews 11:1.

It is our faith that is the substance and our faith that is the evidence of spiritual realities. Just as the scientific method proves the realities of the created world, so our faith proves spiritual realities.

Boisterous wind and crashing waves produced a fearful, sinking Peter. We sometimes criticize Peter for taking his eyes off of Jesus and sinking into the waves; however, Peter walked on water, I know of no one else who walked on water. When we transition from obedient faith to carnal rationalization, we lose power with God.

Are we suggesting that faith is irrational? No, not at all. As a matter of fact, the first act of faith is to believe that Jesus is the logos. John wrote, In the beginning was the Word [Logos], and the Word [Logos], was with God, and the Word [Logos], was God –John 1:1. It is from the Greek word Logos that we get our English word logic.

Just as there are laws in nature that make the scientific method durable and replicable, so there are spiritual laws that give order and cohesion to our inner man. Jesus is the embodiment of these truths. His teachings are the revelation of these truths and through his death and resurrection these truths have become accessible to all. Jesus promised, Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth… –John 16:13.

Men of faith are men who have eyes to see these spiritual realities. Their vision is not limited to the natural world. They understand that there are spiritual realities that have “cause and effect” in our lives that are every bit as powerful as the “cause and effect” that we see about us in the natural world every day.

These realities are only visible to men of faith. Paul wrote, But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned –1 Corinthians 2:14. Men of faith, are men whose lives are governed by spiritual realities that are incomprehensible to the natural man. If you will be a man of faith, expect to be misunderstood. You are embarking on a journey that will run counter to the world view of many.

As Peter began to sink into the waves he cried out, “Lord, save me”. His plaintive cry revealed an absolute trust in his Lord. Jesus reached out His hand and rescued him. Jesus next words continue to challenge us. He said to Peter, …O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? Matthew 14:31. Peter had just walked on water—a feat no man had accomplished before or since, yet Jesus called it “little faith” and asked, “why did you doubt?”.

Jesus said at another time, …If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20.

If Peter’s “little faith” empowered him to walk on water, and if faith as tiny as a grain of mustard seed can remove mountains what does that say of your and my faith?

Perhaps it is evidence that our faith is littler than Peter’s “little faith” and tinier than the tiny grain of mustard seed?! It is also evidence that God honors little faith. What he does not honor is no faith. According to your faith be it unto you. Little faith…walk on water! No faith…sink beneath the waves!

Since Jesus is the “Logos”, He is the master of the natural world and the spirit world. He proved himself to be the Master of the wind and the waves—and when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:32. And He proved Himself to be the Master of the spirit world—then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God –Matthew 14:33.

We, in our western world, have become so satiated with materialism that we can easily be led to believe that natural realities are the most powerful realities. This materialism assaults us, not just with the abundance of material things, but also with a bombardment of humanistic philosophy. Humanistic philosophy is thinking that is devoid of spiritual reality… that is devoid of faith.

If you, as a man, find yourself sinking in waves of despair… be it financial struggles… be it relational difficulties… moral failure or maybe you find yourself being your own worst critic…may I challenge you to lift your eyes to the one who is Logos. Jesus is the one who is master of your circumstances and the one who would be Lord of your soul. To allow Jesus to be Lord of your soul is to live in faith obedience to the radical teachings of Jesus.

To live in harmony with the natural world we honor the laws of nature. When we are replacing a roof, we respect the law of gravity. When driving a vehicle, we slow down for turns out of respect for the law of inertia. Defy the natural laws and someone gets hurt.

To live in harmony with the spiritual world, we honor the law of Christ. We love our neighbor. We forgive our brother. We keep our marriage vows. We bear …one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2.

Men of faith are men who are attune to these spiritual realities and order their lives accordingly.

Na Petro akamjibu akamwambia, Bwana, ikiwa ni wewe, niamuru nisiende kwako juu ya maji. Akamwambia, Njoo. Ndipo Petro alipopanda chini kutoka meli, akatembea juu ya maji ili aende kwa Yasu –Mathayo 14:28-29.

Wanaume wanaomfuata Yesu ni wanaume wa imani. Ufuasi sio kwa wanyonge wa moyo wala kwa wale wasiopenda hatari, wala sio kwa wale wanaotaka sababu za kimantiki kwa matendo ya utiifu. Wanafunzi walikuwa wamemaliza siku pamoja na Yesu. Baada ya kuwalisha watu elfu tano Mathayo anaandika kwamba …kwa papo hilo Yesu alilazimisha wanafunzi wake wapandike meli, nao wamwende yeye mbele upande mwingine, naye akawatuma watu wakaondoke –Mathayo 14:22.

Kama kulikuwa chochote ambacho wanafunzi walikuwa wamerubuni na walikuwa na ujuzi wa kufanya, hicho kilikuwa kuvuka maji ya Galilaya. Hii ilikuwa eneo lao. Petro na Yohana walikuwa wamenjiawuza na baba yao kwenye maji haya tangu walipojua. Lakini usiku huo, walikuwa wanapiga meli polepole… upepo ulikuwa ukikana.

Na katika saa ya nne ya usiku Yesu akawaendea wakitembea juu ya bahari. Wakati wanafunzi walipoona yeye akitembea juu ya bahari, wakatokeza kwa hofu, wakisema, Ni roho; nao wakalia kwa hofu. Lakini papo hapo Yesu akawaambia, Amini; ni mimi; msizitumike na hofu –Mathayo 14:25-27.

Petro kisha alitoa ombi hili thabiti …Bwana, ikiwa ni wewe, niamuru nisiende kwako juu ya maji –Mathayo 14:28. Petro alikuwa akifikiria nini? Hajawahi kutembea juu ya maji. Yesu hakumwomba aendelee kutembea juu ya maji. Haikuwa mantiki. Ilipinga sheria za asili… lakini Yesu aliposema “njoo”, Petro alishtuka kutoka meli na akatembea juu ya maji kuelekea kwa Yesu. Ndiyo! Alikuwa anatembea juu ya maji.

Petro alikuwa akijibu wito wazi kutoka kwa Yesu. Yesu alisema “njoo”. Ni muhimu tuelewe kuwa imani ni jibu letu kwa wito wazi wa Mungu juu ya maisha yetu. Mara nyingi kwa tamaa yetu ya kuwa wa manufaa tunachagua njia yetu na kuitaja tamaa yetu “imani” wakati Mungu huenda asihusike nayo kabisa.

Kama unataka kuwa mwanamume wa imani, fungua Biblia yako na ukamwie Mungu. Muombe Mungu akuonyeshe mpango wake kwa maisha yako. Biblia ina amri nyingi zinazoweza kutoa mwanga wa vitendo kwa maisha yetu. Mwaminiye Neno la Mungu. Toka kwa meli kwa imani na utiifu kisha utashuhudia muujiza wa nguvu za Mungu katika maisha yako.

Meli ya Petro ilikuwa usalama wake. Yeye na meli yake walikuwa na uhusiano wa muda mrefu. Ilimhudumia vizuri kwa miaka mingi. Petro alihisi kutulia kwenye boti lake la zamani, ingawa usiku huo haikuonekana kujibu vizuri ujuzi wake wa uanahabari. Alikuwa ameteka samaki wengi kupitia pembeni za boti yake. Sasa akiwa amesimama juu ya dari yake akiangalia Yesu akimkaribia, “akitembea juu ya maji”, alishikwa na tamaa ya kumwendea Yesu. Kwa uamuzi wa kujionyesha kabisa, alipita kwenye dari yake …na muujiza ukatokea.

Matembezi ya imani mara nyingi yanatuhimiza kuondoka kutoka kwa yale ambayo ni ya kawaida na salama. Ikiwa tunaweka usalama na hifadhi kuwa kipaumbele chetu—ikiwa tunapunguza matendo yetu kwa hatari zilizokadiriwa kikamilifu (zilizounganishwa na yale tutakayoweza kusimamia na kudhibiti)—tunapunguza nguvu za Mungu zinazofanya kazi ndani na kupitia kwetu.

Wazee wetu Ulaya walijua kwamba walipokumbatia safari ya ufuasi usio na masharti, ingeweza kuwa ghali. Walikumbwa na hatari ya kukamatwa mali zao; wengi walipoteza yote waliokuwa nayo. Kwa sababu walikubali kukabiliana na kifungo na kifo, tunawaita mashujaa wa imani. Hawa walikuwa wanaume waliokuwa tayari kuachana na kila kitu kwa ajili ya injili. Kwa ajili ya imani yao tunapokea faida za urithi wenye Mungu.

Nampongeza kizazi chetu kipya cha vijana wa Anabaptisti kwa utayari wao wa kufanya kumfuata Yesu kuwa kipaumbele. Hapo zamani kipaumbele chetu kilikuwa kujenga msingi wetu wa usalama, iwe shamba letu au biashara, kisha tutaangalia kazi ya utume kama uwezekano. Hiyo haikuwa mfano wa huduma wa Yesu. Yesu alipowatuma wanafunzi wake alisema. Nao akawaambia, Msichukue chochote kwa safari yenu, wala fimbo, wala mfuko, wala mkate, wala fedha; wala msivyo wawe na makoti mawili kila mmoja –Luka 9:3.

Baadaye, waliporudi, Yesu akawauliza, Nami akawaambia, Nilipowatuma bila pochi, wala mfuko, wala viatu, kukosekani kitu? Na wakasema, Hakukuwa na kinachotukosea chochote –Luka 22:35.

Huhitaji kwenda utumishi wa kigeni ili kushuhudia nguvu ya Mungu ikitolewa katika maisha yako. Kila tendo la utiifu wa mkali ni tendo la imani. Kuna wanaume katika jamii zetu za Anabaptisti wanaopitia kushindwa kimaadili. Ikiwa tutaanguka kwa mtazamo wa kuwa waathiriwa (“siwezi kusaidia”), na kutaja kushindwa kimaadili kama uraibu, tunajiweka katika mazingira ya kushindwa kwa mara kwa mara. Wanaume wa imani ni wanaume wa vitendo wanaochukua hatua zinazoonekana za utiifu ambazo zitawaongoza kwa ushindi wa mwisho. Kushindwa kimaadili huanza kwa maafikiano madogo yanayoishia kwa kuteketeza kabisa.

Kile Petro alifanya hakikuwa mantiki. Ikiwa Petro angepitisha uamuzi wake kwa kutumia njia ya kisayansi, hangefanya hatua hiyo hatari. Amri nyingi za rahisi za Kristo hazina mantiki ya kisayansi inayoonekana. Kuanzia ubatizo, kwa kumbu kumbu ya Mwili na Damu, kwa kunawa miguu, kwa kumwagia mafuta, yote haya ni matendo ya imani. Umuhimu na nguvu ya kila kitendo iko katika kutekeleza kwake kwa moyo wa utiifu wa imani, si katika kitu hicho yenyewe.

Ndivyo ilivyo na nyanja nyingi za uzoefu wa Kikristo. Tunaweza kuchambua jambo bila kukoma, na hatimaye likafa. Hii hutokea katika makanisa mengi. Tunauzia mantiki kichomoro cha kichwa cha mwanamke. Tunauzia mantiki mtindo wa maisha usiojifaa. Tunauzia mantiki kudumu kwa ndoa. Tunauzia mantiki uwajibikaji wa udugu. Kilichobaki hakina ulinganifu kabisa na mafundisho rahisi ya Yesu. Ufuasi unatuita kwa utiifu wa imani. Yesu na mitume walifundisha hivyo, kwa hivyo tunafanya hivyo. Baraka na nguvu ziko katika kutenda hivyo.

Hicho ndicho Petro alivyozikuta. Alitembea juu ya maji! Hakuingiza kidole chake kujaribu maji kwanza. Napenda kufikiria aliruka kutoka kwenye meli na kukabiliana na maji kwa miguu yote miwili. Hilo lingekuwa imani na Petro alikuwa na imani.

Lakini alipomuona upepo ukitabasamu, akatisha moyo; na akaanza kuzama, akalia, akisema, Bwana, niokoe. Mara Yesu akatembea mkono wake, akamkamata, naye akamwambia, Ee mwenye imani kidogo, kwa nini uliwaza vibaya? Na walipopanda kwenye meli, upepo ukatafutika –Mathayo 14:30-32.

Petro alikuwa na imani ya kutembea juu ya maji hadi alianza kuangalia pande zote na kuanza kuchambua hali yake kwa kutumia njia ya kisayansi. Hii sio kukanusha njia ya kisayansi. Njia ya kisayansi inathibitisha mpangilio wa uumbaji na ushahidi wa Muumba.

Katika Waheshimiwa 11 tunasoma kwamba …imani ni uhakika wa mambo yanayotarajiwa, ni ushahidi wa mambo yasiyoonekana –Waheshimiwa 11:1.

Ni imani yetu inayokuwa msingi na imani yetu ni ushahidi wa ukweli wa kiroho. Kama njia ya kisayansi inavyothibitisha ukweli wa dunia iliyoumbwa, ndivyo imani yetu inavyothibitisha ukweli wa kiroho.

Upepo mkali na mawimbi yanayovunja yalimletea Petro hofu na kuzama. Wakati mwingine tunamuhoji Petro kwa kuondoa macho yake kwa Yesu na kuzama kwenye mawimbi; hata hivyo, Petro alitembea juu ya maji, sijamjua mtu mwingine aliyewahi kutembea juu ya maji. Tunapobadilika kutoka imani ya utiifu kwenda kwenye uhalalishaji wa nyama, tunapoteza nguvu kwa Mungu.

Je, tunapendekeza kwamba imani ni isiyo na mantiki? Hapana, si hivyo kabisa. Kwa kweli, tendo la kwanza la imani ni kuamini kwamba Yesu ndiye Logos. Yohane aliandika, Mwanzoni palikuwa Neno [Logos], naye Neno [Logos] alikuwa kwa Mungu, naye Neno [Logos] alikuwa Mungu –Yohana 1:1. Ni kutoka kwa neno la Kigiriki Logos tunapopata neno la Kiingereza logic (mantiki).

Kama ilivyo kwa sheria za asili zinazofanya njia ya kisayansi kuwa thabiti na kurudiwa, ndivyo pia kuna sheria za kiroho zinazotoa mpangilio na mshikamano kwa mtu wetu wa ndani. Yesu ni mwili wa ukweli hizi. Mafundisho yake ni ufunuo wa ukweli hizi na kupitia kifo chake na ufufuo ukweli hizi zimekuwa zinapatikana kwa wote. Yesu aliahidi, Lakini atakapokuja Yeye, Roho wa ukweli, atawaongoza kwa uzima wote… –Yohana 16:13.

Wanaume wa imani ni wanaume wenye macho ya kuona ukweli hivi wa kiroho. Maono yao hayana mipaka na dunia ya maumbile. Wanafahamu kuwa kuna ukweli wa kiroho ambao una “sabababu na athari” katika maisha yetu ambao ni wenye nguvu kama “sabababu na athari” tunazoona katika dunia ya maumbile kila siku.

Ukweli hizi zinaonekana tu kwa wanaume wa imani. Paulo aliandika, Bali asili ya mwanadamu haipokei mambo ya Roho wa Mungu; kwa kuwa ni ujeuri kwake; wala haviwezi kuyafahamu, kwa kuwa yanatambuliwa kiroho –1 Wakorintho 2:14. Wanaume wa imani, ni wanaume maisha yao yanaamriwa na ukweli za kiroho ambazo hazieleweki kwa mwanadamu wa asili. Ukitaka kuwa mwanamume wa imani, tarajia kutoeleweka. Unaenda kwenye safari ambayo itakuwa kinyume na mtazamo wa wengi wa dunia.

Petro alipokuwa anaanza kuzama ndani ya mawimbi alilia, “Bwana, niokoe”. Kilio chake cha taabu kilionyesha imani kamili kwake kwa Bwana wake. Yesu alitenda mkono wake na kumwokoa. Maneno yafuatayo ya Yesu yanaendelea kutuchangamsha. Alimwambia Petro, …Ee wako mwenye imani kidogo, kwa nini uliwaza vibaya? –Mathayo 14:31. Petro alikuwa ametembea juu ya maji—kazi ambayo hakuna mtu aliyewahi kufanya kabla wala baada yake, lakini Yesu aliita hiyo “imani ndogo” na kumuuliza, “kwa nini uliwaza vibaya?”.

Yesu alisema wakati mwingine, …Siyo kwamba mkiwa na imani kama chembe ya haradali mtamwambia mlima huu, Hameni hapa muende pale, nao utafukuzwa; wala wala jambo hata moja litawezekana kwenu –Mathayo 17:20.

Ikiwa “imani ndogo” ya Petro ilimuwezesha kutembea juu ya maji, na ikiwa imani ndogo kama chembe ya haradali inaweza kuondoa milima, hilo linamwambia nini kuhusu imani yako na yangu?

Labda ni ushahidi kwamba imani yetu ni ndogo zaidi kuliko “imani ndogo” ya Petro na nyonge zaidi kuliko chembe ndogo ya haradali?! Pia ni ushahidi kwamba Mungu anaheshimu imani ndogo. Kile asichoheshimu ni kutokuwa na imani kabisa. Kulingana na imani yako ikawa kwako. Imani ndogo…tembea juu ya maji! Hakuna imani…zama chini ya mawimbi!

Kama Yesu ni “Logos”, Yeye ndiye mwenye nguvu wa dunia ya maumbile na ya roho. Alijidhihirisha kuwa Mkuu wa upepo na mawimbi—na waliposhuka katika meli, upepo ukatafutika –Mathayo 14:32. Na alijidhihirisha pia kuwa Mkuu wa ulimwengu wa roho—wakao wana walipokuwa ndani ya meli wakaenda wakamwabudu, wakisema, Kwa hakika wewe ndiwe Mwana wa Mungu –Mathayo 14:33.

Sisi, katika dunia yetu ya magharibi, tumekuwa tumejaa vitu vya mali kiasi kwamba tunaweza kwa urahisi kuamini kwamba ukweli wa kimwili ndio unaoheshimiwa zaidi. Hali hii ya kinukuu inatuipiga, si tu kwa wingi wa vitu vya mali, bali pia kwa mlipuko wa falsafa za kibinadamu. Falsafa ya kibinadamu ni fikra ambazo zinakosa ukweli wa kiroho… ambazo zinakosa imani.

Kama wewe, kama mwanamume, unajiona ukizama katika mawimbi ya kukata tamaa… iwe matatizo ya kifedha… iwe matatizo ya mahusiano… kushindwa kimaadili au labda unakuta wewe ni mkosoaji wako mwenyewe… naomba nikutia moyo upe macho yako kwa Yule ambaye ni Logos. Yesu ndiye mkuu wa hali zako na ndiye ambaye atakuwa Bwana wa nafsi yako. Kumruhusu Yesu kuwa Bwana wa nafsi yako ni kuishi kwa imani na utiifu kwa mafundisho makali ya Yesu.

Ili kuishi kwa maelewano na dunia ya maumbile tunaheshimu sheria za asili. Tunapobadilisha paa, tunaheshimu sheria ya mvuto. Tunapokuwa tukiendeshaji gari, tunapunguza mwendo kwa ajili ya mizunguko kwa kuheshimu sheria ya inertia. Kukataa sheria za asili kunasababisha mtu kujeruhiwa.

Ili kuishi kwa maelewano na dunia ya kiroho, tunaheshimu sheria ya Kristo. Tunamwipenda jirani yetu. Tunamsamehe ndugu yetu. Tunahifadhi ahadi za ndoa zetu. Tunabeba …mzigo wa mwenzetu, na kwa hivyo kutimiza sheria ya Kristo –Wagalatia 6:2.

Wanaume wa imani ni wanaume walio fahamu ukweli hizi za kiroho na kuandaa maisha yao kwa mujibu wake.
