Kemanusiaan didefinisikan oleh pencariannya akan kebenaran. Beberapa orang mencari kebenaran ini melalui kekuasaan pribadi, saat mereka berusaha menguasai sesama manusia. Beberapa mencari kebenaran dalam kesenangan, melihat pemuasan diri sebagai pencapaian terbesar dalam hidup. Lainnya mencari pencerahan melalui pemikiran dan penalaran mereka sendiri, senantiasa belajar, namun tidak pernah dapat mencapai pengenalan akan kebenaran – 2 Timotius 3:7. Lain lagi percaya bahwa kehidupan melayani akan menjadi ganjaran itu sendiri, sehingga mereka berusaha mencari nama melalui publisitas tindakan pelayanan dan kasih mereka.

Berulang kali, sepanjang sejarah, pemikiran kolektif manusia beralih kepada sesuatu yang lebih besar dari diri mereka sendiri. Agama bangkit, dan agama runtuh, kekaisaran didirikan dan hancur, filsafat berkembang dan kemudian roboh.

Melawan latar gelombang intelektual ini, sebuah gerakan yang kebanyakan pembaca saya akan kenali, berakar di sebuah wilayah pegunungan kecil di bumi. Zurich, Swiss, pada tahun 1525 M, menjadi tempat dan tanggal kelahirannya, tetapi akarnya telah ditanam penuh 1500 tahun sebelumnya, di Galilea, tempat Seorang mengajar dan hidup jawaban terakhir atas semua pertanyaan manusia.

Awal mula gerakan yang lebih baru ini terdokumentasi dengan baik. Singkatnya, ia didirikan oleh sekelompok kecil pelajar, rohaniwan, dan rakyat biasa yang mencari kebenaran dalam bentuknya yang paling murni. Kisah Conrad Grebel, Felix Manz, dan George Blaurock dikenal baik oleh banyak dari kita. Mereka berusaha berpisah dari korupsi rohani yang mengelilingi mereka, ketika mereka mendirikan awal dari apa yang kemudian dikenal sebagai gerakan Anabaptis.

Ketiga orang ini segera menghadapi pengawasan pihak berwenang sipil dan rohani pada masa mereka, menanggung kesengsaraan dan penderitaan karena iman mereka. Dua dari mereka pada akhirnya memberikan nyawa mereka demi kebenaran yang sangat mereka muliakan. Felix Manz adalah Anabaptis pertama yang dimartir. Pada 5 Januari 1527, tidak sampai dua tahun setelah pembaptisan ulangnya yang penuh keberanian, ia ditenggelamkan di Sungai Limmat yang mengalir melalui Zurich. Kata-kata terakhirnya adalah: “Ke dalam tangan-Mu, ya Allah, kujadikan nyawaku.”

Gerakan Anabaptis hidup lebih lama dari ketiga pria ini.

Ia menyebar dan tumbuh di seluruh Moravia, Belanda, Swiss, dan wilayah Pfalz di Jerman. Hampir seratus tahun kemudian ada seorang pemimpin menonjol lain di perbukitan Zurich; yang ini adalah seorang petani lanjut usia. Ia berpengalaman memimpin jemaatnya melalui pasang surut tantangan yang dihadapi orang percaya pada masa itu. Namanya Hans Landis.

Tahun itu 1613, tepatnya 26 Januari. Berkumpul di kastil kecil Wadenswil, di tepi Danau Zurich, adalah Hans Landis yang lanjut usia, bersama empat belas anggota gerejanya. Yang paling menonjol di antaranya adalah Galli Fuchs, seorang guru sekolah dan baru saja menjadi percaya, serta Bachman, seorang pandai besi dan pengacau yang dikenal, yang juga baru bertobat. Bertemu dengan mereka ada sembilan pejabat gereja dan negara, termasuk walikota Zurich, Rudolf Rhan; kepala kepolisian kota, Conrad Grebel (nyata-nyata bernama sama dengan pendiri pembaptisan ulang hampir seabad sebelumnya); dan sejumlah pendeta setempat dari gereja Protestan Zurich. Alasan pertemuan ini adalah bahwa pekerjaan rohani Hans telah diberkati, dan jemaat kecilnya tumbuh pesat, menyebabkan penurunan kehadiran di paroki-paroki pedesaan milik gereja Protestan. Turunnya kehadiran ini menimbulkan beberapa kesulitan bagi pemerintahan gabungan gereja dan negara ini.

Pertama, Gereja Protestan menarik dana besar dari para jemaatnya. Dengan demikian, gereja lain yang menarik dan mengonversi anggotanya dipandang bukan hanya sebagai ancaman rohani, tetapi juga finansial. Kanton-kanton di daerah itu sering terlibat dalam permusuhan yang dipicu agama, mulai dari debat marah hingga kampanye militer penuh. Kedua, doktrin rohani yang menyimpang yang tidak setuju dengan agama resmi pemerintah sering muncul di masa kerusuhan sipil, dan pemberontakan petani di kanton-kanton terdekat masih segar dalam ingatan bangsawan dan kaum rohani setempat. Peristiwa seperti Muensterites dan interpretasi kekerasan mereka terhadap Kitab Suci tetap menjadi peringatan jelas akan semangat agama yang salah arah. Pemberontakan ini terjadi saat gereja Katolik runtuh di wilayah itu, yang memberi kesempatan bagi kepercayaan baru dan kadang ekstrem untuk berakar. Kini, aktivitas Hans dan gerejanya tampak bagi para pejabat ini sebagai masalah yang berbatasan dengan pemberontakan dan pengkhianatan.

Pertemuan ini bukanlah perjumpaan pertama antara Hans Landis dan jemaatnya dengan otoritas setempat. Sebuah penyelidikan sebelumnya telah dilakukan, hampir empat tahun sebelumnya. Laporan itu menyebut tempat pertemuan mereka sebagai hutan, lumbung, dan bahkan rumah Hans Landis. Namun, tidak ada daftar anggota yang disertakan, karena bahkan tetangga Protestan dari gereja itu menolak menyebutkan nama-nama para Anabaptis. Bukan hanya penduduk setempat menolak bekerja sama memberi nama siapa pun dari jemaat Hans, tetapi juga beredar kabar bahwa Taufer memegang dana umum, yang dipercayakan kepada Diaken Jacob Isler, dari mana mereka memenuhi kebutuhan dalam komunitas mereka. Bagi para pejabat, ini tampak sebagai tipu muslihat lain untuk membujuk orang miskin komunitas meninggalkan gereja mereka dan bergabung dengan Hans dan kelompoknya.

Walikota Rhan membuka pertemuan, menyapa rombongannya sebagai “Reverend, tinggi dan berilmu, saleh, bangsawan, cerdas, bijak, (dan) tuan-tuan yang terkasih.” Selanjutnya, ia berbicara kepada Hans dan saudara-saudaranya, memberi salam ramah “Terhormat, terkasih dan sahabat baik” sebelum mengingatkan posisi mereka dengan menyebut mereka “bawahan”. Setelah manuver yang tak begitu halus ini, ia mempertanyakan mereka, meminta penjelasan tentang “alasan [mengapa] kamu berpisah dari gereja kami dan … memulai sekte terpisah.” Setelah pertanyaan ini, ia meyakinkan mereka bahwa dewan ingin bersikap toleran tetapi bahwa para pemisah “tidak menyalahgunakan kesabaran dan kemurahan tuan-tuan.”

Menanggapi pengantar ini, Hans meminta izin bagi dia dan saudara-saudaranya untuk berdiri dan berbicara kepada “Tuan-tuan Yang Mulia”. Diizinkan, ia berdiri, mengucap terima kasih kepada walikota atas kata-kata sambutan yang ramah sebelum mempertanyakan minat mereka terhadap keyakinan Anabaptis, karena menurutnya mereka sering mendengarnya sebelumnya. Ia menambahkan bahwa semua doktrin mereka “tidak lain dari apa yang diajarkan Kristus dan apa yang ditulis para rasul.” Seperti sebelumnya, orang-orang Anabaptis hanya meminta diizinkan mempertahankan hal ini, mendukung pemerintah dalam hal-hal yang tidak berkaitan dengan hati nurani. Mereka juga akan terus berdoa untuk pemerintah dan para pemimpin mereka.

Walikota Rhan tidak senang dengan jawaban ini, menanggapinya seolah tersirat bahwa dia dan gereja Protestan tidak menaati perintah Kristus. Hans, setelah mendengar bantahan ini, meminta izin membawa kelompoknya keluar ruangan sebentar. Setelah kembali, Galli Fuchs dihadapkan dan memberi kesaksian kepada para tuan, menguraikan perjalanan rohaninya melalui gereja Protestan dan Katolik, mengamati bahwa sementara kedua-duanya berkhotbah dengan baik di mimbar, keduanya juga menyangkal pengajaran ini dengan hidupnya yang tidak saleh. Setelah mempelajari iman dan praktik Anabaptis, Galli bertobat.

Para pejabat bersikap skeptis, berargumen bahwa poin-poin Galli “masih belum menunjukkan alasan untuk perpisahanmu.” Menanggapi bantahan ini, seorang yang baru menjadi percaya lain dimajukan, yakni pandai besi Bachman. Bachman segera dikenali oleh Conrad Grebel (bukan pendiri Anabaptis), kepala polisi Zurich, sebagai salah satu pemuda nakal setempat—“Memang benar, engkau dahulu tidak saleh [dan] tidak ada seorang pun di seluruh daerah ini yang membuatku lebih susah darimu.”

Kesaksian Bachman menggema banyak poin Galli, terutama tentang kemurnian dan keterpisahan gereja sejati, berakhir dengan kutipan dari Sirakh: “Barangsiapa mengaduk dalam ter?”

Perdebatan berlanjut, dengan perselisihan memanas seputar komuni, teladan pemimpin gereja, dan pengetahuan tentang keselamatan. Saat pertemuan berakhir, Galli Fuchs tak menahan diri memberi komentar terakhir: “Jika kalian memberi kami gereja di Hirzel, … kalian akan melihat … siapa yang akan punya kerumunan lebih besar!” Ini memicu tawa di ruangan, dan Hans memanfaatkan kesempatan terakhir untuk berbicara, memohon: “Oh, tuan-tuan terhormat, biarkan kami tetap pada apa yang kami percayai.”

Setelah permohonan ini, walikota bermusyawarah, akhirnya memutuskan bahwa saudara-saudara itu diizinkan pergi tanpa ditangkap, yang, saat keluar, terdengar berkata setuju: “Kami juga akan memberikan nyawa, badan, harta, dan darah.” Mereka segera mendapat kesempatan untuk mewujudkan komitmen ini.

Lima belas bulan berlalu. Hans dikurung di menara Wellenberg di Zurich, bersama Galli Fuchs, Diaken Jacob Isler, Hans Meili, Stephen Zehnder, dan Paul Degia (asal Milan, Italia). Di sana mereka ditahan selama empat belas minggu, dan berulang kali dibujuk, diinterogasi, dan diancam. Akhirnya dikeluarkan perintah agar mereka meninggalkan kanton Zurich, tetapi Hans menolak, sehingga dewan menanggapi dengan ancaman yang sering dianggap lebih buruk daripada kematian. Dewan berpendapat bahwa karena ketidakpatuhan sipil para pria ini, bukan keyakinan mereka, mereka akan dijatuhi hukuman menjadi budak galley untuk mendayung kapal-kapal Prancis di Laut Tengah.

Jacob Isler memohon kepada para tuan, menanyakan bagaimana mereka dapat melakukan hal semacam itu, dengan mengetahui bahwa Taufer (Anabaptis) tidak sanggup meninggalkan keluarga mereka. Stephen Zhender menambahkan: “Kami tidak akan takut pergi menyeberang laut dan air karena mereka juga makhluk Allah.” Meski ada permohonan ini, dewan melaksanakan ancaman mereka, menjatuhkan hukuman galley kepada keenamnya.

Hukuman itu mengirimkan gelombang kejut ke seluruh komunitas. Harapan hidup bagi budak galley muda dan sehat tidak lebih dari tiga tahun, dan tiga tahun itu akan dipenuhi kelaparan, paparan, pemukulan, dan kelelahan. Bahkan di kanton Katolik yang lebih keras, hukuman ini berat. Dalam komunitas Protestan yang lebih lunak, hal itu memicu kemarahan publik.

Para tahanan diberi satu kesempatan terakhir untuk meninggalkan kanton, di mana tiga dari mereka akhirnya menyerah. Tetapi Galli Fuchs, Stephen Zehnder, dan Hans Landis teguh menolak mengubah pikiran mereka. Mereka kemudian diarak dengan pengawalan ke barat menuju seorang duta besar Prancis di Solothurn, sebuah kota di kanton Bern. Bern bereaksi serupa seperti Zurich, dengan menawarkan tebusan untuk pembebasan para tahanan. Ketika itu gagal, sebuah berkas diam-diam diselipkan ke dalam sel mereka di Solothurn. Rantai para tahanan dengan cepat dipotong, dan mereka melarikan diri dari kota, kembali ke rumah mereka. Sesampainya di sana, penduduk, yang masih marah atas perlakuan mereka, menolak melaporkan mereka kepada otoritas.

Berita pelarian itu menyebar dan membesar, dan Hans segera bekerja, membaptis orang-orang yang baru percaya, bahkan menyelenggarakan beberapa pernikahan. Anabaptis makmur, membantu orang miskin komunitas melalui makanan dan pinjaman tanpa bunga dari dana amal mereka. Aktivitas yang diperbarui ini membuat marah dan menakutkan para pejabat, yang akhirnya memutuskan bahwa usaha pemimpin lanjut usia itu perlu dinetralisir.

Hans segera ditangkap setelah keputusan ini dan sekali lagi dikurung di Wellenberg. Di sini ancaman dan teguran dari para pejabat ditingkatkan. Jika ia tidak mau mundur atau setidaknya meninggalkan kanton, mereka harus membunuhnya.

Ancaman seperti itu tidak menggoyahkan Hans. Ia malah menegur para penguasa agar tidak berbuat dosa dalam perlakuan mereka terhadapnya, menegaskan tekadnya bahwa ia “menyerahkan dirinya kepada Allah” dan “siap menantikan apa yang Allah izinkan menimpanya.”

Keteguhan berani Hans ini membawa kesadaran serupa bagi para pejabat: mereka harus menepati ancaman mereka. Menganggap Hans sebagai pemberontak, mereka berpendapat bahwa ia “ingin menjadi tuan dan penguasanya sendiri tanpa memandang otoritas yang mulia,” dan bahwa ia menunjukkan “kekeras kepala, perlawanan subversif orang-orang jahat.” Meski tuduhan ini disertai ancaman, para hakim menyadari bahwa sebuah eksekusi akan menjadi tindakan yang tidak populer. Hans sangat dihormati oleh penduduk setempat, dan bahkan memiliki hubungan di Amsterdam, tempat putrinya tinggal, yang menikah dengan seorang Mennonite Belanda.

Perwira Grebel, kaum rohani Protestan, dan berbagai pihak lain banyak berdiskusi dengan Hans di sel penjaranya, namun sia-sia. Pada Kamis, 29 September 1614, mereka menyadari bahwa ia benar-benar tak tergoyahkan dalam imannya, enggan baik bertaubat maupun meninggalkan kanton. Laporan ini, disampaikan kepada para tuan, membuat mereka bermusyawarah dalam-dalam. Beberapa berargumen untuk memotong telinga Hans di depan umum dan mengasingkannya, sementara yang lain menilai penjara seumur hidup lebih pantas. Masalah itu kemudian disahkan melalui pemungutan suara pada tengah hari, dan keputusan mayoritas pun cepat dicapai. Hans Landis akan segera dipenggal di muka umum.

Saat mendengar keputusan itu, Hans menganggapnya hanya tipu daya lain untuk membujuknya bertaubat. Namun, saat mendekati tempat eksekusi umum yang terkenal di Zurich, wajahnya pucat, dan tangannya melambung ke kepala. Tetapi ia segera menenangkan diri, tersenyum dan menasihati orang banyak agar tidak menangis, karena ia percaya pada pengharapan baiknya. Menyadari istri dan anak-anaknya hadir, ia meminta mereka meninggalkan tempat agar tekadnya tidak melemah.

Hukuman dibacakan; Hans berdiri diam. Tidak ada kata kecaman yang dilayangkan terhadap moral pribadinya. Sebaliknya, persoalannya adalah penolakannya membubarkan gerejanya. Ia tetap teguh, dan sang algojo, Paul Vollmar, membawa Hans ke tempat eksekusi. Beberapa pengamat mengklaim bahwa Vollmar melepaskan Hans, seolah memberi jalan agar ia melarikan diri. Ketika Hans tidak melakukannya, Vollmar mengangkat tangannya kepada Allah, memohon pengampunan untuk apa yang hukum perintahkan kepadanya untuk lakukan. Hans, tersenyum, memaafkan pria itu, sementara berbagai pendeta menasihatinya untuk bertaubat, tetapi Hans menjawab bahwa ia tidak melihat pertobatan pada mereka.

Vollmar, setelah mencapai tempat eksekusi, memberi Hans kesempatan untuk berbicara tanpa halangan, dan Hans berbicara singkat: “Aku tidak tahu apa lagi yang harus kukatakan selain bahwa aku ingin semua orang datang kepada pengenalan akan dosa-dosa mereka dan bertobat, supaya mereka diselamatkan; ini yang kuharapkan bagi semua orang.”

Lalu, di tempat yang dapat dilihat dari tempat dimana Felix Manz telah memberikan hidupnya hampir seabad sebelumnya, ia berlutut dan menundukkan kepalanya. Pedang menyambar turun, lalu Paul Vollmar mengajukan pertanyaan ritual: “Apakah aku telah mengeksekusi orang ini dengan benar?”

“Ya,” datang jawaban, “engkau telah mengeksekusi orang miskin ini.”

Dampak langsung dari pengorbanan orang lanjut usia Hans itu adalah gelombang dukungan dan kemarahan di seluruh komunitas non-Anabaptis. Rhudlof Rhan dan Conrad Grebel terus menekan Anabaptis yang tersisa, menahan Margaretha Landis, janda Hans, dalam isolasi di rumah sakit kota setelah penolakannya mematuhi tuntutan mereka. Anak-anak Hans juga tetap teguh, menolak bertaubat, namun beberapa cucunya mulai menghadiri gereja kota tak lama setelah eksekusi kakek mereka.

Gereja Anabaptis setempat juga tetap kuat. Keturunan rohaninya akan membawa firman Kristus ketika, satu abad kemudian, sebuah emigrasi besar menambatkan mereka di pantai liar Dunia Baru. Di sini, dalam kebebasan beragama Pennsylvania, mereka mendirikan komunitas baru di mana iman yang telah menelan nyawa Hans Landis akan berkembang melalui generasi-generasi mendatang. Hari ini, ada orang percaya di seluruh Amerika yang berusaha hidup sesuai iman menurut hati nurani mereka, yang berada di tempat mereka sekarang sebagai hasil dari hidup yang dijalani Hans sekitar 400 tahun yang lalu. Beberapa adalah keturunannya, dan beberapa adalah teman keturunannya. Kiranya kita terinspirasi untuk berjalan seperti Yesus berjalan, sama seperti Hans.

As a child, you might think you can’t make a difference in the lives of people around you, but that is not true! Your little acts of kindness will not soon be forgotten. Being a true friend to someone who is hurting can change that person’s life forever.

This is the true story of “Hadassah” (not her real name) a young girl who was very much looking forward to starting school. Once she started first grade, what a disappointment it was to find that the second-grade girls were ready for someone to be mean to, or so it seemed. Maybe it would have been better if Hadassah had stood up to them, but she didn’t. Instead, she chose to act as if it didn’t hurt and tried to ignore them. Some days were better than others, but sadly this went on for three or four years.

Sure, there were good times too, but many evenings she walked home from school, crying most of the way and wishing that she wouldn’t need to go back to school the next day!

One day, one of the girls lost her pen. She was sure that Hadassah had stolen it. This was very disturbing to a very conscientious Hadassah. At the next recess she was blamed for cheating on her flash cards. Many other made-up stories were also passed around among the girls.

However, there was one little girl in that second-grade group of girls whose name we’ll say was “Esther”. She was Hadassah’s best friend and supported her all through those difficult years.

Esther was a very gentle, sweet girl, which is mostly what Hadassah remembered her for. Esther had cystic fibrosis and in the 1970s they didn’t have as many treatment options available for that disease as they do now, so those patients usually died very young. As Esther’s sickness became worse, the days that she felt well enough to be in school were rare. Since Esther was well-liked, the days when she was in school were special to everyone. Perhaps Esther realized she would be in heaven before the other girls—we don’t know for sure. But she taught the girls a song, “How Far Is Heaven”, which Hadassah still likes to sing today!

Hadassah still remembers seeing the emergency squad go past her house when they took Esther to the hospital for the last time. It was a very sad group of schoolgirls when Esther died at the age of 13. Esther had touched the hearts of many people in her short life, including the nurses who had cared for her during her stay in the hospital. Hadassah still remembers seeing some of the nurses crying at Esther’s funeral. Do you think Hadassah will ever forget Esther? Never!

Besides being her best friend, another bright spot for Hadassah was that when Esther was in school the other girls weren’t as mean to her (Hadassah). It so happened that in about the fourth grade, Esther was in school more often. One day she went home and told her parents what she was witnessing in school—how the other girls were against Hadassah and were being so mean to her. Esther’s father brought this problem up in the next parent/teacher meeting. What a night and day change started the very next day! One of the girls even came to Hadassah and apologized. Finally, they could all be friends and today those girls are Hadassah’s “old school friends”.

It’s worth it to stand beside someone who is being treated unkindly. Your support may be what God uses to help your friend to go through their hard times in a good way! And share it with your parents, they can help find a way to change the problem.

作为孩子，你可能会认为自己无法在周围人的生命中产生影响，但那并不是真的！你那些微小的善举不会很快被遗忘。成为一个真正的朋友，对正在受伤的人伸出援手，可能永远改变那个人的生命。

这是一个真实的故事，关于“哈大沙”（这不是她的真名）——一个非常期待开始上学的小女孩。她一上第一年级，就很失望地发现二年级的女孩们似乎已经准备好找人欺负了。也许哈大沙本可以站出来反抗，但她没有。相反，她选择装作这并不伤她并试图忽视那些人。有些日子好些，但遗憾的是，这种情况持续了三四年。

当然，也有快乐的时光，但许多傍晚她放学回家时一路哭着走，盼望第二天不用再去上学！

有一天，其中一个女孩丢了笔。她确信是哈大沙偷的。对于一向很有良心的哈大沙来说，这件事令她非常不安。下一次课间休息时，她被指责在记忆卡片上作弊。许多其他编造的故事也在女孩们之间传播开来。

然而，在那群二年级的女孩中，有一个小女孩——我们姑且称她为“以斯帖”。她是哈大沙最好的朋友，在那些艰难的岁月里一直支持着她。

以斯帖是一个非常温柔、可爱的女孩，这大概是哈大沙对她印象最深的地方。以斯帖患有囊性纤维化，在上世纪七十年代，治疗这种疾病的可选方法没有现在那么多，这些病人通常寿命很短。随着以斯帖病情恶化，她能上学的日子越来越少。因为以斯帖很受欢迎，她在校的日子对每个人来说都很特别。也许以斯帖意识到自己会比其他女孩更早到达天堂——我们无法确定。但她教给女孩们一首歌，“How Far Is Heaven”，哈大沙至今仍喜欢唱这首歌！

哈大沙仍记得看到急救队开过她家，把以斯帖最后一次送往医院的情景。以斯帖在13岁时去世，那时是一群非常悲伤的女学生。以斯帖在短暂的一生中触动了许多人的心，包括在她住院期间照顾她的护士们。哈大沙仍记得在以斯帖的葬礼上看到一些护士在哭。你觉得哈大沙会忘记以斯帖吗？绝不会！

除了是她最好的朋友之外，对哈大沙来说另一个光亮点是：当以斯帖在学校时，其他女孩就没有那么刻薄（对哈大沙）。碰巧大约到了四年级，以斯帖上学的时间更多了。一天，她回家告诉父母她在学校目睹的事情——其他女孩如何联合对付哈大沙，多么刻薄。以斯帖的父亲在下一次家长会中提出了这个问题。第二天开始，情况发生了天翻地覆的变化！其中一个女孩甚至走到哈大沙面前道歉。终于，她们可以都成为朋友了，而今天那些女孩就是哈大沙的“老同学”。

站在被不友善对待的人身边是值得的。你的支持可能成为神用来帮助你的朋友以良好方式度过困难时期的工具！并且与父母分享这件事，他们可以帮助找到改变问题的方法。

And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus –Matthew 14:28-29.

Men who follow Jesus are men of faith. Discipleship is not for cowards or the faint of heart, nor is it for those who demand a rationale for acts of obedience. The disciples had spent the day with Jesus. After the feeding of the five thousand Matthew writes that …straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away –Matthew 14:22.

If there was anything that the disciples were familiar with and skilled in, it was sailing the waters of Galilee. This was their territory. Peter and John had fished these waters with their father from their earliest remembrance. But tonight, they were making little headway… the wind was contrary.

And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid –Matthew 14:25-27.

Peter then made this bold appeal …Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water –Matthew 14:28. What was Peter thinking? He had never walked on water. Jesus was not asking him to walk on water. It was not logical. It defied the laws of nature… yet when Jesus said “come”. Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water to go to Jesus. That’s right! He was treading on water.

Peter was responding to a clear call from Jesus. Jesus said “come”. It is important that we understand that faith is our response to the clear call of God on our lives. Too often in our ambition to be useful we choose our path and call our ambition “faith” when God may not be in it at all.

If you want to be a man of faith, open your Bible and pray. Ask God to reveal His plan for your life. The Bible contains many commandments that can provide practical direction for our lives. Take God at His Word. Step out in faith and obedience then you will experience the miracle of God’s power in your life.

Peter’s boat was his security. He and his boat had a long relationship. It had served him well for many years. Peter felt right at home in his old bark, although tonight she did not seem to respond well to his masterful seamanship. He had drawn many a draught of fish over her gunwales. Now as he stands on her deck watching Jesus approach, “walking on the water”, he was overcome with a desire to go to Jesus. In reckless abandonment he stepped off her deck …and a miracle happened.

A walk of faith often calls us away from that which is familiar and secure. If we make safety and security our priority—if we limit our actions to carefully calculated risks (limited to that which we can manage and control)—we limit the power of God working in and through us.

Our forefathers in Europe knew that if they embraced the journey of unreserved discipleship, it could be costly. They risked the seizure of their property; many of them lost all that they owned. Since they willingly faced imprisonment and death, we refer to them as heroes of the faith. These were men who were willing to abandon all for the sake of the gospel. Because of their faith we receive the benefits of a godly heritage.

I commend our younger generation of Anabaptist youth for their willingness to make following Jesus a priority. In the past our priority has been to build our security base, be it our farm or business, and then consider mission work as a possibility. That was never Jesus’ model for service. When Jesus sent out his disciples he said. And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece –Luke 9:3.

Later, after they had returned, Jesus asked them, And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing –Luke 22:35.

You do not need to go into foreign missions to experience the power of God released in your life. Every act of radical obedience is an act of faith. There are men in our Anabaptist communities who are experiencing moral defeat. If we are going to succumb to a victim mentality (“I can’t help it”), and define moral failure as an addiction, we set ourselves up for ongoing defeat. Men of faith are men of action who take measurable steps of obedience which will lead them to ultimate victory. Moral failure begins with small compromises that end in crushing defeat.

Peter’s actions were not logical. If Peter would have processed his decision using the scientific method, he would not have taken such a risk. Many of the simple commands of Christ have no apparent scientific reasoning. From baptism, to communion, to foot washing, to anointing with oil, these are all acts of faith. The significance and the power of each lies in the doing of it with a heart of obedient faith, not in the thing itself.

So it is with many aspects of the Christian experience. We can analyze a thing endlessly, ultimately resulting in its demise. This happens in many churches. We reason away the woman’s head covering. We reason away the nonconformed lifestyle. We reason away the permanence of marriage. We reason away brotherhood accountability. What we have left has no resemblance to the simple teachings of Jesus. Discipleship calls us to faithful obedience. Jesus and the apostles taught it, so we do it. The blessing and the power lie in the doing of it.

That is what Peter discovered. He walked on water! He did not dip a toe to test the water first. I like to think he leaped from the boat and hit the water with both feet. That would be faith and Peter had faith.

But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:30-32.

Peter had faith to walk on water until he began to look around and began to process his situation using the scientific method. This is not to invalidate the scientific method. The scientific method proves the order of creation and the evidence of a creator.

In Hebrews 11 we read that …faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen –Hebrews 11:1.

It is our faith that is the substance and our faith that is the evidence of spiritual realities. Just as the scientific method proves the realities of the created world, so our faith proves spiritual realities.

Boisterous wind and crashing waves produced a fearful, sinking Peter. We sometimes criticize Peter for taking his eyes off of Jesus and sinking into the waves; however, Peter walked on water, I know of no one else who walked on water. When we transition from obedient faith to carnal rationalization, we lose power with God.

Are we suggesting that faith is irrational? No, not at all. As a matter of fact, the first act of faith is to believe that Jesus is the logos. John wrote, In the beginning was the Word [Logos], and the Word [Logos], was with God, and the Word [Logos], was God –John 1:1. It is from the Greek word Logos that we get our English word logic.

Just as there are laws in nature that make the scientific method durable and replicable, so there are spiritual laws that give order and cohesion to our inner man. Jesus is the embodiment of these truths. His teachings are the revelation of these truths and through his death and resurrection these truths have become accessible to all. Jesus promised, Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth… –John 16:13.

Men of faith are men who have eyes to see these spiritual realities. Their vision is not limited to the natural world. They understand that there are spiritual realities that have “cause and effect” in our lives that are every bit as powerful as the “cause and effect” that we see about us in the natural world every day.

These realities are only visible to men of faith. Paul wrote, But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned –1 Corinthians 2:14. Men of faith, are men whose lives are governed by spiritual realities that are incomprehensible to the natural man. If you will be a man of faith, expect to be misunderstood. You are embarking on a journey that will run counter to the world view of many.

As Peter began to sink into the waves he cried out, “Lord, save me”. His plaintive cry revealed an absolute trust in his Lord. Jesus reached out His hand and rescued him. Jesus next words continue to challenge us. He said to Peter, …O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? Matthew 14:31. Peter had just walked on water—a feat no man had accomplished before or since, yet Jesus called it “little faith” and asked, “why did you doubt?”.

Jesus said at another time, …If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20.

If Peter’s “little faith” empowered him to walk on water, and if faith as tiny as a grain of mustard seed can remove mountains what does that say of your and my faith?

Perhaps it is evidence that our faith is littler than Peter’s “little faith” and tinier than the tiny grain of mustard seed?! It is also evidence that God honors little faith. What he does not honor is no faith. According to your faith be it unto you. Little faith…walk on water! No faith…sink beneath the waves!

Since Jesus is the “Logos”, He is the master of the natural world and the spirit world. He proved himself to be the Master of the wind and the waves—and when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:32. And He proved Himself to be the Master of the spirit world—then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God –Matthew 14:33.

We, in our western world, have become so satiated with materialism that we can easily be led to believe that natural realities are the most powerful realities. This materialism assaults us, not just with the abundance of material things, but also with a bombardment of humanistic philosophy. Humanistic philosophy is thinking that is devoid of spiritual reality… that is devoid of faith.

If you, as a man, find yourself sinking in waves of despair… be it financial struggles… be it relational difficulties… moral failure or maybe you find yourself being your own worst critic…may I challenge you to lift your eyes to the one who is Logos. Jesus is the one who is master of your circumstances and the one who would be Lord of your soul. To allow Jesus to be Lord of your soul is to live in faith obedience to the radical teachings of Jesus.

To live in harmony with the natural world we honor the laws of nature. When we are replacing a roof, we respect the law of gravity. When driving a vehicle, we slow down for turns out of respect for the law of inertia. Defy the natural laws and someone gets hurt.

To live in harmony with the spiritual world, we honor the law of Christ. We love our neighbor. We forgive our brother. We keep our marriage vows. We bear …one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2.

Men of faith are men who are attune to these spiritual realities and order their lives accordingly.

Y Pedro le respondió y dijo: Señor, si eres tú, mándame que vaya a ti sobre las aguas. Y él dijo: Ven. Y cuando Pedro descendió de la barca, anduvo sobre las aguas para ir a Jesús – Mateo 14:28-29.

Los hombres que siguen a Jesús son hombres de fe. El discipulado no es para cobardes ni para pusilánimes, ni para aquellos que exigen una explicación racional para los actos de obediencia. Los discípulos habían pasado el día con Jesús. Después de la alimentación de los cinco mil, Mateo escribe que …luego Jesús obligó a sus discípulos a subir a la barca, y a pasar al otro lado, mientras él despedía a la gente – Mateo 14:22.

Si había algo con lo que los discípulos estaban familiarizados y en lo que eran diestros, era navegar las aguas del lago de Galilea. Ése era su territorio. Pedro y Juan habían pescado en estas aguas con su padre desde su más temprana memoria. Pero aquella noche avanzaban poco… el viento era adverso.

Y en la cuarta vigilia de la noche, Jesús fue a ellos andando sobre el mar. Y cuando los discípulos le vieron andar sobre el mar, se turbaron, diciendo: ¡Es un fantasma! y gritaron de miedo. Mas luego Jesús les habló, diciendo: Tened ánimo; yo soy; no temáis – Mateo 14:25-27.

Entonces Pedro hizo esta audaz petición: …Señor, si eres tú, manda que yo vaya a ti sobre las aguas – Mateo 14:28. ¿Qué estaría pensando Pedro? Nunca había caminado sobre el agua. Jesús no le estaba pidiendo que caminara sobre el agua. No era lógico. Desafiaba las leyes de la naturaleza… sin embargo, cuando Jesús dijo “ven”, Pedro salió de la barca y caminó sobre el agua para ir a Jesús. ¡Así es! Estaba pisando sobre el agua.

Pedro estaba respondiendo a un llamado claro de Jesús. Jesús dijo “ven”. Es importante que entendamos que la fe es nuestra respuesta al llamado claro de Dios sobre nuestras vidas. Con demasiada frecuencia, en nuestra ambición por ser útiles elegimos nuestro propio camino y llamamos a esa ambición “fe” cuando puede que Dios no esté en ella en absoluto.

Si quieres ser un hombre de fe, abre tu Biblia y ora. Pídele a Dios que revele su plan para tu vida. La Biblia contiene muchos mandamientos que pueden proporcionar dirección práctica para nuestras vidas. Toma a Dios por su Palabra. Da un paso de fe y obediencia y entonces experimentarás el milagro del poder de Dios en tu vida.

La barca de Pedro era su seguridad. Él y su barca tenían una larga relación. Le había servido bien durante muchos años. Pedro se sentía como en casa en su vieja embarcación, aunque aquella noche no parecía responder bien a su maestría marinera. Había sacado muchas capturas de pescado por la borda. Ahora, mientras estaba en la cubierta observando a Jesús acercarse “caminando sobre el agua”, le embargó el deseo de ir a Jesús. Con imprudente abandono saltó desde la cubierta… y ocurrió un milagro.

Un caminar de fe a menudo nos llama a alejarnos de lo que es familiar y seguro. Si hacemos de la seguridad nuestra prioridad—si limitamos nuestras acciones a riesgos cuidadosamente calculados (limitados a aquello que podemos manejar y controlar)—limitamos el poder de Dios obrando en y a través de nosotros.

Nuestros antepasados en Europa sabían que si abrazaban el camino del discipulado sin reservas, podría ser costoso. Arriesgaron la confiscación de sus bienes; muchos de ellos perdieron todo lo que poseían. Como afrontaron voluntariamente la prisión y la muerte, los llamamos héroes de la fe. Eran hombres dispuestos a renunciar a todo por causa del evangelio. Debido a su fe recibimos los beneficios de una herencia piadosa.

Alabo a nuestra generación más joven de jóvenes anabautistas por su disposición a hacer de seguir a Jesús una prioridad. En el pasado nuestra prioridad había sido construir nuestra base de seguridad, ya fuera la granja o el negocio, y luego considerar la obra misional como una posibilidad. Ése nunca fue el modelo de servicio de Jesús. Cuando Jesús envió a sus discípulos dijo: Y les dijo: Tomad nada para el camino; ni báculo, ni alforja, ni pan, ni dinero; ni tengáis dos túnicas – Lucas 9:3.

Después, cuando regresaron, Jesús les preguntó: Y les dijo: Cuando os envié sin bolsa, ni alforja, ni zapatos, ¿os faltó algo? Y dijeron: Nada – Lucas 22:35.

No necesitas ir a misiones en el extranjero para experimentar el poder de Dios en tu vida. Todo acto de obediencia radical es un acto de fe. Hay hombres en nuestras comunidades anabautistas que están experimentando la derrota moral. Si vamos a sucumbir a una mentalidad de víctima (“no puedo evitarlo”), y definir el fracaso moral como una adicción, nos predisponemos a una derrota continua. Los hombres de fe son hombres de acción que toman pasos medibles de obediencia que los guiarán hacia la victoria final. El fracaso moral comienza con pequeños compromisos que terminan en una derrota aplastante.

Las acciones de Pedro no eran lógicas. Si Pedro hubiera procesado su decisión usando el método científico, no habría tomado tal riesgo. Muchos de los mandamientos sencillos de Cristo no tienen razonamiento científico aparente. Desde el bautismo, hasta la comunión, pasando por el lavamiento de pies, y la unción con aceite, todos son actos de fe. La significación y el poder de cada uno radican en hacerlo con un corazón de fe obediente, no en la cosa en sí.

Así sucede con muchos aspectos de la experiencia cristiana. Podemos analizar una cosa sin fin, resultando finalmente en su muerte. Esto ocurre en muchas iglesias. Razonamos en contra del velo en la cabeza de la mujer. Razonamos en contra del estilo de vida conforme. Razonamos en contra de la permanencia del matrimonio. Razonamos en contra de la responsabilidad fraternal. Lo que nos queda no tiene parecido con las enseñanzas sencillas de Jesús. El discipulado nos llama a la obediencia fiel. Jesús y los apóstoles la enseñaron, así que la hacemos. La bendición y el poder están en el acto de hacerlo.

Eso fue lo que Pedro descubrió. ¡Caminó sobre el agua! No sumergió un dedo del pie para probar el agua primero. Me gusta pensar que saltó de la barca y golpeó el agua con ambos pies. Eso sería fe, y Pedro tenía fe.

Pero al ver el viento recio, tuvo miedo; y comenzando a hundirse, clamó, diciendo: Señor, sálvame. Y al momento Jesús, extendiendo la mano, lo agarró, y le dijo: ¡Hombre de poca fe! ¿por qué dudaste? Y cuando subieron a la barca, se calmó el viento – Mateo 14:30-32.

Pedro tuvo fe para caminar sobre el agua hasta que empezó a mirar alrededor y a procesar su situación usando el método científico. Esto no es para invalidar el método científico. El método científico prueba el orden de la creación y la evidencia de un Creador.

En Hebreos 11 leemos que …la fe es la certeza de lo que se espera, la convicción de lo que no se ve – Hebreos 11:1.

Es nuestra fe la que es la sustancia y nuestra fe la que es la evidencia de realidades espirituales. Así como el método científico demuestra las realidades del mundo creado, así nuestra fe demuestra las realidades espirituales.

El viento recio y las olas violentas produjeron un Pedro temeroso y que se hundía. A veces criticamos a Pedro por apartar los ojos de Jesús y hundirse en las olas; sin embargo, Pedro caminó sobre el agua; no conozco a nadie más que haya caminado sobre el agua. Cuando pasamos de una fe obediente a la racionalización carnal, perdemos poder con Dios.

¿Estamos sugiriendo que la fe es irracional? No, en absoluto. De hecho, el primer acto de fe es creer que Jesús es el logos. Juan escribió: En el principio era el Verbo [Logos], y el Verbo [Logos] estaba con Dios, y el Verbo [Logos] era Dios – Juan 1:1. Es de la palabra griega Logos de donde proviene nuestra palabra en inglés logic.

Así como hay leyes en la naturaleza que hacen que el método científico sea duradero y replicable, así hay leyes espirituales que dan orden y cohesión a nuestro hombre interior. Jesús es la encarnación de estas verdades. Sus enseñanzas son la revelación de estas verdades y, por medio de su muerte y resurrección, estas verdades se han hecho accesibles a todos. Jesús prometió: Pero cuando venga el Espíritu de verdad, él os guiará a toda la verdad… – Juan 16:13.

Los hombres de fe son hombres que tienen ojos para ver estas realidades espirituales. Su visión no está limitada al mundo natural. Entienden que hay realidades espirituales que tienen “causa y efecto” en nuestras vidas que son tan poderosas como la “causa y efecto” que vemos a nuestro alrededor en el mundo natural cada día.

Estas realidades sólo son visibles para los hombres de fe. Pablo escribió: Pero el hombre natural no percibe las cosas que son del Espíritu de Dios, porque para él son locura; y no las puede entender, porque se han de discernir espiritualmente – 1 Corintios 2:14. Los hombres de fe son hombres cuyas vidas están gobernadas por realidades espirituales que son incomprensibles para el hombre natural. Si quieres ser un hombre de fe, espera ser malinterpretado. Estás emprendiendo un camino que irá en contra de la cosmovisión de muchos.

Cuando Pedro comenzó a hundirse en las olas clamó: “Señor, sálvame”. Su clamor lastimero reveló una confianza absoluta en su Señor. Jesús extendió su mano y lo rescató. Las siguientes palabras de Jesús continúan desafiándonos. Le dijo a Pedro: …¡Hombre de poca fe! ¿por qué dudaste? – Mateo 14:31. Pedro acababa de caminar sobre el agua — una hazaña que ningún hombre había realizado antes ni después — y, aun así, Jesús la llamó “poca fe” y preguntó: “¿por qué dudaste?”.

Jesús dijo en otra ocasión: …Si tuvierais fe como un grano de mostaza, diréis a este monte: Pásate de aquí allá, y se pasará; y nada os será imposible – Mateo 17:20.

Si la “poca fe” de Pedro lo capacitó para caminar sobre el agua, y si la fe tan pequeña como un grano de mostaza puede mover montañas, ¿qué dice eso de tu fe y de la mía?

Quizá sea evidencia de que nuestra fe es más pequeña que la “poca fe” de Pedro y más diminuta que el minúsculo grano de mostaza. También es evidencia de que Dios honra la fe pequeña. Lo que no honra es la ausencia de fe. Conforme a vuestra fe os sea hecho. Poca fe… ¡camina sobre el agua! Sin fe… ¡hundirse bajo las olas!

Para ser el Logos, Jesús es el Señor del mundo natural y del mundo espiritual. Él se mostró Señor del viento y de las olas — y cuando subieron a la barca, se calmó el viento – Mateo 14:32. Y se mostró Señor del mundo espiritual — entonces los que estaban en la barca vinieron y le adoraron, diciendo: Verdaderamente eres Hijo de Dios – Mateo 14:33.

Nosotros, en nuestro mundo occidental, nos hemos vuelto tan saciados de materialismo que fácilmente podemos ser llevados a creer que las realidades naturales son las realidades más poderosas. Este materialismo nos asalta, no sólo con la abundancia de cosas materiales, sino también con un bombardeo de filosofía humanista. La filosofía humanista es un pensamiento desprovisto de realidad espiritual… desprovisto de fe.

Si tú, como hombre, te hallas hundiéndote en olas de desesperación… sea por problemas financieros… sea por dificultades relacionales… por fracaso moral o quizá te encuentres siendo tu peor crítico… permíteme desafiarte a levantar los ojos al que es el Logos. Jesús es quien domina tus circunstancias y quien quiere ser Señor de tu alma. Permitir que Jesús sea Señor de tu alma es vivir en obediencia de fe a las enseñanzas radicales de Jesús.

Para vivir en armonía con el mundo natural honramos las leyes de la naturaleza. Cuando reemplazamos un tejado, respetamos la ley de la gravedad. Al conducir un vehículo, aminoramos en las curvas por respeto a la ley de inercia. Si desafías las leyes naturales, alguien sale lastimado.

Para vivir en armonía con el mundo espiritual honramos la ley de Cristo. Amamos a nuestro prójimo. Perdonamos a nuestro hermano. Conservamos nuestros votos matrimoniales. Soportamos …los unos a los otros cargas, y así cumplid la ley de Cristo – Gálatas 6:2.

Los hombres de fe son hombres que están sintonizados con estas realidades espirituales y ordenan sus vidas en consecuencia.

This hymn is generally considered to be one of the greatest hymns ever written and is found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. It was written by a man who was frail in body, but strong in spirit. It was he who coined the phrase, “It is better to wear out than to rust out.” Let us now take a glimpse into the life of this servant of God.

Henry Francis Lyte, the author of this great and noteworthy hymn, was born June 1, 1793, in Ednam, near Kelso, Scotland. At a young age, he was left an orphan and was in comparative poverty. He was educated at Trinity College in Dublin, Ireland. It was there that his gift of poetry began to appear, winning him three prizes. His primary goal with his studies was to become a physician, instead, by the providence of God, he became a minister of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

One day in Cornwall, a fellow clergyman who was on his deathbed, requested that Lyte would come and give him some spiritual comfort. “To their mutual grief, they found themselves [both] groping for the light, veritable blind guides”. As they searched for truth and assurance of salvation, they fixed their faith on Christ, and Lyte came away from that sickroom a changed man, never to be the same again. It is said that it was his encounter with God at the bedside of that dying man that prompted Lyte’s noble hymn, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.” In the year 1823, Henry F. Lyte took charge of a seashore parish, Lower Brixham, in Devonshire, England. It was at that place where he spent the last 23 years of his life toiling as a pastor for the spiritual good of the poor fishing people and the rough seafaring men of that region until his death in the fall of 1847. For all of Henry’s dedication and labor, he received a reward: having a Sunday school of several hundred scholars, as well as “a splendid company of seventy or eighty teachers, personally trained by him.”

Throughout his lifetime, his health was continually threatened by asthma and tuberculosis. Notwithstanding his physical frailties, he worked tirelessly with an established reputation as a poet, musician, and minister. Wherever he went, he was greatly loved and admired by his people. Toward the end of these later years, his health became gradually worse. So it was that during the winter months, he felt compelled to seek a warmer climate in Italy, which is a part of southern Europe.

Though he was greatly weakened by his sickness, on September 4, 1847, as Lyte was about to leave to head southward, he was arrested by an “irresistible desire” to preach once more to his congregation. He dearly loved these people and he had labored among them for so many years. “Against the protest of his amazed friends, he accomplished this purpose, and it is recorded that Lyte nearly had to crawl to the pulpit and his message came as from a dying man.” “O brethren,” he said, as he entered the familiar pulpit for the last time, “I stand here among you today, as alive from the dead, if I may hope to impress it upon you, and induce you to prepare for that solemn hour which must come to all, by a timely appreciation and dependance on the death of Christ.” These final words made a deep impact upon his congregation, after which he closed the service by administering the Lord’s Supper to his weeping people. Later that evening, after the service, he was inspired to “poetical composition” and wrote the eight stanzas of his last and greatest hymn:

Abide with me: fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide:
when other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

Swift to its close ebbs out life’s little day;
Earth’s joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But, as Thou dwell’st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free,
Come, not to sojourn, but abide, with me.

Come not in terrors, as the King of kings;
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings;
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea;
Come, Friend of sinners, and thus ‘bide with me.

Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though rebellious and perverse meanwhile,
thou hast not left me, oft as I left thee:
On to the close, O Lord, abide with me.

I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, O abide with me.

I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless:
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death’s sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom, and point me to the skies;
Heaven’s morning breaks, and earth’s vain shadows flee:
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

This hymn he gave to one of the family members that very night. Leaving the following day, he began his trek to Rome, Italy, hoping to gain some relief from his sickness. Lyte make it as far as Nice, France where his sickness prevented his further travel. He passed away soon after the age of 55, on November 20, 1847. His last words were “Joy! Peace!”

The scene behind this hymn is that of the resurrected Christ Jesus walking on the road to Emmaus with two of His somewhat sad and discouraged disciples. As they neared the end of their seven-mile walk and approached the village where they were going, Jesus …made as though he would have gone further. But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them –Luke 24:28-29.

We can draw a parallel between that scene and Henry F. Lyte’s own experience of drawing toward the close of his earthly journey. Thus, as the disciples besought the risen Lord to abide with them in the close of that ancient day, so was the meaning of this song written in the “shadows of death” to the hymn writer.

Lyte himself composed a tune for this hymn on the same evening that he wrote it, but it never became widely used. However, the tune universally used was written fourteen years later by William Henry Monk, a noted London musician, and editor of the well-known Anglican hymnal, Hymns Ancient and Modern. He included this song in his first edition, which was published in 1861.

In all, William H. Monk composed 50 tunes for the hymnal. It is said that Monk, being “inspired by the beauty of a glorious sunset while yet experiencing a deep personal sorrow,” composed (in only 10 minutes) the tune, Eventide, for the song, “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk also wrote the music for other familiar hymns such as “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious”, and “The Strife Is O’er”.

To summarize, Henry Lyte experienced many sorrows during his lifetime. Both of his parents died at an early age leaving him an orphan. And his own sickness and frailty caused him to be in ongoing danger of asthma and tuberculosis. Yet, in spite of all his trials, we find in him a resilient spirit to reach out to others; to touch and minister the Gospel to those poor people among whom he lived. “In no other writer,” says Dr. Breed (in the Treasury of Hymn Stories), “are poetry and religion more exquisitely united.”

101 Hymn Stories,
Treasury of Hymn Stories
Author- Henry Francis Lyte, 1793-1847
Composer- William Henry Monk, 1823-1889
Tune Name - “Eventide”

Este himno suele considerarse uno de los mayores himnos jamás escritos y se encuentra en casi todos los himnarios o libros de himnos publicados hoy. Fue escrito por un hombre de cuerpo frágil, pero de espíritu fuerte. Fue él quien acuñó la frase: «Es mejor desgastarse que oxidarse». Demos ahora un vistazo a la vida de este siervo de Dios.

Henry Francis Lyte, el autor de este gran y notable himno, nació el 1 de junio de 1793 en Ednam, cerca de Kelso, Escocia. Siendo joven quedó huérfano y vivió en relativa pobreza. Se educó en el Trinity College de Dublín, Irlanda. Fue allí donde comenzó a manifestarse su don de la poesía, que le valió tres premios. Su objetivo principal con los estudios era llegar a ser médico; en cambio, por la providencia de Dios, llegó a ser ministro del evangelio de Jesucristo.

Un día en Cornualles, un compañero clérigo que estaba en su lecho de muerte pidió que Lyte fuera a darle consuelo espiritual. “Para su mutuo pesar, se hallaron [ambos] tanteando la luz, verdaderos guías ciegos”. Mientras buscaban la verdad y la certeza de la salvación, fijaron su fe en Cristo, y Lyte salió de esa habitación del enfermo siendo un hombre cambiado, para no volver a ser el mismo. Se dice que fue su encuentro con Dios al lado de ese hombre moribundo lo que impulsó el noble himno de Lyte, «Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken». En el año 1823, Henry F. Lyte asumió el cargo de una parroquia costera, Lower Brixham, en Devonshire, Inglaterra. Fue en ese lugar donde pasó los últimos 23 años de su vida trabajando como pastor para el bien espiritual de la gente pobre de pescadores y de los rudos marineros de esa región hasta su muerte en el otoño de 1847. Por toda la dedicación y labor de Henry, recibió una recompensa: una escuela dominical con varios cientos de alumnos, así como “una espléndida compañía de setenta u ochenta maestros, entrenados personalmente por él”.

A lo largo de su vida, su salud estuvo continuamente amenazada por el asma y la tuberculosis. No obstante sus fragilidades físicas, trabajó incansablemente y tuvo una reputación establecida como poeta, músico y ministro. Dondequiera que iba, era muy amado y admirado por su pueblo. Hacia el final de esos últimos años, su salud empeoró gradualmente. Así fue que durante los meses de invierno se sintió obligado a buscar un clima más cálido en Italia, que forma parte del sur de Europa.

Pese a estar muy debilitado por su enfermedad, el 4 de septiembre de 1847, cuando Lyte estaba a punto de partir hacia el sur, fue detenido por un “deseo irresistible” de predicar una vez más a su congregación. Amaba profundamente a esa gente y había trabajado entre ellos durante tantos años. “Contra la protesta de sus asombrados amigos, cumplió este propósito, y está registrado que Lyte casi tuvo que arrastrarse hasta el púlpito y su mensaje vino como de un hombre moribundo.” “Oh hermanos,” dijo, al subir al púlpito familiar por última vez, “estoy aquí entre vosotros hoy, como vivo de entre los muertos, si puedo esperar impresionar esto en vosotros, e induciros a prepararos para aquella solemne hora que debe llegar a todos, mediante una apreciación oportuna y dependencia en la muerte de Cristo.” Estas últimas palabras causaron un profundo impacto en su congregación, después de lo cual cerró el servicio administrando la Cena del Señor a su pueblo lloroso. Más tarde esa noche, después del servicio, se sintió inspirado para la “composición poética” y escribió las ocho estrofas de su último y mayor himno:

Abide with me: fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide:
when other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

Swift to its close ebbs out life’s little day;
Earth’s joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But, as Thou dwell’st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free,
Come, not to sojourn, but abide, with me.

Come not in terrors, as the King of kings;
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings;
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea;
Come, Friend of sinners, and thus ‘bide with me.

Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though rebellious and perverse meanwhile,
thou hast not left me, oft as I left thee:
On to the close, O Lord, abide with me.

I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, O abide with me.

I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless:
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death’s sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom, and point me to the skies;
Heaven’s morning breaks, and earth’s vain shadows flee:
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

Este himno lo entregó a un miembro de la familia esa misma noche. Partiendo al día siguiente, comenzó su caminata hacia Roma, Italia, con la esperanza de obtener algún alivio para su enfermedad. Lyte llegó hasta Niza, Francia, donde su dolencia le impidió continuar el viaje. Falleció poco después, a los 55 años, el 20 de noviembre de 1847. Sus últimas palabras fueron “¡Gozo! ¡Paz!”

La escena que subyace a este himno es la del Cristo resucitado caminando por el camino a Emaús con dos de Sus discípulos algo tristes y desanimados. Cuando se acercaban al final de su caminata de siete millas y se aproximaban al pueblo adonde iban, Jesús …parecía que iba más lejos. Pero ellos le obligaron a quedarse, diciendo: Quédate con nosotros; porque raya el día y se ha puesto ya el sol. Y entró para quedarse con ellos –Lucas 24:28-29.

Podemos trazar un paralelismo entre esa escena y la propia experiencia de Henry F. Lyte al acercarse al final de su jornada terrenal. Así, como los discípulos rogaron al Señor resucitado que se quedara con ellos al cierre de aquel antiguo día, tal fue el significado de esta canción escrita en las “sombras de la muerte” para el autor del himno.

La misma noche en que lo escribió, Lyte compuso una melodía para este himno, pero nunca llegó a usarse ampliamente. Sin embargo, la melodía usada universalmente fue escrita catorce años después por William Henry Monk, un músico londinense de renombre y editor del conocido himnario anglicano Hymns Ancient and Modern. Incluyó esta canción en su primera edición, publicada en 1861.

En total, William H. Monk compuso 50 melodías para el himnario. Se dice que Monk, estando “inspirado por la belleza de un glorioso atardecer mientras aún experimentaba un profundo dolor personal”, compuso (en solo 10 minutos) la melodía Eventide para la canción “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk también escribió la música de otros himnos conocidos como “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious” y “The Strife Is O’er”.

En resumen, Henry Lyte experimentó muchas penas a lo largo de su vida. Ambos padres murieron a edad temprana, dejándolo huérfano. Y su propia enfermedad y fragilidad lo mantuvieron en peligro continuo por el asma y la tuberculosis. Sin embargo, a pesar de todas sus pruebas, encontramos en él un espíritu resiliente para alcanzar a los demás; para tocar y ministrar el Evangelio a esas gentes pobres entre las que vivió. “En ningún otro autor,” dice el Dr. Breed (en Treasury of Hymn Stories), “la poesía y la religión están más exquisitamente unidas.”

101 Hymn Stories,
Treasury of Hymn Stories
Autor- Henry Francis Lyte, 1793-1847
Compositor- William Henry Monk, 1823-1889
Nombre de la melodía - “Eventide”

And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus –Matthew 14:28-29.

Men who follow Jesus are men of faith. Discipleship is not for cowards or the faint of heart, nor is it for those who demand a rationale for acts of obedience. The disciples had spent the day with Jesus. After the feeding of the five thousand Matthew writes that …straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away –Matthew 14:22.

If there was anything that the disciples were familiar with and skilled in, it was sailing the waters of Galilee. This was their territory. Peter and John had fished these waters with their father from their earliest remembrance. But tonight, they were making little headway… the wind was contrary.

And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid –Matthew 14:25-27.

Peter then made this bold appeal …Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water –Matthew 14:28. What was Peter thinking? He had never walked on water. Jesus was not asking him to walk on water. It was not logical. It defied the laws of nature… yet when Jesus said “come”. Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water to go to Jesus. That’s right! He was treading on water.

Peter was responding to a clear call from Jesus. Jesus said “come”. It is important that we understand that faith is our response to the clear call of God on our lives. Too often in our ambition to be useful we choose our path and call our ambition “faith” when God may not be in it at all.

If you want to be a man of faith, open your Bible and pray. Ask God to reveal His plan for your life. The Bible contains many commandments that can provide practical direction for our lives. Take God at His Word. Step out in faith and obedience then you will experience the miracle of God’s power in your life.

Peter’s boat was his security. He and his boat had a long relationship. It had served him well for many years. Peter felt right at home in his old bark, although tonight she did not seem to respond well to his masterful seamanship. He had drawn many a draught of fish over her gunwales. Now as he stands on her deck watching Jesus approach, “walking on the water”, he was overcome with a desire to go to Jesus. In reckless abandonment he stepped off her deck …and a miracle happened.

A walk of faith often calls us away from that which is familiar and secure. If we make safety and security our priority—if we limit our actions to carefully calculated risks (limited to that which we can manage and control)—we limit the power of God working in and through us.

Our forefathers in Europe knew that if they embraced the journey of unreserved discipleship, it could be costly. They risked the seizure of their property; many of them lost all that they owned. Since they willingly faced imprisonment and death, we refer to them as heroes of the faith. These were men who were willing to abandon all for the sake of the gospel. Because of their faith we receive the benefits of a godly heritage.

I commend our younger generation of Anabaptist youth for their willingness to make following Jesus a priority. In the past our priority has been to build our security base, be it our farm or business, and then consider mission work as a possibility. That was never Jesus’ model for service. When Jesus sent out his disciples he said. And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece –Luke 9:3.

Later, after they had returned, Jesus asked them, And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing –Luke 22:35.

You do not need to go into foreign missions to experience the power of God released in your life. Every act of radical obedience is an act of faith. There are men in our Anabaptist communities who are experiencing moral defeat. If we are going to succumb to a victim mentality (“I can’t help it”), and define moral failure as an addiction, we set ourselves up for ongoing defeat. Men of faith are men of action who take measurable steps of obedience which will lead them to ultimate victory. Moral failure begins with small compromises that end in crushing defeat.

Peter’s actions were not logical. If Peter would have processed his decision using the scientific method, he would not have taken such a risk. Many of the simple commands of Christ have no apparent scientific reasoning. From baptism, to communion, to foot washing, to anointing with oil, these are all acts of faith. The significance and the power of each lies in the doing of it with a heart of obedient faith, not in the thing itself.

So it is with many aspects of the Christian experience. We can analyze a thing endlessly, ultimately resulting in its demise. This happens in many churches. We reason away the woman’s head covering. We reason away the nonconformed lifestyle. We reason away the permanence of marriage. We reason away brotherhood accountability. What we have left has no resemblance to the simple teachings of Jesus. Discipleship calls us to faithful obedience. Jesus and the apostles taught it, so we do it. The blessing and the power lie in the doing of it.

That is what Peter discovered. He walked on water! He did not dip a toe to test the water first. I like to think he leaped from the boat and hit the water with both feet. That would be faith and Peter had faith.

But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:30-32.

Peter had faith to walk on water until he began to look around and began to process his situation using the scientific method. This is not to invalidate the scientific method. The scientific method proves the order of creation and the evidence of a creator.

In Hebrews 11 we read that …faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen –Hebrews 11:1.

It is our faith that is the substance and our faith that is the evidence of spiritual realities. Just as the scientific method proves the realities of the created world, so our faith proves spiritual realities.

Boisterous wind and crashing waves produced a fearful, sinking Peter. We sometimes criticize Peter for taking his eyes off of Jesus and sinking into the waves; however, Peter walked on water, I know of no one else who walked on water. When we transition from obedient faith to carnal rationalization, we lose power with God.

Are we suggesting that faith is irrational? No, not at all. As a matter of fact, the first act of faith is to believe that Jesus is the logos. John wrote, In the beginning was the Word [Logos], and the Word [Logos], was with God, and the Word [Logos], was God –John 1:1. It is from the Greek word Logos that we get our English word logic.

Just as there are laws in nature that make the scientific method durable and replicable, so there are spiritual laws that give order and cohesion to our inner man. Jesus is the embodiment of these truths. His teachings are the revelation of these truths and through his death and resurrection these truths have become accessible to all. Jesus promised, Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth… –John 16:13.

Men of faith are men who have eyes to see these spiritual realities. Their vision is not limited to the natural world. They understand that there are spiritual realities that have “cause and effect” in our lives that are every bit as powerful as the “cause and effect” that we see about us in the natural world every day.

These realities are only visible to men of faith. Paul wrote, But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned –1 Corinthians 2:14. Men of faith, are men whose lives are governed by spiritual realities that are incomprehensible to the natural man. If you will be a man of faith, expect to be misunderstood. You are embarking on a journey that will run counter to the world view of many.

As Peter began to sink into the waves he cried out, “Lord, save me”. His plaintive cry revealed an absolute trust in his Lord. Jesus reached out His hand and rescued him. Jesus next words continue to challenge us. He said to Peter, …O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? Matthew 14:31. Peter had just walked on water—a feat no man had accomplished before or since, yet Jesus called it “little faith” and asked, “why did you doubt?”.

Jesus said at another time, …If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20.

If Peter’s “little faith” empowered him to walk on water, and if faith as tiny as a grain of mustard seed can remove mountains what does that say of your and my faith?

Perhaps it is evidence that our faith is littler than Peter’s “little faith” and tinier than the tiny grain of mustard seed?! It is also evidence that God honors little faith. What he does not honor is no faith. According to your faith be it unto you. Little faith…walk on water! No faith…sink beneath the waves!

Since Jesus is the “Logos”, He is the master of the natural world and the spirit world. He proved himself to be the Master of the wind and the waves—and when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:32. And He proved Himself to be the Master of the spirit world—then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God –Matthew 14:33.

We, in our western world, have become so satiated with materialism that we can easily be led to believe that natural realities are the most powerful realities. This materialism assaults us, not just with the abundance of material things, but also with a bombardment of humanistic philosophy. Humanistic philosophy is thinking that is devoid of spiritual reality… that is devoid of faith.

If you, as a man, find yourself sinking in waves of despair… be it financial struggles… be it relational difficulties… moral failure or maybe you find yourself being your own worst critic…may I challenge you to lift your eyes to the one who is Logos. Jesus is the one who is master of your circumstances and the one who would be Lord of your soul. To allow Jesus to be Lord of your soul is to live in faith obedience to the radical teachings of Jesus.

To live in harmony with the natural world we honor the laws of nature. When we are replacing a roof, we respect the law of gravity. When driving a vehicle, we slow down for turns out of respect for the law of inertia. Defy the natural laws and someone gets hurt.

To live in harmony with the spiritual world, we honor the law of Christ. We love our neighbor. We forgive our brother. We keep our marriage vows. We bear …one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2.

Men of faith are men who are attune to these spiritual realities and order their lives accordingly.
