Greetings to one and all in our dear Saviour’s name, Jesus Christ. Another year has passed from the present into the annals of history. Nothing that we have said or done can be recalled and re-lived. Another year is before us. Many are waiting with bated breath, anticipating what this new year will bring forth.

I read somewhere in the news that those on the frontier of technology believe that this year will be a big year for artificial intelligence. One example given was: they are anticipating that this technology will be able to be a part of events such as board meetings with the ability to hear and understand all that is shared by each one present. Then at the end of the meeting, with the push of a button, the artificial intelligence will produce detailed minutes of that meeting with a fair degree of accuracy. Over the last number of years, many of the things that used to be considered science fiction have recently become reality, so, likely, this will become a new reality as well.

What is this world coming to? To the Bible-literate Christian, the end of time certainly seems to be fast approaching. According to the United Nations, the world’s population surpassed 8 billion on November 15, 2022. Many in the world are desperately trying to figure out how to sustain that many people for the long term. Just like the Bible has prophesied, there is an uptick in the number of famines, drought, floods, earthquakes, wars, and rumors of wars, etc. One thing that I find interesting is that even though the world does not want to retain God in their knowledge, insurance companies still refer to certain specific events as “acts of God”.

As Bible-believing Christians how shall we then live? And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet –Matthew 24:6. Let us remember that we should not be troubled. Rather, we should remember that …he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:13. If we, like Peter, take our eyes off of our Lord and start focusing on the stormy conditions around us we will start to sink as well. Remember, it is …the fearful, and unbelieving … [who] shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone… –Revelation 21:8. But, He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son –Revelation 21:7.

In this issue of the magazine, we again have an interesting group of articles for your consideration. Join us as we learn of a somewhat obscure, yet influential leader of the early Anabaptist movement in Switzerland. Let’s honestly evaluate our own hearts as we follow the expository teaching from Habakkuk regarding what it means to have a real faith that is first personal, then corporate. Together we can consider what it really means to enter into the rest of God that is detailed in Hebrews chapter four. The youth can take a look into their emotions as they consider those times when they feel like giving up. The author for our sisters’ article has tackled a very difficult subject—when and how to be submissive as a godly wife. We have another thought-provoking article in the discipleship series. And the doctor has chosen to venture into some uncharted territory with the first of a two-part series on cancer.

A final thought I wish to share, a story in fact… Recently, I heard a first-hand account of a man who was lost before God, how he came to spiritual awakening, and how this started affecting his life. This story caused me to stop and consider where I am as a Christian. Is my relationship with my Lord vibrant? How strong is my commitment towards God and His Word? Is my love for my Lord and Saviour still as real and as strong as it was when I first had my awakening and was converted? I’m sure there are more questions that we could ask ourselves in light of this real-life story. I’ll let you as a reader start compiling your own list. Now for the story…

This man is living somewhere within the United States of America. He is a married man with a young family. He is part of a certain religious group within the plain people—those of Anabaptist heritage. Throughout his lifetime he had endeavored to live his life according to the mandates set forth by the leaders of his local church. Yet, for some reason, he had not been finding answers to his personal need, whatever that was—perhaps even he didn’t know.

This man and some of his family were traveling and ended up lodging overnight in a motel. There, in the nightstand drawer he discovered a book titled “The Holy Bible”. Sure, in his church the Bible was read or quoted each week during their normal worship services. Although this man understood English quite well, his church had a policy that they did not want to be too worldly or too modern by reading from an English Bible so they continued their efforts of teaching God’s Word using the original language of their people.

The problem was that this man, somehow, never developed an understanding of that language, thus he never heard the truth of God’s Word. All that he heard was what 1 Corinthians chapter 14 refers to as tongues (languages) and since he didn’t understand the language and since there was no interpretation given, he was not able to be edified. The purpose of this story is not to find fault or to place blame, but rather to bring light to an obvious problem among some of the plain people. A problem for which God would surely desire to see changes made for the betterment of those seeking Him in such settings.

With this in mind, we now come back to this man—a man zealous in his religious life—yet having NEVER heard the message of the Gospel of Jesus Christ. As he hesitantly picked up this English Bible he cautiously started to read the message contained within those book covers. As he read, he became more and more excited. Here were things that he had never heard before—teachings that brought sense to his many questions and the emptiness that he felt within his soul. He was so engrossed that he almost couldn’t pull himself away to allow time for sleep. After a short night, they went on with their travels.

Completing their business they returned home, but life would never be the same for that man. Something had been awakened deep within his soul. Questions had been answered. Longings had been met. Peace had begun to settle over his troubled heart. At long last, he had found the answer, but his time of reading had been so short. Surely there was more to learn, much more. So, before too much time had elapsed, he once more scheduled a trip to get away from his local area and to once more provide a reason to spend another night in a motel with a Bible in the nightstand drawer. He eagerly anticipated another night alone with God and His Word. After a second sleepless night spent devouring the teachings of the Scriptures, he started seeking others who understood and practiced what the Bible said. He was desiring to fellowship and learn all that he could from those who understood God’s Word and who practiced what they preached.

As this man has endeavored to find his way through this confusing maze of religious idiosyncrasies he finally purchased a German/English Bible. He felt driven in his continued pursuit of the Truth, yet he was afraid to be found out by his local church leaders. He wanted to stay within his local church, yet his conscience demanded that he must continue his search. For some reason he believed that his local church leaders would not be understanding in his quest for truth and that maybe he would be placed under church discipline for his actions.

His local church is a part of the descendants of the Anabaptists who were persecuted for their faith, including their desire to understand, and read the Scriptures in their native tongue—Swiss or German, instead of Latin as was required by the church leaders of their day. Yet here he is, some 500 years later, in America, possibly facing persecution from his own church which claims to be a part of the “right” church of God. Herein, his church leaders are finding themselves on the opposite side of the issue of freedom of religious worship that their forefathers suffered for, since they are insisting that the only way to learn of God’s will is through the official language of Scripture—German. This is NO different than the struggle of the original Anabaptists who were persecuted for not studying the Scriptures in the official language of their day—Latin.

Let’s remember, IF church members do not understand the teachings of God’s Word due to their church leaders’ stubborn insistence that the church members are NOT allowed to read or hear the Scriptures in the language that they understand, then the ignorance of the common man WILL be laid at the feet of those leaders come judgment day. Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account… –Hebrews 13:17. Obey here is only in the context of God’s Word, not just according to church leaders’ personal ideas or whims. For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad –2 Corinthians 5:10. Every person will receive personal judgment based on what the Bible teaches NOT according to a church’s detailed dogma.

When I think of the zealous efforts of this man I think of the verse of Scripture… When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel –Matthew 8:10. I also observe the current trends of some of our plain publishing houses—they have borrowed from the world’s idea (in a spiritual way, of course) that to sell books and reading material they need to print exhilarating stories, ones that keep people on the edge of their seats—all this because today’s Christian has become bored with that which seems old-fashioned.

What a difference between this story and many of today’s Anabaptist descendants. Many of today’s conservative Anabaptist people have a difficult time getting excited about the Bible. They are too over-stimulated by the lack of rest and quiet in their normal daily lives.

Usually, we hear of stories like this from the jungles of Central America, the deserts of Africa, or the slums of India. What I am amazed about is that this story takes place right in the midst of one of our plain groups of conservative Anabaptists. Let’s seek God for opportunities to share the truth of the Gospel message with those within the sphere of our influence. We might be surprised how many people we rub shoulders with during our daily lives who would be just as hungry for the Truth as the man in our story.

Hilsener til alle i vår kjære Frelsers navn, Jesus Kristus. Nok et år har gått fra nåtiden inn i historiens annaler. Ingenting av det vi har sagt eller gjort kan hentes tilbake og leves om igjen. Et nytt år ligger foran oss. Mange venter spent og undrende på hva dette nye året vil bringe.

Jeg leste et sted i nyhetene at de som står i fronten for teknologien mener at dette året vil bli stort for kunstig intelligens. Ett eksempel som ble nevnt var: de forventer at denne teknologien vil kunne delta i hendelser som styremøter med evne til å høre og forstå alt som blir delt av hver enkelt til stede. Så, på slutten av møtet, med et tastetrykk, vil den kunstige intelligensen produsere detaljerte referater av møtet med en rimelig grad av nøyaktighet. I løpet av de siste årene har mange ting som før ble sett på som science fiction blitt virkelighet, så sannsynligvis vil også dette bli en ny realitet.

Hva går denne verdenen mot? For den bibelkunnige kristne virker endetiden å nærme seg raskt. Ifølge De forente nasjoner passerte verdens befolkning 8 milliarder den 15. november 2022. Mange i verden prøver fortvilet å finne ut hvordan man kan holde så mange mennesker i live på lang sikt. Akkurat som Bibelen har profetert, er det en økning i antallet hungersnød, tørke, flom, jordskjelv, kriger og rykter om krig, osv. En ting jeg synes er interessant, er at selv om verden ikke vil bevare Gud i sin kunnskap, refererer forsikringsselskaper fremdeles enkelte bestemte hendelser som «Guds gjerninger».

Som bibeltro kristne, hvordan skal vi da leve? Og dere skal høre om kriger og rykter om kriger: se at dere ikke blir forstyrret: for alt dette må skje, men enden er ennå ikke –Matteus 24:6. La oss huske at vi ikke skal la oss forstyrre. Snarere bør vi minne oss om at …den som står ut til enden, han skal bli frelst –Matteus 24:13. Hvis vi, som Peter, tar øynene av vår Herre og begynner å fokusere på de stormfulle omstendighetene rundt oss, vil vi også begynne å synke. Husk at …de feige og vantro … [skal] ha sin del i sjøen som brenner med ild og svovel… –Åpenbaringen 21:8. Men, Den som seirer skal arve alt dette; og jeg vil være hans Gud, og han skal være min sønn –Åpenbaringen 21:7.

I dette nummeret av bladet har vi igjen en interessant gruppe artikler til din overveielse. Bli med oss når vi lærer om en noe uklar, men likevel innflytelsesrik leder i den tidlige anabaptistbevegelsen i Sveits. La oss ærlig vurdere våre egne hjerter når vi følger den ekspositoriske undervisningen fra Habakkuk om hva det betyr å ha en ekte tro som først er personlig, så fellesskapelig. Sammen kan vi vurdere hva det virkelig betyr å gå inn i Guds sabbatstro som er detaljert i Hebreerne kapittel fire. Ungdommen kan se nærmere på sine følelser når de vurderer de tider de føler for å gi opp. Forfatteren av vår søsterartikkel har tatt for seg et svært vanskelig tema—når og hvordan være underdanig som en gudfryktig ektefelle. Vi har en annen tankevekkende artikkel i disippelgjøringsserien. Og legen har valgt å våge seg inn på uutforsket terreng med første del av en to-delt serie om kreft.

En siste tanke jeg ønsker å dele, faktisk en historie… Nylig hørte jeg førstehåndsfortellingen om en mann som var fortapt for Gud, hvordan han kom til åndelig oppvåkning, og hvordan dette begynte å påvirke hans liv. Denne historien fikk meg til å stoppe opp og vurdere hvor jeg er som kristen. Er mitt forhold til min Herre levende? Hvor sterk er min forpliktelse til Gud og hans Ord? Er min kjærlighet til min Herre og Frelser fortsatt like ekte og sterk som da jeg først fikk mitt åndelige oppvåkning og ble omvendt? Jeg er sikker på at det finnes flere spørsmål vi kan stille oss i lys av denne virkelige historien. Jeg lar deg som leser begynne å lage din egen liste. Nå—til historien…

Denne mannen bor et sted i Amerikas forente stater. Han er en gift mann med en ung familie. Han er en del av en bestemt religiøs gruppe blant de enkle folkene—de av anabaptistisk arv. Gjennom hele livet hadde han forsøkt å leve etter påbudene som ble gitt av lederne i hans lokale menighet. Likevel, av en eller annen grunn, hadde han ikke funnet svar på sitt personlige behov, hva det enn var—kanskje visste ikke engang han det selv.

Denne mannen og noen av hans familie var på reise og endte opp med å overnatte på et motell. Der, i nattbordskuffen, oppdaget han en bok med tittelen «Den hellige Bibel». Sikkert, i hans menighet ble Bibelen lest eller sitert hver uke under deres normale gudstjenester. Selv om denne mannen forstod engelsk ganske godt, hadde hans menighet en politikk om at de ikke ønsket å være for verdenslige eller for moderne ved å lese fra en engelsk Bibel, så de fortsatte sin undervisning av Guds Ord ved hjelp av folkets opprinnelige språk.

Problemet var at denne mannen på en eller annen måte aldri hadde utviklet forståelse for det språket, og derfor hadde han aldri hørt sannheten i Guds Ord. Alt han hørte var det 1 Korinterbrev kapittel 14 omtaler som tunger (språk), og siden han ikke forstod språket og det ikke ble gitt noen tolkning, kunne han ikke bli oppbygget. Hensikten med denne historien er ikke å finne feil eller gi skyld, men heller å belyse et åpenbart problem blant noen av de enkle folkene. Et problem som Gud uten tvil ville ønske å se endringer for, til det bedre for dem som søker ham i slike sammenhenger.

Med dette i tankene kommer vi nå tilbake til denne mannen—en mann nidkjær i sitt religiøse liv—men som ALDRI hadde hørt budskapet om evangeliet om Jesus Kristus. Da han nølende plukket opp denne engelske Bibelen begynte han forsiktig å lese budskapet som lå mellom permene. Etter hvert som han leste, ble han mer og mer begeistret. Her var ting han aldri hadde hørt før—læresetninger som gav mening til hans mange spørsmål og tomheten han hadde følt i sin sjel. Han var så oppslukt at han nesten ikke klarte å rive seg løs for å få tid til søvn. Etter en kort natt fortsatte de reisen.

Da de var ferdige med sine ærend, vendte de hjem, men livet ville aldri bli det samme for den mannen. Noe hadde våknet dypt i hans sjel. Spørsmål var blitt besvart. Lengsler var blitt møtt. Fred hadde begynt å senke seg over hans plagede hjerte. Endelig hadde han funnet svaret, men lesetiden hans hadde vært så kort. Sikkert var det mer å lære, mye mer. Så, før det gikk for lang tid, planla han nok en tur for å komme seg bort fra lokalmiljøet og igjen ha en grunn til å tilbringe en natt på et motell med en Bibel i nattbordskuffen. Han så ivrig frem mot en ny natt alene med Gud og hans Ord. Etter en andre søvnløs natt brukt til å sluke Skriftens læresetninger, begynte han å søke andre som forstod og praktiserte det Bibelen sa. Han ønsket fellesskap og å lære alt han kunne fra dem som forstod Guds Ord og som praktiserte det de forkynte.

Mens denne mannen forsøkte å finne sin vei gjennom dette forvirrende labyrintet av religiøse særegenheter, kjøpte han til slutt en tysk/engelsk bibel. Han følte seg drevet i sin fortsatte søken etter sannheten, men han var redd for å bli oppdaget av lederne i hans lokale menighet. Han ønsket å bli i sin menighet, men hans samvittighet krevde at han måtte fortsette sin søken. Av en eller annen grunn trodde han at menighetslederne ikke ville være forståelsesfulle i hans søken etter sannhet, og at han kanskje ville bli utsatt for menighetsstraff for sine handlinger.

Hans lokale menighet er en del av etterkommerne av anabaptistene som ble forfulgt for sin tro, inkludert deres ønske om å forstå og lese Skriftene på sitt eget morsmål—sveitsisk eller tysk, i stedet for latin som ble påkrevd av kirkens ledere i deres tid. Men her er han, noen 500 år senere, i Amerika, muligens utsatt for forfølgelse fra sin egen menighet som påstår å være en del av Guds «rette» kirke. Her setter menighetslederne seg på motsatt side av spørsmålet om frihet i religionsutøvelse som deres forfedre led for, siden de insisterer på at den eneste måten å lære Guds vilje på er gjennom Skriftens offisielle språk—tysk. Dette er IKKE annerledes enn kampen de opprinnelige anabaptistene hadde, som ble forfulgt for ikke å studere Skriftene på tidens offisielle språk—latin.

La oss huske, HVIS menighetsmedlemmer ikke forstår Guds Ords lære fordi menighetslederne sta insisterer på at medlemmene IKKE får lese eller høre Skriftene på et språk de forstår, så vil den vanlige manns uvitenhet BLI lagt ved disse lederes føtter på dommens dag. Adlyd dem som har ledelsen over dere, og underordn dere: for de våker over deres sjeler, som de må gi regnskap for… –Hebreerne 13:17. Å adlyde her er kun i sammenheng med Guds Ord, ikke bare i henhold til menighetslederes personlige ideer eller innfall. For vi må alle åpenbare oss for Kristi domsstol; for at var og en må få det han har gjort i sin kropp, etter det han har gjort, enten det er godt eller ondt –2 Korinterbrev 5:10. Hver person vil få personlig dom basert på hva Bibelen lærer, IKKE etter en menighets detaljerte dogmer.

Når jeg tenker på denne mannens nidkjære anstrengelser, tenker jeg på skriftstedet… Da Jesus hørte det ble han forbauset, og sa til dem som fulgte ham: Sannelig sier jeg dere: Jeg har ikke funnet så stor tro, ikke engang i Israel –Matteus 8:10. Jeg observerer også nåværende trender hos noen av våre enkle forlag—de har lånt fra verdens ideer (på en åndelig måte, selvfølgelig) om at for å selge bøker og lesestoff må de trykke opp spennende historier, slike som holder folk på kanten av setet—alt dette fordi dagens kristne er blitt lei av det som virker gammeldags.

For en forskjell mellom denne historien og mange av dagens anabaptistiske etterkommere. Mange av dagens konservative anabaptistfolk har vanskelig for å bli begeistret over Bibelen. De er for overstimulerte av mangel på hvile og stillhet i sine daglige liv.

Vanligvis hører vi historier som denne fra junglene i Mellom-Amerika, ørkenene i Afrika eller slumstrøkene i India. Det som forundrer meg er at denne historien finner sted midt i en av våre enkle grupper av konservative anabaptister. La oss søke Gud om muligheter til å dele sannheten i evangeliebudskapet med dem innenfor vår innflytelsessfære. Vi kan bli overrasket over hvor mange mennesker vi kommer i berøring med i vår daglige omgang som ville være like sultne etter sannheten som mannen i vår historie.

Over the last number of years, we have spent much of our time in Haiti serving on the mission field. From time to time, we would return to America for visits of varying lengths and reasons. Each trip back to the U.S. has been challenging as we have observed the changes—changes in culture, in technology, in values, etc. Sometimes, as our family looks at our country, it seems as if there is little hope. Clearly evil is taking control. However, to me the change that seems to be the most concerning is that of the church. Most, if not all, God-fearing Christians clearly see the moral decline of our land, but what about our churches? Is the church holding firm to biblical teaching or is it following the world in gradual change and compromise?

Overall, the American church seems to be thriving financially. Our businesses are improving, along with our standard of living, while spiritually, many Christians seem to be losing their zeal for godliness. What will the church look like in 40, 50, or 80 years?

When we read the book of Acts, we see something over and over. God’s power is revealed, and souls are added to the kingdom—daily.

Usually, when people see something that they need, they go after it. When they see something that they are sure that they must have, they can even become desperate or radical as they pursue a way to get that thing.

Jesus tells the parable of a field containing a lost or hidden treasure—Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field –Matthew 13:44.

Here you have a man that may be satisfied with his life. He has possessions and good health. As he is walking home, he sees something that he has never seen before, something of great value, something that he must have. No one needed to force him to take action. Also, it didn’t take days or weeks before he acted—he saw it and decided that he must have it immediately. So, he went and sold all that he had. (Selling ‘most’ would not buy the field. No, he must sell all.) After he buys the field, he now possesses the most important thing in the world. He will keep it forever, he will never part with it, no matter the cost. He also realizes that this treasure is not only good for him, but for all mankind. In fact, he soon understands that if he does not find this treasure, then sell all that he has, and purchase the treasure, he will perish—forever. People around him may not understand him—his actions, his decisions, his moves—they may be confused at first, as to why he did what he did. However, they will not be confused about one thing—this treasure was worth all the world to this man. His love for it cannot be denied.

This man now possesses something within himself out of which flows love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance… –Galatians 5:22-23, which is the fruit of the Spirit. He seems to have a special power about him. He overcomes suffering and difficulties with ease—at least that’s how it appears to those looking on. He holds no grudges and loves even his enemies. Truly this man has found something for which it is worth selling all. Then, lo and behold, others begin to sell what they have, to possess this treasure for themselves also.

According to the Bible, God’s people are expected to be the light of the world and the salt of the earth. Let’s seriously and honestly ask ourselves this question: “Do those around us experience us as biblical light and salt?!”

During the time of the Acts of the Apostles, there were clear lines, and the church grew. Yes, it suffered; however, it still grew, at times daily.

As I travel to different communities, I see something that is hard to understand. There are certain groups of people that seem to look different from the world around them, but still, they seem to act the same as mainstream America. Their interests are the same; their desires are the same. I have wondered why they continue to look different from the world while they seem to have the same values.

I was in a grocery store when a woman that I had never seen before approached me. She was very cheerful and asked me some random questions, then before she left, she said, “I love you Mennonites; you are so cute!” It was heart-breaking—we did not cause conviction in her heart. We did not even set an example for her. Instead, we were simply entertaining her.

In Haiti, my family would walk into a church or a spiritual gathering, and the ladies would pull at their miniskirts, trying desperately to cover their nakedness. I’ve even seen some remove their jewelry, without us speaking a word! Light exposes darkness: it brings conviction. That is why Christians used to be hated by those around them.

So why are we a cultural display to the world? What has changed? Could it be that we are simply reproducing the cultural norms that the world holds dear? Are we leaving God out, while we continue to do the things this world has come to accept?

When Nicodemus came to Jesus, he instantly began to lift up the Lord saying …we know that thou art a teacher come from God: for no man can do these miracles that thou doest, except God be with him –John 3:2.

However, Jesus seems to ignore these words and He cuts right to the chase, when He says: …Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God –John 3:3. It’s almost as if He was saying, [“Although you come seeking, you seem to possess some truth, and you are a ruler of the Jews, but the first thing that you must know is this: You must be born again.”] Powerful words. He then goes on to state the obvious—That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit –John 3:6.

Today we try to hide behind our flesh (our unregenerated human nature). We are good at blaming our shortcomings on the fact that we are in the flesh; some go as far as to say we are all sinners and therefore, we can do nothing but fail. However, here Jesus says that that which is flesh is flesh, and that which is spirit is spirit! Oh, that we could grasp the simplicity in these profound words! Flesh is flesh, not spirit. And spirit is spirit, not flesh. We are born with an adamic nature (a bent towards doing evil) from our mother’s womb. The prophet Jeremiah tells us that The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it? –Jeremiah 17:9. He goes on to explain: I the LORD search the heart, I try the reins… –Jeremiah 17:10.

We may try, like the masses, to tame our human nature with all of its desires and passions. We may practice and prepare; we can groom the flesh in a certain way that seems good unto us. However, there is no hope, for in the flesh we cannot please God. So, according to Jesus we must be born again. Nicodemus asks: …How can a man be born when he is old? can he enter the second time into his mother’s womb, and be born? –John 3:4.

Jesus then profoundly preaches a sermon to him, stating how there must be death …as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up –John 3:14.

Jesus goes on to say …every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved –John 3:20. If we must first die, to be born again, how do we die? And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts –Galatians 5:24. So how does a sincerely seeking person practically become “born again”?

  • That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved… –Romans 10:9-10.
  • Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost –Acts 2:38.
  • …the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it –Hebrews 4:2.
  • But without faith it is impossible to please him… –Hebrews 11:6.
  • And he came … preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins –Luke 3:3.
  • I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved… –John 10:9.
  • …Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me… –Mark 8:34-35.
  • Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me –Revelation 3:20.
  • …And Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and it is he that talketh with thee. And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him –John 9:35-38.
  • For by grace are ye saved through faith … it is the gift of God: Not of works… –Ephesians 2:8-9.

Here we see that there are various aspects of becoming, of being, and of remaining born again. We have faith that is full and unwavering. We need to have faith in the God of the Bible—The great I AM, THAT I AM. Our faith must be open to those around us—we must not keep it hidden. We must not allow the fear of man to keep our faith in God quiet. We need to start walking in repentance. We need to seek baptism unto repentance for the remission of sins. We need to see Jesus as the door—the only way to God through which we must enter and then walk in righteousness. We need to see Jesus’ death on the cross as the gift of God to us for salvation. And as we see God for who He is and Jesus, His Son, for who He is, then we must worship. All of these (and others) are a part of becoming born again, or it is the outworking thereof, which continues to perpetuate the process of staying born again.

Are true conversions still happening in our day—are people being born again the way that Jesus was explaining to Nicodemus? We mock the prayer of the cheap-grace gospel, we look down on the powerless altar calls, but what are we doing about our need? We need to crucify the flesh. We need to live no longer unto self. And we need to be born again by the spirit of God. After spending time at the feet of Jesus, learning of Him and His Father and Their ways, we then need to go forth with Holy Spirit power to share with lost and struggling souls what God has done for us. As people see our life that has been changed by God, He will draw the souls that are seeking into the kingdom of His dear Son.

If we are truly born again, we will have the same testimony and passion as the disciples. We will grow in grace and understanding. We will allow God to be God and His Word to be the Truth—final and complete! We will stop trying to reform the goats among us. Rather we will share the Gospel message with them so they can become converted—they will then be sheep with hearts of flesh instead of hearts of stone. A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you: and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them –Ezekiel 36:26-27.

So why is there a lack of truly born-again believers among us? I believe this world has captivated us. We look for compromise wherever we can. Sure, we will dress a little differently if we must, but don’t take away all our pleasure and fun. We fill our lives with everything this sin-sick world has to offer—money, entertainment, luxury, vacations, food, and drink, then when we walk by the field with the treasure hidden in it, we do not even notice it. It’s there, simply forgotten.

When we sing the songs of Zion and pray the prayers of petition and praise, is God at work? Is there an everlasting joy in our hearts or are we tossed about by the storms of life? Are we out trying to help the blind to see or are we trying to conceal the fact that we’re Christians?!

Let’s put an end to this defeated Christian life that knows little of victory. Let’s put an end to the lukewarm living that’s accepted by the masses around us! Let’s put an end to loving this present evil world! Let’s put an end to individualism and self! Let’s put on the Lord Jesus Christ and together march out to battle against the enemy of our souls. Enough of just sitting at home singing the songs; let’s go out and fight for that which so many before us have fought. We read about it in our church history books. We glean encouragement and insight from our Bibles and our copies of the Martyrs Mirror. But what will future generations say about us? Will there be any godly testimonies written about us?

The Bible is full of promises:

  • Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you… –Matthew 7:7-8.
  • …God … will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it –1 Corinthians 10:13.
  • …If ye have faith, and doubt not … ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou removed, and be thou cast into the sea; it shall be done –Matthew 21:21.
  • This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh –Galatians 5:16.

And the list goes on! Are these a part of our lives? Are we living in victory, or are we hiding behind a failed culture with no power?

Dear ones, God wants a people to call His own today just as much as He did in the beginning. He wants us! It is a sobering thought. God wants to raise us up by His Spirit, He wants to breathe into us His breath—the Breath of Life. He wants to bless us with spiritual blessings that cannot be fathomed!

However, the old man must die—his pride, his name, his attitude, his fame. The old man must give way for the new; they cannot live together in the same body. According to scripture, it’s one or the other. One will die, and one will live—forever!

Let’s not allow the serpent (or the devil) to deceive us any longer. The pleasures of this life are only for a moment. We reap what we sow; we will not escape the Judgment. God wants to give us the Kingdom; He wants to give us the inheritance. He wants to be a father to us, to call us His dear children. He wants to walk with us through this narrow way. He wants to encourage us when we are down, and He wants to fight for us when we are weak. He wants to give us an identity, a part of the family of God—His children. He wants to give us power to overcome all sin (not just some), today and tomorrow and for the rest of our life. When we fail, He wants to give us a desire to repent. Then when we accept that desire and move back towards Him, He wants to forgive us.

The darker this world gets, the easier the light should shine. Are we, through the Spirit, that lighthouse standing tall in the face of the storm? The wind and the waves beat against it, but it cannot be moved. Its light shines through the darkest times, giving hope to the weary souls stranded in life. Its foundation does not move; its purpose does not change.

We can fill our heads with knowledge and know all the right things to say and do. However, if we are not quickened by the Spirit of God, we are simply a culture that will change with each generation. This change will continue until the last generation has been fully submerged in the seas of this world. All the while, the destroyer of our souls gains more for himself.

This battle is real—some will win, many will lose. The loss is great, greater than I can describe; and so is the win.

Twenty first century Christian, what will you do?

Selama beberapa tahun terakhir, kami menghabiskan banyak waktu di Haiti melayani di ladang misi. Dari waktu ke waktu, kami kembali ke Amerika untuk kunjungan dengan berbagai panjang dan alasan. Setiap perjalanan kembali ke AS selalu menantang saat kami mengamati perubahan—perubahan dalam budaya, dalam teknologi, dalam nilai-nilai, dan sebagainya. Terkadang, saat keluarga kami memandang negeri ini, tampak seolah ada sedikit harapan. Jelas kejahatan mulai menguasai. Namun, bagi saya perubahan yang paling mengkhawatirkan adalah perubahan di gereja. Sebagian besar, jika bukan semua, orang Kristen yang takut akan Tuhan jelas melihat kemerosotan moral negeri kita, tetapi bagaimana dengan gereja kita? Apakah gereja bertahan pada pengajaran alkitabiah atau mengikuti dunia dalam perubahan dan kompromi yang perlahan?

Secara keseluruhan, gereja Amerika tampaknya makmur secara finansial. Bisnis kita meningkat, bersamaan dengan standar hidup kita, sementara secara rohani, banyak orang Kristen tampak kehilangan semangat untuk ketakwaan. Seperti apa rupa gereja dalam 40, 50, atau 80 tahun?

Saat kita membaca kitab Kisah Para Rasul, kita melihat sesuatu berulang kali. Kuasa Allah dinyatakan, dan jiwa-jiwa ditambahkan ke dalam kerajaan—setiap hari.

Biasanya, ketika orang melihat sesuatu yang mereka butuhkan, mereka mengejarnya. Ketika mereka melihat sesuatu yang mereka yakin harus dimiliki, mereka bahkan bisa menjadi putus asa atau radikal saat mencari cara untuk mendapatkannya.

Yesus menceritakan perumpamaan tentang ladang yang berisi harta yang hilang atau tersembunyi—Lagi pula, Kerajaan sorga itu adalah seperti harta yang terpendam di dalam suatu ladang; seorang yang mendapatkannya menyembunyikannya, lalu karena sukacitanya pergi menjual segala miliknya lalu membeli ladang itu –Matius 13:44.

Di sini ada seorang laki-laki yang mungkin puas dengan hidupnya. Ia memiliki harta dan kesehatan yang baik. Saat ia pulang berjalan, ia melihat sesuatu yang belum pernah ia lihat sebelumnya, sesuatu yang bernilai besar, sesuatu yang harus dimilikinya. Tidak ada yang memaksanya untuk bertindak. Juga, tidak butuh hari atau minggu sebelum ia bertindak—ia melihatnya dan memutuskan bahwa ia harus memilikinya segera. Maka, ia pergi dan menjual segala miliknya. (Menjual ‘kebanyakan’ tidak akan membeli ladang itu. Tidak, ia harus menjual segalanya.) Setelah ia membeli ladang itu, sekarang ia memiliki hal paling penting di dunia. Ia akan menyimpannya selamanya, ia tak akan pernah melepaskannya, tak peduli berapa biayanya. Ia juga menyadari bahwa harta ini tidak hanya baik bagi dirinya, tetapi bagi seluruh umat manusia. Bahkan, ia segera mengerti bahwa jika ia tidak menemukan harta ini, lalu menjual segala miliknya, dan membeli harta itu, ia akan binasa—selamanya. Orang-orang di sekelilingnya mungkin tidak memahaminya—tindakannya, keputusannya, gerak-geriknya—mereka mungkin bingung pada awalnya, mengapa ia melakukan apa yang dilakukannya. Namun, mereka tidak akan bingung tentang satu hal—harta ini sangat berharga bagi laki-laki itu. Kasihnya terhadapnya tak dapat disangkal.

Laki-laki ini sekarang memiliki sesuatu dalam dirinya yang memancarkan kasih, sukacita, damai sejahtera, kesabaran, kelemahlembutan, kebaikan, iman, kelemahlembutan, penguasaan diri… –Galatia 5:22-23, yang adalah buah Roh. Ia tampak memiliki kuasa istimewa. Ia mengatasi penderitaan dan kesulitan dengan mudah—setidaknya demikian yang tampak bagi orang yang melihat. Ia tidak menyimpan dendam dan mengasihi bahkan musuh-musuhnya. Sesungguhnya laki-laki ini telah menemukan sesuatu yang pantas untuk dijual segala-galanya. Lalu, lihatlah, orang lain mulai menjual milik mereka, untuk memiliki harta ini bagi diri mereka juga.

Menurut Alkitab, umat Allah diharapkan menjadi terang dunia dan garam bumi. Marilah kita bertanya dengan sungguh-sungguh dan jujur kepada diri sendiri: “Apakah orang di sekitar kita mengalami kita sebagai terang dan garam yang alkitabiah?!”

Pada masa Kisah Para Rasul, ada garis-garis yang jelas, dan gereja tumbuh. Ya, gereja menderita; namun, tetap tumbuh, kadang-kadang tiap hari.

Saat saya bepergian ke berbagai komunitas, saya melihat sesuatu yang sulit dimengerti. Ada kelompok-kelompok tertentu yang tampak berbeda dari dunia di sekitar mereka, tetapi masih tampak berperilaku sama seperti arus utama Amerika. Minat mereka sama; keinginan mereka sama. Saya heran mengapa mereka terus terlihat berbeda dari dunia sementara tampak memiliki nilai-nilai yang sama.

Saya sedang di sebuah toko kelontong ketika seorang wanita yang belum pernah saya lihat sebelumnya mendekati saya. Ia sangat ceria dan menanyakan beberapa pertanyaan acak, lalu sebelum pergi, ia berkata, “Aku cinta kalian Mennonite; kalian sangat lucu!” Itu menyayat hati—kita tidak menimbulkan pertobatan di hatinya. Kita bahkan tidak memberikan teladan kepadanya. Sebaliknya, kita sekadar menghiburnya.

Di Haiti, keluarga saya masuk ke sebuah gereja atau pertemuan rohani, dan para wanita segera menarik rok mini mereka, berusaha dengan susah payah menutupi ketelanjangan mereka. Saya bahkan melihat beberapa melepaskan perhiasan mereka, tanpa kami mengucapkan sepatah kata pun! Terang menyingkap kegelapan: itu membawa pertobatan. Itulah sebabnya orang Kristen dulu dibenci oleh orang di sekitar mereka.

Jadi mengapa kita menjadi tontonan budaya bagi dunia? Apa yang berubah? Mungkinkah kita sekadar mereproduksi norma-norma budaya yang dihargai dunia? Apakah kita mengesampingkan Tuhan, sementara kita terus melakukan hal-hal yang dunia ini sudah terima?

Ketika Nikodemus datang kepada Yesus, ia langsung memuji Tuhan dengan mengatakan …kami tahu bahwa Engkau datang sebagai seorang guru yang datang dari Allah; karena tak seorang pun dapat membuat tanda-tanda yang Engkau lakukan, kalau Allah tidak menyertai dia –Yohanes 3:2.

Namun, Yesus tampak mengabaikan kata-kata itu dan Ia langsung ke intinya, ketika Ia berkata: …Sesungguhnya, sesungguhnya, Kukatakan kepadamu, Jika seorang tidak dilahirkan kembali, ia tidak dapat melihat Kerajaan Allah –Yohanes 3:3. Hampir seolah-olah Dia berkata, [“Meskipun engkau datang mencari, engkau tampak memiliki beberapa kebenaran, dan engkau adalah seorang pemimpin orang Yahudi, tetapi hal pertama yang harus engkau tahu adalah ini: Engkau harus dilahirkan kembali.”] Kata-kata yang kuat. Ia kemudian menerangkan yang jelas—Apa yang dilahirkan dari daging ialah daging, dan apa yang dilahirkan dari Roh ialah roh –Yohanes 3:6.

Hari ini kita mencoba bersembunyi di balik daging kita (sifat manusia yang belum diperbarui). Kita pandai menyalahkan kekurangan kita pada fakta bahwa kita berada dalam daging; beberapa sampai mengatakan kita semua berdosa dan karena itu, kita tak bisa melakukan apa-apa selain gagal. Namun, di sini Yesus mengatakan bahwa apa yang daging adalah daging, dan apa yang roh adalah roh! Oh, kiranya kita dapat menangkap kesederhanaan dalam kata-kata yang mendalam ini! Daging itu daging, bukan roh. Dan roh itu roh, bukan daging. Kita dilahirkan dengan sifat Adamik (kecenderungan melakukan kejahatan) sejak dalam kandungan ibu kita. Nabi Yeremia berkata bahwa Hati lebih licik dari segala sesuatu dan sangat jahat; siapakah yang dapat mengetahuinya? –Yeremia 17:9. Ia melanjutkan menjelaskan: Akulah TUHAN yang menyelidiki hati, yang menguji batin-batin, untuk memberikan kepada setiap orang menurut jalannya, menurut buah perbuatannya –Yeremia 17:10.

Kita mungkin berusaha, seperti kebanyakan orang, menjinakkan sifat manusia kita dengan segala keinginan dan nafsunya. Kita dapat berlatih dan bersiap; kita bisa membentuk daging sedemikian rupa yang tampak baik bagi kita. Namun, tidak ada harapan, karena dalam daging kita tidak dapat menyenangkan Allah. Jadi, menurut Yesus kita harus dilahirkan kembali. Nikodemus bertanya: …Bagaimana mungkin seorang dilahirkan, ketika ia sudah tua? Dapatkah ia masuk ke rahim ibunya untuk kedua kali dan dilahirkan? –Yohanes 3:4.

Yesus lalu dengan penuh makna berkhotbah kepadanya, menyatakan bagaimana harus ada kematian …seperti Musa meninggikan ular di padang gurun, demikian juga Anak Manusia harus ditinggikan –Yohanes 3:14.

Yesus melanjutkan berkata …setiap orang yang berbuat jahat membenci terang dan tidak datang kepada terang, supaya perbuatan-perbuatannya tidak disingkapkan –Yohanes 3:20. Jika kita harus terlebih dahulu mati, supaya dilahirkan kembali, bagaimana kita mati? Dan mereka yang menjadi milik Kristus telah menyalibkan daging dengan segala hawa nafsunya –Galatia 5:24. Jadi bagaimana seorang yang sungguh-sungguh mencari secara praktis menjadi “dilahirkan kembali”?

  • Jika kamu mengaku dengan mulutmu, bahwa Yesus adalah Tuhan, dan percaya dalam hatimu, bahwa Allah telah membangkitkan Dia dari antara orang mati, maka kamu diselamatkan… –Roma 10:9-10.
  • Lalu Petrus berkata kepada mereka: Bertobatlah dan hendaklah seorang seorang dari kamu dibaptis dalam nama Yesus Kristus untuk pengampunan dosa; maka kamu akan menerima karunia Roh Kudus –Kisah Para Rasul 2:38.
  • …firman yang disampaikan tidaklah menguntungkan mereka, karena tidak disertai iman pada orang-orang yang mendengarnya –Ibrani 4:2.
  • Tetapi tanpa iman tidak mungkin berkenan kepada-Nya… –Ibrani 11:6.
  • Ia datang … memberitakan baptisan pertobatan untuk pengampunan dosa –Lukas 3:3.
  • Akulah pintu; barangsiapa masuk melalui Aku ia akan diselamatkan… –Yohanes 10:9.
  • …barangsiapa mau mengikut Aku, ia harus menyangkal dirinya, memikul salibnya dan mengikut Aku… –Markus 8:34-35.
  • Lihatlah, Aku berdiri di muka pintu dan mengetuk; jika ada orang yang mendengar suara-Ku dan membuka pintu, Aku akan masuk mendapatinya dan makan bersama-sama dengan dia, dan ia bersama-sama dengan Aku –Wahyu 3:20.
  • …Yesus berkata kepadanya: Engkau telah melihat Dia, dan Dialah yang berbicara kepadamu. Lalu ia berkata: Tuhanku, aku percaya. Dan ia menyembah Dia –Yohanes 9:35-38.
  • Sebab oleh kasih karunia kamu diselamatkan oleh iman … dan ini bukan dari dirimu, itu pemberian Allah: bukan hasil pekerjaanmu… –Efesus 2:8-9.

Di sini kita melihat bahwa ada berbagai aspek menjadi, berada, dan tetap dilahirkan kembali. Kita memiliki iman yang penuh dan tak goyah. Kita perlu memiliki iman kepada Allah dalam Alkitab—Aku adalah AKU ADALAH. Iman kita harus terbuka kepada orang di sekitar kita—kita tidak boleh menyembunyikannya. Kita tidak boleh membiarkan takut akan manusia membuat iman kita kepada Allah menjadi sunyi. Kita perlu mulai hidup dalam pertobatan. Kita perlu mencari baptisan kepada pertobatan untuk pengampunan dosa. Kita perlu melihat Yesus sebagai pintu—satu-satunya jalan kepada Allah melalui mana kita harus masuk dan kemudian hidup dalam kebenaran. Kita perlu melihat kematian Yesus di kayu salib sebagai pemberian Allah bagi kita untuk keselamatan. Dan ketika kita melihat Allah sebagaimana Dia adanya dan Yesus, Anak-Nya, sebagaimana Dia adanya, maka kita harus menyembah. Semua ini (dan lain-lain) adalah bagian dari menjadi dilahirkan kembali, atau merupakan buah dari itu, yang terus mengerjakan proses tetap dilahirkan kembali.

Apakah pertobatan sejati masih terjadi di zaman kita—apakah orang dilahirkan kembali sebagaimana Yesus menjelaskan kepada Nikodemus? Kita mengejek doa-doa dari Injil kasih karunia murah, kita meremehkan panggilan altar yang tak berkuasa, tetapi apa yang kita lakukan tentang kebutuhan kita? Kita perlu menyalibkan daging. Kita perlu hidup bukan lagi untuk diri sendiri. Dan kita perlu dilahirkan kembali oleh Roh Allah. Setelah menghabiskan waktu di kaki Yesus, belajar tentang Dia dan Bapa-Nya dan cara-cara Mereka, kita kemudian perlu maju dengan kuasa Roh Kudus untuk berbagi dengan jiwa-jiwa yang hilang dan berjuang apa yang telah Allah lakukan bagi kita. Ketika orang melihat hidup kita yang telah diubahkan oleh Allah, Dia akan menarik jiwa-jiwa yang sedang mencari ke dalam kerajaan Anak-Nya yang terkasih.

Jika kita sungguh-sungguh dilahirkan kembali, kita akan memiliki kesaksian dan hasrat yang sama seperti para murid. Kita akan bertumbuh dalam kasih karunia dan pengertian. Kita akan membiarkan Allah menjadi Allah dan Firman-Nya menjadi Kebenaran—akhir dan lengkap! Kita akan berhenti mencoba mereformasi kambing-kambing di antara kita. Sebaliknya kita akan membagikan pesan Injil kepada mereka sehingga mereka dapat menjadi bertobat—mereka kemudian akan menjadi domba dengan hati yang berdenyut daripada hati yang berbalut batu. Kuanggapalah hati yang baru akan Kuberikan kepadamu, dan roh yang baru akan Kutaruhkan di dalam batinmu; dan akan Keluarkan dari tubuhmu hati yang keras dan akan Kuberikan kepadamu hati yang berdenyut. Dan akan Kutaruhkan Roh-Ku di dalam kamu, dan akan membuat kamu hidup menurut ketetapan-Ku, dan kamu akan menaruh dan melakukan penghakiman-Ku –Yehezkiel 36:26-27.

Jadi mengapa kurangnya orang yang benar-benar dilahirkan kembali di antara kita? Saya percaya dunia ini telah memikat kita. Kita mencari kompromi di mana pun kita bisa. Tentu, kita akan berpakaian sedikit berbeda jika perlu, tetapi jangan ambil semua kesenangan dan hiburan kita. Kita memenuhi hidup kita dengan segala yang ditawarkan dunia yang sakit karena dosa ini—uang, hiburan, kemewahan, liburan, makanan, dan minuman, lalu ketika kita berjalan melewati ladang dengan harta yang tersembunyi di dalamnya, kita bahkan tidak memperhatikannya. Itu ada, hanya terlupakan.

Saat kita menyanyikan lagu-lagu Sion dan mendoakan doa-doa permohonan dan pujian, apakah Allah sedang bekerja? Apakah ada sukacita kekal di dalam hati kita atau kita diombang-ambingkan badai kehidupan? Apakah kita sedang berusaha menolong orang buta agar melihat atau kita sedang berusaha menyembunyikan fakta bahwa kita orang Kristen?!

Marilah kita mengakhiri kehidupan Kristen yang kalah ini yang sedikit mengetahui kemenangan. Marilah kita mengakhiri kehidupan yang suam-suam kuku yang diterima oleh banyak orang di sekitar kita! Marilah kita mengakhiri mengasihi dunia jahat ini sekarang juga! Marilah kita mengakhiri individualisme dan keakuan! Marilah kita mengenakan Tuhan Yesus Kristus dan bersama-sama maju berperang melawan musuh jiwa kita. Cukuplah duduk di rumah sambil bernyanyi lagu-lagu; mari kita keluar dan berjuang demi apa yang telah diperjuangkan oleh begitu banyak sebelum kita. Kita membacanya dalam buku sejarah gereja kita. Kita mengambil dorongan dan pengertian dari Alkitab kita dan salinan Martyrs Mirror kita. Tetapi apa yang akan generasi mendatang katakan tentang kita? Akankah ada kesaksian saleh yang ditulis tentang kita?

Alkitab penuh dengan janji-janji:

  • Mintalah, maka akan diberikan kepadamu; carilah, maka kamu akan mendapat; ketoklah, maka pintu akan dibukakan bagimu… –Matius 7:7-8.
  • …Allah … tidak akan membiarkan kamu dicobai melampaui kekuatanmu; tetapi bersama dengan pencobaan Ia akan menyediakan jalan keluar, supaya kamu sanggup menanggungnya –1 Korintus 10:13.
  • …Jika kamu mempunyai iman dan tidak bimbang … kamu akan berkata kepada gunung ini: Beranjaklah dan tercampaklah ke dalam laut! Maka hal itu akan terjadi –Matius 21:21.
  • Demikianlah kataku: Hendaklah kamu hidup oleh Roh, dan kamu tidak akan menuruti hawa nafsu daging –Galatia 5:16.

Dan daftarnya terus berlanjut! Apakah ini menjadi bagian dari hidup kita? Apakah kita hidup dalam kemenangan, atau kita bersembunyi di balik budaya yang gagal tanpa kuasa?

Sahabat-sahabat, Allah menginginkan suatu umat untuk dipanggil milik-Nya hari ini sama seperti pada permulaan. Dia menginginkan kita! Ini adalah pemikiran yang menggugah nurani. Allah ingin membangkitkan kita oleh Roh-Nya, Ia ingin meniupkan nafas-Nya ke dalam kita—Napas Hidup. Ia ingin memberkati kita dengan berkat rohani yang tak terselami!

Namun, manusia lama itu harus mati—kesombongannya, namanya, sikapnya, ketenaran. Manusia lama itu harus memberi jalan bagi yang baru; keduanya tidak dapat hidup bersama dalam tubuh yang sama. Menurut Kitab Suci, itu salah satu atau yang lain. Satu akan mati, dan yang lain akan hidup—selamanya!

Janganlah kita biarkan ular (atau Iblis) menipu kita lagi. Kesenangan hidup ini hanya untuk sesaat. Kita menuai apa yang kita tabur; kita tidak akan luput dari Penghakiman. Allah ingin memberi kita Kerajaan; Ia ingin memberi kita warisan. Ia ingin menjadi seorang Bapa bagi kita, memanggil kita anak-anak-Nya yang terkasih. Ia ingin berjalan bersama kita melalui jalan yang sempit ini. Ia ingin mendorong kita ketika kita terpuruk, dan Ia ingin berjuang bagi kita ketika kita lemah. Ia ingin memberi kita identitas, bagian dari keluarga Allah—anak-anak-Nya. Ia ingin memberi kita kuasa untuk mengatasi segala dosa (bukan hanya beberapa), hari ini dan esok dan sepanjang hidup kita. Ketika kita gagal, Ia ingin memberi kita keinginan untuk bertobat. Lalu ketika kita menerima keinginan itu dan bergerak kembali kepada-Nya, Ia ingin mengampuni kita.

Semakin gelap dunia ini, semakin mudah cahaya harus bersinar. Apakah kita, oleh Roh, menjadi mercusuar yang tegak menghadapi badai? Angin dan gelombang menyerangnya, tetapi ia tak dapat dipindahkan. Cahayanya bersinar melalui masa-masa tergelap, memberi harapan kepada jiwa-jiwa yang lelah yang terdampar dalam hidup. Fondasinya tidak goyah; tujuannya tidak berubah.

Kita dapat memenuhi kepala kita dengan pengetahuan dan mengetahui semua hal yang benar untuk dikatakan dan dilakukan. Namun, jika kita tidak dikehidupkan oleh Roh Allah, kita hanyalah sebuah budaya yang akan berubah tiap generasi. Perubahan ini akan terus berlanjut sampai generasi terakhir benar-benar terbenam dalam lautan dunia ini. Sementara itu, perusak jiwa kita memperoleh lebih banyak bagi dirinya sendiri.

Pertempuran ini nyata—beberapa akan menang, banyak akan kalah. Kekalahan itu besar, lebih besar dari yang dapat saya gambarkan; demikian pula kemenangan.

Orang Kristen abad kedua puluh satu, apa yang akan kamu lakukan?

Greetings to one and all in our dear Saviour’s name, Jesus Christ. Another year has passed from the present into the annals of history. Nothing that we have said or done can be recalled and re-lived. Another year is before us. Many are waiting with bated breath, anticipating what this new year will bring forth.

I read somewhere in the news that those on the frontier of technology believe that this year will be a big year for artificial intelligence. One example given was: they are anticipating that this technology will be able to be a part of events such as board meetings with the ability to hear and understand all that is shared by each one present. Then at the end of the meeting, with the push of a button, the artificial intelligence will produce detailed minutes of that meeting with a fair degree of accuracy. Over the last number of years, many of the things that used to be considered science fiction have recently become reality, so, likely, this will become a new reality as well.

What is this world coming to? To the Bible-literate Christian, the end of time certainly seems to be fast approaching. According to the United Nations, the world’s population surpassed 8 billion on November 15, 2022. Many in the world are desperately trying to figure out how to sustain that many people for the long term. Just like the Bible has prophesied, there is an uptick in the number of famines, drought, floods, earthquakes, wars, and rumors of wars, etc. One thing that I find interesting is that even though the world does not want to retain God in their knowledge, insurance companies still refer to certain specific events as “acts of God”.

As Bible-believing Christians how shall we then live? And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet –Matthew 24:6. Let us remember that we should not be troubled. Rather, we should remember that …he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:13. If we, like Peter, take our eyes off of our Lord and start focusing on the stormy conditions around us we will start to sink as well. Remember, it is …the fearful, and unbelieving … [who] shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone… –Revelation 21:8. But, He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son –Revelation 21:7.

In this issue of the magazine, we again have an interesting group of articles for your consideration. Join us as we learn of a somewhat obscure, yet influential leader of the early Anabaptist movement in Switzerland. Let’s honestly evaluate our own hearts as we follow the expository teaching from Habakkuk regarding what it means to have a real faith that is first personal, then corporate. Together we can consider what it really means to enter into the rest of God that is detailed in Hebrews chapter four. The youth can take a look into their emotions as they consider those times when they feel like giving up. The author for our sisters’ article has tackled a very difficult subject—when and how to be submissive as a godly wife. We have another thought-provoking article in the discipleship series. And the doctor has chosen to venture into some uncharted territory with the first of a two-part series on cancer.

A final thought I wish to share, a story in fact… Recently, I heard a first-hand account of a man who was lost before God, how he came to spiritual awakening, and how this started affecting his life. This story caused me to stop and consider where I am as a Christian. Is my relationship with my Lord vibrant? How strong is my commitment towards God and His Word? Is my love for my Lord and Saviour still as real and as strong as it was when I first had my awakening and was converted? I’m sure there are more questions that we could ask ourselves in light of this real-life story. I’ll let you as a reader start compiling your own list. Now for the story…

This man is living somewhere within the United States of America. He is a married man with a young family. He is part of a certain religious group within the plain people—those of Anabaptist heritage. Throughout his lifetime he had endeavored to live his life according to the mandates set forth by the leaders of his local church. Yet, for some reason, he had not been finding answers to his personal need, whatever that was—perhaps even he didn’t know.

This man and some of his family were traveling and ended up lodging overnight in a motel. There, in the nightstand drawer he discovered a book titled “The Holy Bible”. Sure, in his church the Bible was read or quoted each week during their normal worship services. Although this man understood English quite well, his church had a policy that they did not want to be too worldly or too modern by reading from an English Bible so they continued their efforts of teaching God’s Word using the original language of their people.

The problem was that this man, somehow, never developed an understanding of that language, thus he never heard the truth of God’s Word. All that he heard was what 1 Corinthians chapter 14 refers to as tongues (languages) and since he didn’t understand the language and since there was no interpretation given, he was not able to be edified. The purpose of this story is not to find fault or to place blame, but rather to bring light to an obvious problem among some of the plain people. A problem for which God would surely desire to see changes made for the betterment of those seeking Him in such settings.

With this in mind, we now come back to this man—a man zealous in his religious life—yet having NEVER heard the message of the Gospel of Jesus Christ. As he hesitantly picked up this English Bible he cautiously started to read the message contained within those book covers. As he read, he became more and more excited. Here were things that he had never heard before—teachings that brought sense to his many questions and the emptiness that he felt within his soul. He was so engrossed that he almost couldn’t pull himself away to allow time for sleep. After a short night, they went on with their travels.

Completing their business they returned home, but life would never be the same for that man. Something had been awakened deep within his soul. Questions had been answered. Longings had been met. Peace had begun to settle over his troubled heart. At long last, he had found the answer, but his time of reading had been so short. Surely there was more to learn, much more. So, before too much time had elapsed, he once more scheduled a trip to get away from his local area and to once more provide a reason to spend another night in a motel with a Bible in the nightstand drawer. He eagerly anticipated another night alone with God and His Word. After a second sleepless night spent devouring the teachings of the Scriptures, he started seeking others who understood and practiced what the Bible said. He was desiring to fellowship and learn all that he could from those who understood God’s Word and who practiced what they preached.

As this man has endeavored to find his way through this confusing maze of religious idiosyncrasies he finally purchased a German/English Bible. He felt driven in his continued pursuit of the Truth, yet he was afraid to be found out by his local church leaders. He wanted to stay within his local church, yet his conscience demanded that he must continue his search. For some reason he believed that his local church leaders would not be understanding in his quest for truth and that maybe he would be placed under church discipline for his actions.

His local church is a part of the descendants of the Anabaptists who were persecuted for their faith, including their desire to understand, and read the Scriptures in their native tongue—Swiss or German, instead of Latin as was required by the church leaders of their day. Yet here he is, some 500 years later, in America, possibly facing persecution from his own church which claims to be a part of the “right” church of God. Herein, his church leaders are finding themselves on the opposite side of the issue of freedom of religious worship that their forefathers suffered for, since they are insisting that the only way to learn of God’s will is through the official language of Scripture—German. This is NO different than the struggle of the original Anabaptists who were persecuted for not studying the Scriptures in the official language of their day—Latin.

Let’s remember, IF church members do not understand the teachings of God’s Word due to their church leaders’ stubborn insistence that the church members are NOT allowed to read or hear the Scriptures in the language that they understand, then the ignorance of the common man WILL be laid at the feet of those leaders come judgment day. Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account… –Hebrews 13:17. Obey here is only in the context of God’s Word, not just according to church leaders’ personal ideas or whims. For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad –2 Corinthians 5:10. Every person will receive personal judgment based on what the Bible teaches NOT according to a church’s detailed dogma.

When I think of the zealous efforts of this man I think of the verse of Scripture… When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel –Matthew 8:10. I also observe the current trends of some of our plain publishing houses—they have borrowed from the world’s idea (in a spiritual way, of course) that to sell books and reading material they need to print exhilarating stories, ones that keep people on the edge of their seats—all this because today’s Christian has become bored with that which seems old-fashioned.

What a difference between this story and many of today’s Anabaptist descendants. Many of today’s conservative Anabaptist people have a difficult time getting excited about the Bible. They are too over-stimulated by the lack of rest and quiet in their normal daily lives.

Usually, we hear of stories like this from the jungles of Central America, the deserts of Africa, or the slums of India. What I am amazed about is that this story takes place right in the midst of one of our plain groups of conservative Anabaptists. Let’s seek God for opportunities to share the truth of the Gospel message with those within the sphere of our influence. We might be surprised how many people we rub shoulders with during our daily lives who would be just as hungry for the Truth as the man in our story.

خلاصہ نجات دہندہ ییسوع مسیح کے نام میں تمام حضرات کو سلام۔ ایک اور سال ماضی کی کتابِ تاریخ میں شامل ہو گیا۔ جو کچھ ہم نے کہا یا کیا ہے وہ واپس نہیں لایا جا سکتا اور دوبارہ زندہ نہیں کیا جا سکتا۔ ایک اور سال ہمارے سامنے ہے۔ کئی لوگ بے صبری سے انتظار کر رہے ہیں کہ یہ نیا سال کیا لا رہا ہے۔

میں نے کہیں خبر میں پڑھا کہ ٹیکنالوجی کے محاذ پر کام کرنے والے لوگ سمجھتے ہیں کہ اس سال مصنوعی ذہانت کے لیے بڑا سال ہوگا۔ ایک مثال یہ دی گئی تھی کہ وہ توقع کرتے ہیں کہ یہ ٹیکنالوجی ایسی تقریبات کا حصہ بن سکے گی جیسے بورڈ میٹنگز، جس میں وہ بیٹھے ہر شخص کی بات سن سکے گی اور سمجھ سکے گی۔ پھر میٹنگ کے اختتام پر ایک بٹن دباتے ہی مصنوعی ذہانت اس میٹنگ کے تفصیلی منٹس کافی حد تک درستگی کے ساتھ تیار کر دے گی۔ پچھلے چند سالوں میں وہ بہت سی چیزیں جو پہلے سائنسی فکشن سمجھی جاتی تھیں حال ہی میں حقیقت بن گئی ہیں، لہٰذا ممکن ہے یہ بھی جلد ہی حقیقت بن جائے۔

یہ دنیا کس طرف جا رہی ہے؟ بائبل سے واقف مسیحی کے لیے بلاشبہ وقتِ انجام قریب معلوم ہوتا ہے۔ اقوام متحدہ کے مطابق دنیا کی آبادی 15 نومبر 2022 کو 8 ارب سے زائد ہو گئی۔ دنیا کے بہت سے لوگ مایوسی میں یہ تلاش کر رہے ہیں کہ اس تعداد کو طویل مدت تک کس طرح برقرار رکھا جائے۔ جیسا کہ بائبل نے پیشگوئی کی ہے، قحط، خشک سالی، سیلاب، زلزلے، جنگیں اور جنگوں کی افواہیں وغیرہ میں اضافہ ہوا ہے۔ ایک دلچسپ بات یہ ہے کہ اگرچہ دنیا خدا کو اپنے علم میں رکھنا نہیں چاہتی، پھر بھی بیمہ کمپنیاں مخصوص واقعات کو "خدا کے اعمال" کے طور پر یاد کرتی ہیں۔

ہم بائبل-باور مسیحیوں کے طور پر پھر کیسے جئیں؟ اور تم جنگوں اور جنگوں کی افواہوں کو سنو گے: توجہ رکھو کہ تم پر کوئی گھبراہٹ نہ آئے: کیونکہ یہ سب چیزیں ہوں گی، مگر آخر وقت ابھی نہیں آیا—متی 24:6۔ یاد رکھیں کہ ہمیں گھبراہٹ نہیں کرنی چاہئے۔ بلکہ ہمیں یہ یاد رکھنا چاہئے کہ …جو آخر تک ثابت رہے گا، وہی نجات پائے گا—متی 24:13۔ اگر ہم بھی پیطرس کی طرح اپنے رب سے نظر ہٹا کر اپنے اردگرد کے طوفانی حالات پر دھیان دیں تو ہم بھی ڈوبنا شروع کر دیں گے۔ یاد رکھو، …ڈرپوک اور بے ایمان … [جن کا] حصہ وہی ہوگا جو آگ اور گندھک کی جھیل میں جلا کرتا ہے…—مکاشفہ 21:8۔ مگر جو غالب آئے گا وہ سب کچھ وارث پائے گا؛ اور میں اُس کا خدا ہوں گا، اور وہ میرا بیٹا ہوگا—مکاشفہ 21:7۔

اس رسالے کے اس شمارے میں، آپ کے غور و فکر کے لیے پھر کچھ دلچسپ مضامین موجود ہیں۔ ہمارے ساتھ شامل ہوں جب ہم سوئٹزرلینڈ میں اوائل انا بپٹسٹ تحریک کے ایک نسبتاً کم معروف مگر بااثر رہنما کے بارے میں جانیں گے۔ ہبقوق کی تشریحی تعلیم سے ہم ایمانداری کے ساتھ اپنے دلوں کا جائزہ لیں کہ حقیقی ایمان کا مطلب سب سے پہلے ذاتی اور پھر اجتماعی طور پر کیا ہے۔ مل کر ہم یہ غور کر سکتے ہیں کہ عبرانیوں کے چوتھے باب میں مفصل خدا کی راحت میں داخل ہونے کا کیا مطلب ہے۔ نوجوان اپنے جذبات پر نظر ڈال سکتے ہیں جب وہ ایسے اوقات پر غور کریں جب انہیں ہار ماننے جیسا محسوس ہوتا ہے۔ بہنوں کے لیے مصنف نے ایک نہایت مشکل موضوع سنبھالا ہے—ایک نیک عورت کے طور پر متواضع کب اور کیسے ہونا چاہیے۔ ہمارے شاگردی سلسلے میں ایک اور سوچ کے لیے مجبور کرنے والا مضمون ہے۔ اور ڈاکٹر نے کینسر پر دو حصوں پر مشتمل سلسلے کے پہلے حصے کے ساتھ کچھ انجان زمینوں میں قدم رکھنے کا انتخاب کیا ہے۔

ایک آخری سوچ جو میں شیئر کرنا چاہتا ہوں، اصل میں ایک کہانی… حال ہی میں میں نے ایک ایسے آدمی کا کرداراً براہِ راست بیان سنا جو خدا کے حضور گمراہ تھا، کیسے اسے روحانی بیداری ملی، اور اس نے اپنی زندگی میں کیسے اثر ڈالنا شروع کیا۔ اس کہانی نے مجھے توقف پر مجبور کیا اور سوچنے پر کہ میں ایک مسیحی کے طور پر کہاں کھڑا ہوں۔ کیا میرا رب کے ساتھ تعلق زندہ ہے؟ میری خدا اور اُس کے کلام کے تئیں وابستگی کتنی مضبوط ہے؟ کیا میری اپنے رب اور نجات دہندہ کے لیے محبت وہی حقیقی اور مضبوط ہے جو میری پہلی بیداری اور تبدیل ہونے کے وقت تھی؟ مجھے یقین ہے کہ اس حقیقی زندگی کی کہانی کے پیشِ نظر ہم اپنے آپ سے اور بھی سوالات پوچھ سکتے ہیں۔ میں آپ کو بطور قاری اپنی فہرست مرتب کرنے کی دعوت دیتا ہوں۔ اب کہانی سنتے ہیں…

یہ آدمی ریاستِ متحدۂ امریکہ کے کسی مقام پر رہتا ہے۔ وہ شادی شدہ ہے اور اس کا ایک ننھا خاندان ہے۔ وہ سادہ لوگوں کے اندر ایک مخصوص مذہبی گروپ کا حصہ ہے—انا بپٹسٹ نسب کا۔ اپنی پوری زندگی میں اس نے اپنی مقامی جماعت کے رہنماؤں کے مقرر کردہ احکامات کے مطابق جینے کی کوشش کی۔ پھر بھی، کسی وجہ سے، وہ اپنی ذاتی ضرورت کا حل نہیں پا رہا تھا، جو بھی وہ تھا—شاید وہ خود بھی جانتا نہ تھا۔

یہ آدمی اور اس کے خاندان کے چند افراد سفر کر رہے تھے اور ایک موٹل میں رات گزارنے کے لیے ٹھہرے۔ وہاں، نائٹ اسٹینڈ کے دراز میں اسے ایک کتاب ملی جس کا عنوان تھا "مقدس بائبل"۔ یقینأ، اس کے چرچ میں بائبل ان کے معمول کے عبادتی اجتماعات کے دوران ہر ہفتے پڑھی یا حوالہ دی جاتی تھی۔ اگرچہ یہ آدمی انگریزی اچھی طرح سمجھتا تھا، اس کے چرچ کی پالیسی یہ تھی کہ وہ بہت دنیا دار یا جدید نہ لگیں اس لیے انگریزی بائبل پڑھنے سے باز رہتے اور اپنے لوگوں کی اصل زبان میں خدا کے کلام کی تعلیم دینے کی کوشش جاری رکھتے۔

مسئلہ یہ تھا کہ یہ آدمی کسی طرح اس زبان کو سمجھنے میں کبھی ماہر نہیں ہوا، اس طرح اس نے خدا کے کلام کی حقیقت کبھی سنی ہی نہیں۔ جو کچھ وہ سنتا تھا وہ 1 کرنتھیوں باب 14 میں جسے زبانیں (لسانیات) کہا گیا ہے، ویسا ہی تھا اور چونکہ وہ زبان نہیں سمجھتا تھا اور نہ ہی کسی تفسیر کا اہتمام ہوتا تھا، وہ تعلیم اور دل کی تعمیر سے محروم رہتا تھا۔ اس کہانی کا مقصد قصور تلاش کرنا یا الزام تراشی کرنا نہیں ہے، بلکہ کچھ سادہ لوگوں میں ایک واضح مسئلے کو اجاگر کرنا ہے۔ ایک ایسا مسئلہ جس کے لیے خدا یقینی طور پر بہتری کے لیے تبدیلیاں دیکھنا چاہے گا تاکہ ایسے ماحول میں خدا کی تلاش کرنے والوں کی بھلائی ہو سکے۔

اس بات کے ساتھ ہم اس آدمی کی طرف لوٹتے ہیں—ایک مذہبی جوش و خروش والا آدمی—پھر بھی یسوع مسیح کے انجیل کا پیغام کبھی سننے والا بالکل نہیں۔ جب اس نے ہچکچاتے ہوئے یہ انگریزی بائبل اٹھائی تو اس نے احتیاط سے ان کتابوں میں موجود پیغام کو پڑھنا شروع کیا۔ پڑھتے جانے پر وہ اور زیادہ پرجوش ہو گیا۔ یہاں ایسی باتیں تھیں جو اس نے کبھی نہیں سنی تھیں—تعلیمات جو اس کے بے شمار سوالات اور اس کی روح کی خالی پن کو معنی دیتی تھیں۔ وہ اتنا محو تھا کہ تقریباً خود کو نیند کے لیے الگ نہیں کر پارہا تھا۔ مختصر رات کے بعد وہ اپنے سفر پر روانہ ہوئے۔

اپنا کام مکمل کر کے وہ گھر واپس آئے، مگر اس آدمی کے لیے زندگی کبھی وہ سابقہ نہ رہی۔ اس کی روح کے اندر گہری بیداری پیدا ہو چکی تھی۔ سوالات کے جواب مل گئے۔ تمنائیں پوری ہوئیں۔ اس کے مضطرب دل پر سکون چھانے لگا۔ آخر کار، اس نے جواب پا لیا، مگر اس کا پڑھنے کا وقت بہت کم تھا۔ بے شک سیکھنے کے لیے اور بہت کچھ تھا۔ لہٰذا، زیادہ دیر گزرنے سے پہلے اس نے ایک اور سفر کا پروگرام بنایا تاکہ اپنے مقامی علاقے سے دور رہ کر ایک اور رات موٹل میں گزارے جہاں نائٹ اسٹینڈ کے دراز میں بائبل ملے۔ وہ خدا اور اس کے کلام کے ساتھ ایک اور رات کے لیے بے تاب تھا۔ دوسری بے خوابی کی رات میں صحیفوں کی تعلیمات کو کھا کھا کر پڑھنے کے بعد وہ دوسروں کی تلاش کرنے لگا جو سمجھتے اور اس بات پر عمل کرتے تھے جو بائبل کہتی تھی۔ وہ اُن لوگوں کے ساتھ اجتماع اور علم حاصل کرنے کا متمنی تھا جو خدا کے کلام کو سمجھتے اور جو جو کچھ وہ زندہ کرتے تھے اس پر عمل پیرا تھے۔

جب یہ آدمی مذہبی انفرادیتوں کے اس الجھے ہوئے بھول بھلیاں میں اپنا راستہ تلاش کرنے کی کوشش کر رہا تھا تو آخر کار اس نے ایک جرمن/انگریزی بائبل خرید لی۔ وہ سچ کی تلاش میں مسلسل محروم محسوس کرتا تھا، پھر بھی وہ اپنے مقامی چرچ کے سربراہان سے پکڑے جانے کے خوف میں گھبرا رہا تھا۔ وہ اپنی مقامی جماعت میں رہنا چاہتا تھا، مگر اس کا ضمیر اسے طلب کرتا تھا کہ وہ اپنی تلاش جاری رکھے۔ کسی وجہ سے وہ مانتا تھا کہ اس کے مقامی چرچ کے رہنما اس کی سچائی کی تلاش میں سمجھدار نہیں ہوں گے اور شاید اس کے اعمال کے سبب اسے چرچ کی تادیب کا سامنا کرنا پڑے گا۔

اس کا مقامی چرچ انا بپٹسٹس کے نسلوں کا حصہ ہے جنہیں اپنے ایمان کی وجہ سے ظلم و ستم سہنا پڑا، جن میں اُن کا یہ خواہش بھی شامل تھی کہ وہ صحیفوں کو اپنی مادری زبان—سوئس یا جرمن—میں سمجھیں اور پڑھیں، بجائے لاطینی کے جو اُن کے دن کے چرچ کے رہنماؤں کی مانگ تھی۔ پھر بھی وہ یہاں ہیں، تقریباً پانچ سو سال بعد، امریکہ میں، ممکنہ طور پر اپنے ہی چرچ کی طرف سے ظلم و ستم کا سامنا کرتے ہوئے جو خود کو خدا کے "صحیح" چرچ کا حصہ کہتا ہے۔ یہاں اُن کے چرچ کے رہنما خود اپنے بُزرگوں کی جدوجہدِ مذہبی عبادت کی آزادی کے برعکس کھڑے دکھائی دیتے ہیں جنہوں نے اپنی نسلوں کے لیے جدوجہد کی، کیونکہ وہ اِصرار کرتے ہیں کہ خدا کی مرضی کو جاننے کا واحد طریقہ صحیفوں کی سرکاری زبان—جرمن—کے ذریعے ہے۔ یہ کوئی مختلف صورت نہیں ہے اُن اصل انا بپٹسٹس کی جدوجہد سے جنہیں اُن کے دور کی سرکاری زبان—لاطینی—میں صحیفے نہ پڑھنے پر ستایا گیا تھا۔

یاد رکھیں، اگر چرچ کے اراکین چرچ کے رہنماؤں کی ضد کی وجہ سے وہ کلامِ خدا کی تعلیمات نہیں سمجھتے کیونکہ انہیں اپنی سمجھ کی زبان میں صحیفہ پڑھنے یا سننے کی اجازت نہیں دی جاتی، تو عام آدمی کی جہالت اُن رہنماؤں کے سر رکھ دی جائے گی قیامت کے دن۔ ان لوگوں کی اطاعت کرو جو تم پر حکم کرتے ہیں، اور ان کے تابع ہو جاؤ: کیونکہ وہ تمہاری جانوں کے لیے نگہبان ہیں، ایسے جو محاسبہ کرنا پڑے گا…—عبرانیوں 13:17۔ اطاعت یہاں صرف خدا کے کلام کے تناظر میں ہے، نہ کہ صرف چرچ کے رہنماؤں کے ذاتی خیالات یا خواہشات کے مطابق۔ کیونکہ ہم سب کو مسیح کی عدالت کے سامنے ظاہر ہونا ہے؛ تاکہ ہر ایک اپنے اعمال کے مطابق جو کچھ اس نے اپنے بدن میں کیا وہ لے، چاہے وہ اچھا ہو یا براء—2 کرنتھیوں 5:10۔ ہر شخص کو ذاتی حساب ملے گا جو بائبل کیا سکھاتی ہے اس کی بنیاد پر، نہ کہ کسی چرچ کے مفصل عقائد کے مطابق۔

جب میں اس آدمی کی جوشیلے کوششوں کے بارے میں سوچتا ہوں تو میں وہ آیت یاد کرتا ہوں… جب یسوع نے یہ سنا تو وہ متحیّر ہوا، اور اُن سے جو پیچھے تھے اُن سے کہا، میں تم سے سچ کہتا ہوں، نہ تو اسرائیل میں اتنا بڑا ایمان ملا—متی 8:10۔ میں ہمارے کچھ سادہ پبلشنگ ہاؤسز کے موجودہ رجحانات کا بھی مشاہدہ کرتا ہوں—انہوں نے دنیا کے خیال سے مستعار لیا ہے (روحانی معنوں میں، بطورِ ضابطہ) کہ کتابیں اور مطالعہ شدہ مواد بیچنے کے لیے انہیں ایسی دلکش کہانیاں چھاپنی چاہئیں جو لوگوں کو کرسی کے کنارے لا کھڑی کریں—یہ سب اس لیے کہ آج کا مسیحی ان چیزوں سے اکتا گیا ہے جو پرانی فیشن معلوم ہوتی ہیں۔

اس کہانی اور آج کے بہت سے انا بپٹسٹ اولاد کے درمیان کیا فرق ہے۔ آج کے بہت سے قدامت پسند انا بپٹسٹ لوگوں کو بائبل کے بارے میں پرجوش ہونا مشکل لگتا ہے۔ وہ اپنے روزمرہ کے معمول میں آرام اور خاموشی کی کمی سے حد درجہ پریشان ہیں۔

عموماً ہم ایسی کہانیاں وسطی امریکہ کے جنگلات، افریقہ کے صحرا یا بھارت کے جھگڑوں سے سنتے ہیں۔ مجھے حیرت ہے کہ یہ کہانی ہمارے قدامت پسند انا بپٹسٹسٹ گروپوں میں سے ایک کے بیچ ہی رونما ہوئی۔ آئیں ہم خدا سے مواقع مانگیں تاکہ ہم اپنے اثر کے دائرے میں موجود لوگوں کے ساتھ انجیل کے پیغام کی سچائی بانٹ سکیں۔ ہمیں حیرانی ہو سکتی ہے کہ ہم روزمرہ کی زندگی میں کتنے لوگوں کے قریب گزرتے ہیں جو اس کہانی کے آدمی کی طرح سچ کی بھوک رکھ سکتے ہیں۔
