Greetings to one and all in our dear Saviour’s name, Jesus Christ. Another year has passed from the present into the annals of history. Nothing that we have said or done can be recalled and re-lived. Another year is before us. Many are waiting with bated breath, anticipating what this new year will bring forth.

I read somewhere in the news that those on the frontier of technology believe that this year will be a big year for artificial intelligence. One example given was: they are anticipating that this technology will be able to be a part of events such as board meetings with the ability to hear and understand all that is shared by each one present. Then at the end of the meeting, with the push of a button, the artificial intelligence will produce detailed minutes of that meeting with a fair degree of accuracy. Over the last number of years, many of the things that used to be considered science fiction have recently become reality, so, likely, this will become a new reality as well.

What is this world coming to? To the Bible-literate Christian, the end of time certainly seems to be fast approaching. According to the United Nations, the world’s population surpassed 8 billion on November 15, 2022. Many in the world are desperately trying to figure out how to sustain that many people for the long term. Just like the Bible has prophesied, there is an uptick in the number of famines, drought, floods, earthquakes, wars, and rumors of wars, etc. One thing that I find interesting is that even though the world does not want to retain God in their knowledge, insurance companies still refer to certain specific events as “acts of God”.

As Bible-believing Christians how shall we then live? And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet –Matthew 24:6. Let us remember that we should not be troubled. Rather, we should remember that …he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:13. If we, like Peter, take our eyes off of our Lord and start focusing on the stormy conditions around us we will start to sink as well. Remember, it is …the fearful, and unbelieving … [who] shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone… –Revelation 21:8. But, He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son –Revelation 21:7.

In this issue of the magazine, we again have an interesting group of articles for your consideration. Join us as we learn of a somewhat obscure, yet influential leader of the early Anabaptist movement in Switzerland. Let’s honestly evaluate our own hearts as we follow the expository teaching from Habakkuk regarding what it means to have a real faith that is first personal, then corporate. Together we can consider what it really means to enter into the rest of God that is detailed in Hebrews chapter four. The youth can take a look into their emotions as they consider those times when they feel like giving up. The author for our sisters’ article has tackled a very difficult subject—when and how to be submissive as a godly wife. We have another thought-provoking article in the discipleship series. And the doctor has chosen to venture into some uncharted territory with the first of a two-part series on cancer.

A final thought I wish to share, a story in fact… Recently, I heard a first-hand account of a man who was lost before God, how he came to spiritual awakening, and how this started affecting his life. This story caused me to stop and consider where I am as a Christian. Is my relationship with my Lord vibrant? How strong is my commitment towards God and His Word? Is my love for my Lord and Saviour still as real and as strong as it was when I first had my awakening and was converted? I’m sure there are more questions that we could ask ourselves in light of this real-life story. I’ll let you as a reader start compiling your own list. Now for the story…

This man is living somewhere within the United States of America. He is a married man with a young family. He is part of a certain religious group within the plain people—those of Anabaptist heritage. Throughout his lifetime he had endeavored to live his life according to the mandates set forth by the leaders of his local church. Yet, for some reason, he had not been finding answers to his personal need, whatever that was—perhaps even he didn’t know.

This man and some of his family were traveling and ended up lodging overnight in a motel. There, in the nightstand drawer he discovered a book titled “The Holy Bible”. Sure, in his church the Bible was read or quoted each week during their normal worship services. Although this man understood English quite well, his church had a policy that they did not want to be too worldly or too modern by reading from an English Bible so they continued their efforts of teaching God’s Word using the original language of their people.

The problem was that this man, somehow, never developed an understanding of that language, thus he never heard the truth of God’s Word. All that he heard was what 1 Corinthians chapter 14 refers to as tongues (languages) and since he didn’t understand the language and since there was no interpretation given, he was not able to be edified. The purpose of this story is not to find fault or to place blame, but rather to bring light to an obvious problem among some of the plain people. A problem for which God would surely desire to see changes made for the betterment of those seeking Him in such settings.

With this in mind, we now come back to this man—a man zealous in his religious life—yet having NEVER heard the message of the Gospel of Jesus Christ. As he hesitantly picked up this English Bible he cautiously started to read the message contained within those book covers. As he read, he became more and more excited. Here were things that he had never heard before—teachings that brought sense to his many questions and the emptiness that he felt within his soul. He was so engrossed that he almost couldn’t pull himself away to allow time for sleep. After a short night, they went on with their travels.

Completing their business they returned home, but life would never be the same for that man. Something had been awakened deep within his soul. Questions had been answered. Longings had been met. Peace had begun to settle over his troubled heart. At long last, he had found the answer, but his time of reading had been so short. Surely there was more to learn, much more. So, before too much time had elapsed, he once more scheduled a trip to get away from his local area and to once more provide a reason to spend another night in a motel with a Bible in the nightstand drawer. He eagerly anticipated another night alone with God and His Word. After a second sleepless night spent devouring the teachings of the Scriptures, he started seeking others who understood and practiced what the Bible said. He was desiring to fellowship and learn all that he could from those who understood God’s Word and who practiced what they preached.

As this man has endeavored to find his way through this confusing maze of religious idiosyncrasies he finally purchased a German/English Bible. He felt driven in his continued pursuit of the Truth, yet he was afraid to be found out by his local church leaders. He wanted to stay within his local church, yet his conscience demanded that he must continue his search. For some reason he believed that his local church leaders would not be understanding in his quest for truth and that maybe he would be placed under church discipline for his actions.

His local church is a part of the descendants of the Anabaptists who were persecuted for their faith, including their desire to understand, and read the Scriptures in their native tongue—Swiss or German, instead of Latin as was required by the church leaders of their day. Yet here he is, some 500 years later, in America, possibly facing persecution from his own church which claims to be a part of the “right” church of God. Herein, his church leaders are finding themselves on the opposite side of the issue of freedom of religious worship that their forefathers suffered for, since they are insisting that the only way to learn of God’s will is through the official language of Scripture—German. This is NO different than the struggle of the original Anabaptists who were persecuted for not studying the Scriptures in the official language of their day—Latin.

Let’s remember, IF church members do not understand the teachings of God’s Word due to their church leaders’ stubborn insistence that the church members are NOT allowed to read or hear the Scriptures in the language that they understand, then the ignorance of the common man WILL be laid at the feet of those leaders come judgment day. Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account… –Hebrews 13:17. Obey here is only in the context of God’s Word, not just according to church leaders’ personal ideas or whims. For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad –2 Corinthians 5:10. Every person will receive personal judgment based on what the Bible teaches NOT according to a church’s detailed dogma.

When I think of the zealous efforts of this man I think of the verse of Scripture… When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel –Matthew 8:10. I also observe the current trends of some of our plain publishing houses—they have borrowed from the world’s idea (in a spiritual way, of course) that to sell books and reading material they need to print exhilarating stories, ones that keep people on the edge of their seats—all this because today’s Christian has become bored with that which seems old-fashioned.

What a difference between this story and many of today’s Anabaptist descendants. Many of today’s conservative Anabaptist people have a difficult time getting excited about the Bible. They are too over-stimulated by the lack of rest and quiet in their normal daily lives.

Usually, we hear of stories like this from the jungles of Central America, the deserts of Africa, or the slums of India. What I am amazed about is that this story takes place right in the midst of one of our plain groups of conservative Anabaptists. Let’s seek God for opportunities to share the truth of the Gospel message with those within the sphere of our influence. We might be surprised how many people we rub shoulders with during our daily lives who would be just as hungry for the Truth as the man in our story.

Saluti a tutti nel nome del nostro caro Salvatore, Gesù Cristo. Un altro anno è passato dall’attualità negli annali della storia. Nulla di ciò che abbiamo detto o fatto può essere richiamato e rivissuto. Davanti a noi c’è un altro anno. Molti attendono con il fiato sospeso, anticipando ciò che porterà questo nuovo anno.

Ho letto da qualche parte nelle notizie che coloro che sono in prima linea nella tecnologia ritengono che quest’anno sarà un anno importante per l’intelligenza artificiale. Un esempio citato era: si prevede che questa tecnologia sarà in grado di partecipare a eventi come riunioni del consiglio con la capacità di ascoltare e comprendere tutto ciò che viene detto da ciascuno dei presenti. Poi, alla fine della riunione, con la pressione di un pulsante, l’intelligenza artificiale produrrà verbali dettagliati di quella riunione con un discreto grado di accuratezza. Negli ultimi anni, molte delle cose che una volta erano considerate fantascienza sono recentemente diventate realtà, quindi è probabile che anche questo diventerà una nuova realtà.

Dove sta andando questo mondo? Per il cristiano istruito nella Bibbia, la fine dei tempi certamente sembra avvicinarsi rapidamente. Secondo le Nazioni Unite, la popolazione mondiale ha superato gli 8 miliardi il 15 novembre 2022. Molti nel mondo cercano disperatamente di capire come sostenere così tante persone a lungo termine. Come ha profetizzato la Bibbia, c’è un aumento del numero di carestie, siccità, alluvioni, terremoti, guerre e voci di guerre, ecc. Una cosa che trovo interessante è che, anche se il mondo non vuole trattenere Dio nella loro conoscenza, le compagnie di assicurazione continuano a riferirsi ad alcuni eventi specifici come “atti di Dio”.

Come dovremmo vivere, dunque, noi cristiani che crediamo nella Bibbia? E udrete di guerre e di rumori di guerre: guardate che non vi turbiate: poiché tutte queste cose devono avvenire, ma la fine non è ancora–Matteo 24:6. Ricordiamo che non dobbiamo essere turbati. Piuttosto, dobbiamo ricordare che …chi avrà perseverato fino alla fine, costui sarà salvato–Matteo 24:13. Se noi, come Pietro, distogliamo gli occhi dal nostro Signore e iniziamo a concentrarci sulle condizioni tempestose intorno a noi, inizieremo anche noi ad affondare. Ricordate, sono …i timorosi, gli increduli … [che] avranno la loro parte nel lago che arde di fuoco e zolfo…–Apocalisse 21:8. Ma, Colui che vince erediterà tutte le cose; ed io sarò il suo Dio ed egli sarà il mio figlio–Apocalisse 21:7.

In questo numero della rivista, abbiamo di nuovo un gruppo interessante di articoli per la vostra considerazione. Unitevi a noi mentre conosciamo un leader alquanto oscuro, ma influente, del primo movimento anabattista in Svizzera. Valutiamo onestamente i nostri cuori seguendo l’insegnamento espositivo di Abacuc su ciò che significa avere una fede vera che è prima personale, poi corporativa. Insieme possiamo considerare cosa significhi realmente entrare nel riposo di Dio descritto in dettaglio in Ebrei capitolo quattro. I giovani possono esaminare le proprie emozioni mentre considerano quei momenti in cui sentono di voler rinunciare. L’autrice dell’articolo per le nostre sorelle ha affrontato un tema molto difficile—quando e come essere sottomesse come mogli pie. Abbiamo un altro articolo che stimola la riflessione nella serie sul discepolato. E il dottore ha scelto di avventurarsi in un territorio inesplorato con la prima parte di una serie in due puntate sul cancro.

Un ultimo pensiero che desidero condividere, una storia in effetti… Recentemente ho ascoltato la testimonianza diretta di un uomo che era perduto davanti a Dio, di come giunse al risveglio spirituale, e di come questo iniziò a influenzare la sua vita. Questa storia mi ha fatto fermare e considerare dove mi trovo come cristiano. La mia relazione con il Signore è vibrante? Quanto è forte il mio impegno verso Dio e la Sua Parola? Il mio amore per il mio Signore e Salvatore è ancora reale e forte come lo era quando ho avuto il mio primo risveglio e mi sono convertito? Sono certo che ci sono altre domande che potremmo porci alla luce di questa storia di vita reale. Vi lascio come lettore a compilare la vostra lista. Ora la storia…

Quest’uomo vive da qualche parte negli Stati Uniti d’America. È un uomo sposato con una famiglia giovane. Fa parte di un certo gruppo religioso all’interno dei plain—quelli di eredità anabattista. Per tutta la sua vita si era sforzato di vivere secondo i dettami stabiliti dai leader della sua chiesa locale. Eppure, per qualche ragione, non aveva trovato risposte al suo bisogno personale, qualunque esso fosse—forse neanche lui lo sapeva.

Quest’uomo e parte della sua famiglia stavano viaggiando e finirono per alloggiare per la notte in un motel. Lì, nel cassetto del comodino, scoprì un libro intitolato “La Sacra Bibbia”. Certo, nella sua chiesa la Bibbia veniva letta o citata ogni settimana durante i loro servizi di culto normali. Sebbene quest’uomo comprendesse abbastanza bene l’inglese, la sua chiesa aveva una politica per cui non voleva essere troppo mondana o troppo moderna leggendo da una Bibbia in inglese, così continuarono i loro sforzi di insegnare la Parola di Dio usando la lingua originale del loro popolo.

Il problema era che quest’uomo, in qualche modo, non aveva mai sviluppato una comprensione di quella lingua, così non aveva mai udito la verità della Parola di Dio. Tutto ciò che aveva sentito era ciò a cui 1 Corinzi capitolo 14 si riferisce come lingue e poiché non capiva la lingua e non veniva data alcuna interpretazione, non poteva essere edificato. Lo scopo di questa storia non è trovare colpe o addossare responsabilità, ma piuttosto portare alla luce un problema evidente tra alcuni dei plain. Un problema per il quale Dio certamente desidererebbe vedere dei cambiamenti per il miglioramento di coloro che lo cercano in tali contesti.

Con questo in mente, torniamo ora a quest’uomo—un uomo zelante nella sua vita religiosa—eppure che NON aveva MAI udito il messaggio del Vangelo di Gesù Cristo. Mentre prendeva con esitazione questa Bibbia in inglese, cominciò cautamente a leggere il messaggio contenuto in quelle copertine. Man mano che leggeva, diventava sempre più eccitato. Qui c’erano cose che non aveva mai udito prima—insegnamenti che davano senso alle sue molte domande e al vuoto che avvertiva nell’anima. Era così preso che quasi non riusciva a staccarsi per permettere al sonno di arrivare. Dopo una breve notte, ripresero il viaggio.

Completati gli affari tornarono a casa, ma la vita per quell’uomo non sarebbe mai più stata la stessa. Qualcosa era stato risvegliato in profondità nella sua anima. Le domande avevano ricevuto risposta. I desideri erano stati soddisfatti. La pace aveva cominciato a posarsi sul suo cuore turbato. Finalmente aveva trovato la risposta, ma il suo tempo di lettura era stato così breve. Sicuramente c’era molto altro da imparare. Così, prima che passasse troppo tempo, organizzò di nuovo un viaggio per allontanarsi dalla sua zona locale e per avere un motivo per trascorrere un’altra notte in un motel con una Bibbia nel cassetto del comodino. Attendeva con impazienza un’altra notte da solo con Dio e la Sua Parola. Dopo una seconda notte insonne trascorsa a divorare gli insegnamenti delle Scritture, iniziò a cercare altri che capissero e praticassero ciò che la Bibbia diceva. Desiderava avere comunione e imparare tutto ciò che poteva da coloro che comprendevano la Parola di Dio e che praticavano ciò che predicavano.

Mentre quest’uomo si è sforzato di trovare la sua via attraverso questo confuso labirinto di idiosincrasie religiose, alla fine ha acquistato una Bibbia tedesco/inglese. Si sentiva spinto nella sua continua ricerca della Verità, eppure aveva paura di essere scoperto dai leader della sua chiesa locale. Voleva rimanere nella sua chiesa locale, ma la sua coscienza esigeva che egli continuasse la sua ricerca. Per qualche ragione credeva che i leader della sua chiesa locale non sarebbero stati comprensivi nella sua ricerca della verità e che forse sarebbe stato sottoposto a disciplina ecclesiastica per le sue azioni.

La sua chiesa locale fa parte dei discendenti degli Anabattisti che furono perseguitati per la loro fede, incluso il loro desiderio di comprendere e leggere le Scritture nella loro lingua madre—svizzero o tedesco—invece del latino come era richiesto dai leader della chiesa della loro epoca. Eppure eccolo qui, circa 500 anni dopo, in America, possibilmente a fronteggiare persecuzione dalla propria chiesa che dichiara di essere parte della chiesa “giusta” di Dio. In ciò, i suoi leader si trovano sul lato opposto della questione della libertà di culto religioso per la quale i loro antenati patirono, poiché insistono che l’unico modo per conoscere la volontà di Dio sia mediante la lingua ufficiale delle Scritture—il tedesco. Questo NON è diverso dalla lotta degli Anabattisti originali che furono perseguitati per non studiare le Scritture nella lingua ufficiale del loro tempo—il latino.

Ricordiamo, SE i membri della chiesa non comprendono gli insegnamenti della Parola di Dio a causa dell’insistenza testarda dei loro leader che i membri della chiesa NON siano autorizzati a leggere o ascoltare le Scritture nella lingua che comprendono, allora l’ignoranza dell’uomo comune SARÀ posta ai piedi di quei leader nel giorno del giudizio. Obbedite a quelli che vi guidano e soggiacete loro: perché vegliano per le vostre anime, come quelli che rendono conto…–Ebrei 13:17. Obbedire qui è solo nel contesto della Parola di Dio, non semplicemente secondo le idee personali o i capricci dei leader della chiesa. Perché tutti dobbiamo apparire davanti al tribunale di Cristo; affinché ciascuno possa ricevere la retribuzione delle cose fatte nel corpo, secondo abbia operato, o bene o male–2 Corinzi 5:10. Ogni persona riceverà un giudizio personale basato su ciò che insegna la Bibbia, NON secondo il dogma dettagliato di una chiesa.

Quando penso agli sforzi zelanti di quest’uomo penso al verso delle Scritture… Udendo ciò Gesù si meravigliò e disse a quelli che lo seguivano: In verità vi dico, non ho trovato una così grande fede, neppure in Israele–Matteo 8:10. Osservo anche le tendenze attuali di alcune delle nostre case editrici plain—hanno preso spunto dall’idea del mondo (in senso spirituale, naturalmente) che per vendere libri e materiale di lettura debbano stampare storie esaltanti, che tengano le persone con il fiato sospeso—il tutto perché il cristiano di oggi si è annoiato di ciò che sembra antiquato.

Che differenza tra questa storia e molti dei discendenti anabattisti di oggi. Molti dei conservatori anabattisti odierni hanno difficoltà a entusiasmarvisi per la Bibbia. Sono troppo sovrastimolati dalla mancanza di riposo e di quiete nella loro vita quotidiana normale.

Di solito sentiamo storie come questa dalle giungle dell’America Centrale, dai deserti dell’Africa o dalle baraccopoli dell’India. Ciò che mi stupisce è che questa storia avviene proprio in mezzo a uno dei nostri gruppi plain di conservatori anabattisti. Cerchiamo Dio per opportunità di condividere la verità del messaggio del Vangelo con coloro che sono nella sfera della nostra influenza. Potremmo essere sorpresi di quante persone sfioriamo nella nostra vita quotidiana che sarebbero altrettanto affamate della Verità come l’uomo della nostra storia.

A score is a review judgment, NOT a measured percentage of accuracy. Accept only a total of at least 95 and no major or critical finding.

Distinguish Scripture references from times of day: an equivalent localized clock rendering, such as 2 pm becoming 14:00 in clear clock context, is not an added or changed Scripture reference.

Return strict JSON with score (integer 0 through 100), passed (boolean), and findings (array). Do not rewrite the article.

Greetings to one and all in our dear Saviour’s name, Jesus Christ. Another year has passed from the present into the annals of history. Nothing that we have said or done can be recalled and re-lived. Another year is before us. Many are waiting with bated breath, anticipating what this new year will bring forth.

I read somewhere in the news that those on the frontier of technology believe that this year will be a big year for artificial intelligence. One example given was: they are anticipating that this technology will be able to be a part of events such as board meetings with the ability to hear and understand all that is shared by each one present. Then at the end of the meeting, with the push of a button, the artificial intelligence will produce detailed minutes of that meeting with a fair degree of accuracy. Over the last number of years, many of the things that used to be considered science fiction have recently become reality, so, likely, this will become a new reality as well.

What is this world coming to? To the Bible-literate Christian, the end of time certainly seems to be fast approaching. According to the United Nations, the world’s population surpassed 8 billion on November 15, 2022. Many in the world are desperately trying to figure out how to sustain that many people for the long term. Just like the Bible has prophesied, there is an uptick in the number of famines, drought, floods, earthquakes, wars, and rumors of wars, etc. One thing that I find interesting is that even though the world does not want to retain God in their knowledge, insurance companies still refer to certain specific events as “acts of God”.

As Bible-believing Christians how shall we then live? And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet –Matthew 24:6. Let us remember that we should not be troubled. Rather, we should remember that …he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:13. If we, like Peter, take our eyes off of our Lord and start focusing on the stormy conditions around us we will start to sink as well. Remember, it is …the fearful, and unbelieving … [who] shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone… –Revelation 21:8. But, He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son –Revelation 21:7.

In this issue of the magazine, we again have an interesting group of articles for your consideration. Join us as we learn of a somewhat obscure, yet influential leader of the early Anabaptist movement in Switzerland. Let’s honestly evaluate our own hearts as we follow the expository teaching from Habakkuk regarding what it means to have a real faith that is first personal, then corporate. Together we can consider what it really means to enter into the rest of God that is detailed in Hebrews chapter four. The youth can take a look into their emotions as they consider those times when they feel like giving up. The author for our sisters’ article has tackled a very difficult subject—when and how to be submissive as a godly wife. We have another thought-provoking article in the discipleship series. And the doctor has chosen to venture into some uncharted territory with the first of a two-part series on cancer.

A final thought I wish to share, a story in fact… Recently, I heard a first-hand account of a man who was lost before God, how he came to spiritual awakening, and how this started affecting his life. This story caused me to stop and consider where I am as a Christian. Is my relationship with my Lord vibrant? How strong is my commitment towards God and His Word? Is my love for my Lord and Saviour still as real and as strong as it was when I first had my awakening and was converted? I’m sure there are more questions that we could ask ourselves in light of this real-life story. I’ll let you as a reader start compiling your own list. Now for the story…

This man is living somewhere within the United States of America. He is a married man with a young family. He is part of a certain religious group within the plain people—those of Anabaptist heritage. Throughout his lifetime he had endeavored to live his life according to the mandates set forth by the leaders of his local church. Yet, for some reason, he had not been finding answers to his personal need, whatever that was—perhaps even he didn’t know.

This man and some of his family were traveling and ended up lodging overnight in a motel. There, in the nightstand drawer he discovered a book titled “The Holy Bible”. Sure, in his church the Bible was read or quoted each week during their normal worship services. Although this man understood English quite well, his church had a policy that they did not want to be too worldly or too modern by reading from an English Bible so they continued their efforts of teaching God’s Word using the original language of their people.

The problem was that this man, somehow, never developed an understanding of that language, thus he never heard the truth of God’s Word. All that he heard was what 1 Corinthians chapter 14 refers to as tongues (languages) and since he didn’t understand the language and since there was no interpretation given, he was not able to be edified. The purpose of this story is not to find fault or to place blame, but rather to bring light to an obvious problem among some of the plain people. A problem for which God would surely desire to see changes made for the betterment of those seeking Him in such settings.

With this in mind, we now come back to this man—a man zealous in his religious life—yet having NEVER heard the message of the Gospel of Jesus Christ. As he hesitantly picked up this English Bible he cautiously started to read the message contained within those book covers. As he read, he became more and more excited. Here were things that he had never heard before—teachings that brought sense to his many questions and the emptiness that he felt within his soul. He was so engrossed that he almost couldn’t pull himself away to allow time for sleep. After a short night, they went on with their travels.

Completing their business they returned home, but life would never be the same for that man. Something had been awakened deep within his soul. Questions had been answered. Longings had been met. Peace had begun to settle over his troubled heart. At long last, he had found the answer, but his time of reading had been so short. Surely there was more to learn, much more. So, before too much time had elapsed, he once more scheduled a trip to get away from his local area and to once more provide a reason to spend another night in a motel with a Bible in the nightstand drawer. He eagerly anticipated another night alone with God and His Word. After a second sleepless night spent devouring the teachings of the Scriptures, he started seeking others who understood and practiced what the Bible said. He was desiring to fellowship and learn all that he could from those who understood God’s Word and who practiced what they preached.

As this man has endeavored to find his way through this confusing maze of religious idiosyncrasies he finally purchased a German/English Bible. He felt driven in his continued pursuit of the Truth, yet he was afraid to be found out by his local church leaders. He wanted to stay within his local church, yet his conscience demanded that he must continue his search. For some reason he believed that his local church leaders would not be understanding in his quest for truth and that maybe he would be placed under church discipline for his actions.

His local church is a part of the descendants of the Anabaptists who were persecuted for their faith, including their desire to understand, and read the Scriptures in their native tongue—Swiss or German, instead of Latin as was required by the church leaders of their day. Yet here he is, some 500 years later, in America, possibly facing persecution from his own church which claims to be a part of the “right” church of God. Herein, his church leaders are finding themselves on the opposite side of the issue of freedom of religious worship that their forefathers suffered for, since they are insisting that the only way to learn of God’s will is through the official language of Scripture—German. This is NO different than the struggle of the original Anabaptists who were persecuted for not studying the Scriptures in the official language of their day—Latin.

Let’s remember, IF church members do not understand the teachings of God’s Word due to their church leaders’ stubborn insistence that the church members are NOT allowed to read or hear the Scriptures in the language that they understand, then the ignorance of the common man WILL be laid at the feet of those leaders come judgment day. Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account… –Hebrews 13:17. Obey here is only in the context of God’s Word, not just according to church leaders’ personal ideas or whims. For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad –2 Corinthians 5:10. Every person will receive personal judgment based on what the Bible teaches NOT according to a church’s detailed dogma.

When I think of the zealous efforts of this man I think of the verse of Scripture… When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel –Matthew 8:10. I also observe the current trends of some of our plain publishing houses—they have borrowed from the world’s idea (in a spiritual way, of course) that to sell books and reading material they need to print exhilarating stories, ones that keep people on the edge of their seats—all this because today’s Christian has become bored with that which seems old-fashioned.

What a difference between this story and many of today’s Anabaptist descendants. Many of today’s conservative Anabaptist people have a difficult time getting excited about the Bible. They are too over-stimulated by the lack of rest and quiet in their normal daily lives.

Usually, we hear of stories like this from the jungles of Central America, the deserts of Africa, or the slums of India. What I am amazed about is that this story takes place right in the midst of one of our plain groups of conservative Anabaptists. Let’s seek God for opportunities to share the truth of the Gospel message with those within the sphere of our influence. We might be surprised how many people we rub shoulders with during our daily lives who would be just as hungry for the Truth as the man in our story.

사랑하는 구주 예수 그리스도의 이름으로 모두에게 문안드립니다. 또 한 해가 현재로부터 역사의 기록 속으로 흘러갔습니다. 우리가 말하고 행한 것을 다시 불러내어 다시 살 수는 없습니다. 또 한 해가 우리 앞에 놓여 있습니다. 많은 사람들이 새해에 무엇이 일어날지 숨을 죽이고 기대하고 있습니다.

어디선가 읽었는데, 기술 최전선에 있는 이들은 올해가 인공지능에게 큰 해가 될 것이라고 믿는다고 합니다. 한 가지 예로, 이 기술이 각 참석자가 나누는 모든 말을 듣고 이해할 수 있어 이사회를 비롯한 회의에 참여할 수 있게 될 것으로 예상된다고 합니다. 그러고는 회의가 끝나면 버튼 하나로 인공지능이 상당한 정확도로 그 회의의 상세한 회의록을 만들어 낼 것이라고 합니다. 지난 수년간 한때 공상과학으로 여겨졌던 많은 것들이 최근 현실이 되었으니, 아마 이것도 곧 현실이 되리라 생각합니다.

이 세상은 어디로 가고 있는가요? 성경에 익숙한 그리스도인에게는 종말이 확실히 빠르게 다가오는 듯 보입니다. 유엔에 따르면 세계 인구는 2022년 11월 15일에 80억을 돌파했습니다. 세계의 많은 사람들은 그 많은 인구를 장기적으로 어떻게 부양할지 필사적으로 고민하고 있습니다. 성경이 예언한 대로 기근, 가뭄, 홍수, 지진, 전쟁과 전쟁의 소문 등이 증가하고 있습니다. 흥미로운 점 하나는 세상 사람들은 하나님을 그 지식에서 보존하려 하지 않는데도 보험회사들은 여전히 특정 사건들을 ‘하나님의 행위(acts of God)’라고 칭한다는 사실입니다.

성경을 믿는 그리스도인으로서 우리는 어떻게 살아야 합니까? And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet –Matthew 24:6. 우리가 근심하지 말아야 함을 기억합시다. 오히려 …he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved –Matthew 24:13. 베드로처럼 주님의 눈을 떼고 주위의 폭풍우 같은 상황에 눈을 고정하면 우리도 침몰하기 시작할 것입니다. 기억하십시오, …the fearful, and unbelieving … [who] shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone… –Revelation 21:8. 그러나 He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son –Revelation 21:7.

이번 호 잡지에는 다시 한 번 숙고할 만한 흥미로운 글들이 모였습니다. 스위스 초기 재세례파 운동에서 다소 잘 알려지지 않았지만 영향력 있던 지도자에 대해 배워 보십시오. 하박국의 설교적 교훈을 따라 우리가 진정한 믿음을 갖는다는 것이 개인적으로 그리고 그 다음에 공동체적으로 무엇을 의미하는지 우리 자신의 마음을 정직하게 평가해 봅시다. 함께 히브리서 4장에서 자세히 다루는 하나님의 안식에 실제로 들어간다는 것이 무엇을 의미하는지 고려해 볼 수 있습니다. 젊은이들은 포기하고 싶을 때의 감정들을 들여다볼 수 있습니다. 자매들을 위한 글의 필자는 매우 어려운 주제를 다루었습니다—경건한 아내로서 언제 그리고 어떻게 복종해야 하는가. 제자훈련 시리즈에서는 또 하나의 사색을 불러일으키는 글이 있습니다. 그리고 의사는 암에 관한 2부작 시리즈의 첫 부분으로 미지의 영역을 개척하려는 선택을 했습니다.

마지막으로 나누고 싶은 생각 하나, 사실 한 이야기가 있습니다… 최근에 저는 하나님 앞에서 길 잃은 한 사람이 어떻게 영적으로 깨어났고 이것이 그의 삶에 어떻게 영향을 주기 시작했는지에 대한 직접적인 이야기를 들었습니다. 이 이야기는 제가 그리스도인으로서 어디에 서 있는지 되돌아보게 했습니다. 나와 주님과의 관계는 활기 있는가? 하나님과 그분의 말씀을 향한 나의 헌신은 얼마나 강한가? 각성하고 회심했을 때 가졌던 주님과 구주에 대한 나의 사랑은 여전히 같은 정도로 진실하고 강한가? 이 실화에 비추어 우리가 스스로에게 물어볼 수 있는 질문은 더 많을 것입니다. 독자 여러분도 스스로 목록을 만들어 보시기 바랍니다. 이제 그 이야기입니다…

이 남자는 미국 어딘가에 살고 있습니다. 그는 어린 자녀가 있는 기혼 남성입니다. 그는 평안한 계통의 특정 종교 집단, 즉 재세례파 계통의 사람들 중 하나입니다. 평생 동안 그는 지역 교회 지도자들이 제시한 명령에 따라 살려고 애썼습니다. 그런데 어떤 이유에서인지 그는 자신의 개인적 필요, 어쩌면 스스로도 알지 못했을 그 필요에 대한 해답을 찾지 못해왔습니다.

이 남자와 그의 가족 일부는 여행 중 모텔에서 하룻밤을 묵게 되었습니다. 그곳 협탁 서랍에서 그는 "The Holy Bible"이라는 제목의 책을 발견했습니다. 물론 그의 교회에서는 정상 예배 시간에 성경이 읽히거나 인용되곤 했습니다. 이 남자는 영어를 꽤 잘 이해했음에도 불구하고 그의 교회는 너무 세속적이거나 현대적으로 보이는 것을 원하지 않아 영어 성경을 읽지 않으려 했고, 그들 민족의 원어로 하나님의 말씀을 가르치려는 노력을 계속해 왔습니다.

문제는 이 남자가 어떻게든 그 언어를 전혀 이해하지 못해 하나님의 말씀의 진리를 들어 본 적이 없다는 것입니다. 그가 듣는 것은 고린도전서 14장이 언급하는 방언(언어)이었고, 그 언어를 이해하지 못했고 통역도 주어지지 않았기 때문에 그는 세우임을 받지 못했습니다. 이 이야기의 목적은 누군가를 비난하거나 탓하기 위함이 아니라, 이런 환경에서 하나님을 찾는 사람들의 유익을 위해 일부 평안 계통 사람들 사이에 있는 분명한 문제에 빛을 비추기 위함입니다.

이 점을 염두에 두고 우리는 다시 이 남자로 돌아옵니다—종교적으로 열심이지만 결코 예수 그리스도의 복음 메시지를 들어 본 적이 없는 남자였습니다. 그는 조심스럽게 영어 성경을 집어 들고 그 책 표지 안에 담긴 메시지를 조심스럽게 읽기 시작했습니다. 읽을수록 그는 점점 더 흥분했습니다. 그가 이전에 들어 본 적이 없는 것들—그의 많은 질문들과 영혼의 공허함에 이치를 가져다 주는 가르침들이 그 안에 있었습니다. 그는 너무 몰두한 나머지 잠잘 시간을 떼어 놓기조차 힘들었습니다. 짧은 밤을 보낸 뒤 그들은 여행을 계속했습니다.

일을 마치고 집으로 돌아왔지만 그 남자의 삶은 결코 예전 같지 않았습니다. 그의 영혼 깊은 곳에서 무언가가 깨어났습니다. 질문들이 답을 얻었습니다. 갈망이 채워졌습니다. 평화가 그의 괴로운 마음 위에 자리하기 시작했습니다. 마침내 그는 해답을 찾았지만 그가 읽은 시간은 너무 짧았습니다. 분명히 배울 것이 더 많았습니다. 그래서 많은 시간이 흐르기 전에 그는 다시 지역을 벗어나 모텔에서 하룻밤을 보내고 협탁 서랍의 성경과 함께 시간을 보내기 위해 또 여행을 계획했습니다. 그는 하나님과 그분의 말씀과 단둘이 보낼 또 다른 밤을 간절히 기대했습니다. 두 번째로 잠 못 이루는 밤을 성경의 가르침을 탐독하며 보낸 뒤, 그는 성경을 이해하고 실천하는 사람들을 찾기 시작했습니다. 그는 성경을 이해하고 그들이 설교하는 것을 실천하는 이들과 교제하며 가능한 한 많이 배우고자 했습니다.

이 남자가 종교적 편벽성의 혼란스러운 미로를 헤쳐 나가려고 애쓰는 가운데 그는 마침내 독일어/영어 성경을 구입했습니다. 그는 진리를 향한 계속된 추구에 사로잡혀 있었지만 지역 교회 지도자들에게 발각될까 두려워했습니다. 그는 지역 교회 안에 남아 있으려 했지만 양심은 그가 계속해서 진리를 찾아야 한다고 요구했습니다. 어째서인지 그는 지역 교회 지도자들이 그의 진리 탐구를 이해하지 못할 것이며 어쩌면 그의 행동 때문에 교회 징계를 받을지도 모른다고 믿었습니다.

그의 지역 교회는 라틴어가 그들의 시대에 교회 지도자들이 요구했던 것인 반면, 스위스어나 독일어 같은 자국어로 성경을 이해하고 읽기 원했던 신앙 때문에 박해받은 재세례파의 자손들에 속해 있습니다. 그런데 여기 이 남자는 500여 년이 지난 미국에서, 하나님의 "바른" 교회라 주장하는 자신의 교회로부터 박해를 받을지도 모르는 처지에 놓여 있습니다. 이 문제에서 그의 교회 지도자들은 조상들이 고통받았던 종교적 예배의 자유 문제의 반대편에 서게 됩니다. 그들은 성경의 뜻을 알기 위한 유일한 길은 성경의 공식 언어인 독일어를 통해서만 가능하다고 주장하고 있기 때문입니다. 이것은 당시의 공식 언어인 라틴어로 성경을 공부하지 않았다는 이유로 박해받았던 최초의 재세례파들의 투쟁과 전혀 다르지 않습니다.

교인들이 교회 지도자들이 고집스럽게 성도들이 자신들이 이해하는 언어로 성경을 읽거나 들을 수 없다고 강요하기 때문에 하나님의 말씀의 가르침을 이해하지 못한다면, 평신도의 무지는 심판 날에 그 지도자들의 책임으로 돌아갈 것임을 기억합시다. Obey them that have the rule over you, and submit yourselves: for they watch for your souls, as they that must give account… –Hebrews 13:17. 여기서 순종은 오직 하나님의 말씀의 맥락 안에서만이며, 단지 교회 지도자들의 개인적 사상이나 변덕에 따른 것은 아닙니다. For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad –2 Corinthians 5:10. 각 사람은 교회의 상세한 교리들이 아니라 성경이 가르치는 바에 근거하여 개인적 심판을 받게 될 것입니다.

이 남자의 열심을 생각할 때 나는 성경의 한 구절을 떠올립니다… When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel –Matthew 8:10. 또한 나는 일부 평안 출판사들의 현재 경향을 관찰합니다—그들은 세상(물론 영적 방식으로)의 아이디어를 차용하여 책과 읽을거리를 팔기 위해 사람들을 긴장시켜 좌석 가장자리에 붙들어 매는 전율적인 이야기를 인쇄해야 한다고 생각합니다—오늘날의 그리스도인들이 구식으로 보이는 것에 지쳐 버렸기 때문이라는 것입니다.

이 이야기와 오늘날 많은 재세례파 후손들 사이의 차이는 참으로 큽니다. 오늘날의 보수적 재세례파 사람들은 성경에 대해 흥분하기가 어렵습니다. 그들은 일상생활에서 휴식과 고요가 부족하여 과도하게 자극을 받고 있습니다.

보통 우리는 이런 이야기를 중앙아메리카의 정글, 아프리카의 사막, 또는 인도의 빈민가에서 듣습니다. 놀라운 점은 이 이야기가 우리의 보수적 평안 그룹 한가운데에서 일어났다는 것입니다. 우리가 영향력을 미칠 수 있는 범위 내의 이들에게 복음 진리를 나눌 기회를 위해 하나님께 구합시다. 일상생활에서 어깨를 마주치는 사람들이 이 이야기 속의 남자만큼 진리를 갈망하는 사람이 얼마나 많은지에 우리는 놀랄지도 모릅니다.

This hymn is generally considered to be one of the greatest hymns ever written and is found in nearly every hymnal or book of hymns published today. It was written by a man who was frail in body, but strong in spirit. It was he who coined the phrase, “It is better to wear out than to rust out.” Let us now take a glimpse into the life of this servant of God.

Henry Francis Lyte, the author of this great and noteworthy hymn, was born June 1, 1793, in Ednam, near Kelso, Scotland. At a young age, he was left an orphan and was in comparative poverty. He was educated at Trinity College in Dublin, Ireland. It was there that his gift of poetry began to appear, winning him three prizes. His primary goal with his studies was to become a physician, instead, by the providence of God, he became a minister of the gospel of Jesus Christ.

One day in Cornwall, a fellow clergyman who was on his deathbed, requested that Lyte would come and give him some spiritual comfort. “To their mutual grief, they found themselves [both] groping for the light, veritable blind guides”. As they searched for truth and assurance of salvation, they fixed their faith on Christ, and Lyte came away from that sickroom a changed man, never to be the same again. It is said that it was his encounter with God at the bedside of that dying man that prompted Lyte’s noble hymn, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken.” In the year 1823, Henry F. Lyte took charge of a seashore parish, Lower Brixham, in Devonshire, England. It was at that place where he spent the last 23 years of his life toiling as a pastor for the spiritual good of the poor fishing people and the rough seafaring men of that region until his death in the fall of 1847. For all of Henry’s dedication and labor, he received a reward: having a Sunday school of several hundred scholars, as well as “a splendid company of seventy or eighty teachers, personally trained by him.”

Throughout his lifetime, his health was continually threatened by asthma and tuberculosis. Notwithstanding his physical frailties, he worked tirelessly with an established reputation as a poet, musician, and minister. Wherever he went, he was greatly loved and admired by his people. Toward the end of these later years, his health became gradually worse. So it was that during the winter months, he felt compelled to seek a warmer climate in Italy, which is a part of southern Europe.

Though he was greatly weakened by his sickness, on September 4, 1847, as Lyte was about to leave to head southward, he was arrested by an “irresistible desire” to preach once more to his congregation. He dearly loved these people and he had labored among them for so many years. “Against the protest of his amazed friends, he accomplished this purpose, and it is recorded that Lyte nearly had to crawl to the pulpit and his message came as from a dying man.” “O brethren,” he said, as he entered the familiar pulpit for the last time, “I stand here among you today, as alive from the dead, if I may hope to impress it upon you, and induce you to prepare for that solemn hour which must come to all, by a timely appreciation and dependance on the death of Christ.” These final words made a deep impact upon his congregation, after which he closed the service by administering the Lord’s Supper to his weeping people. Later that evening, after the service, he was inspired to “poetical composition” and wrote the eight stanzas of his last and greatest hymn:

Abide with me: fast falls the eventide;
The darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide:
when other helpers fail, and comforts flee,
Help of the helpless, O abide with me.

Swift to its close ebbs out life’s little day;
Earth’s joys grow dim, its glories pass away;
Change and decay in all around I see;
O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

Not a brief glance I beg, a passing word;
But, as Thou dwell’st with Thy disciples, Lord,
Familiar, condescending, patient, free,
Come, not to sojourn, but abide, with me.

Come not in terrors, as the King of kings;
But kind and good, with healing in Thy wings;
Tears for all woes, a heart for every plea;
Come, Friend of sinners, and thus ‘bide with me.

Thou on my head in early youth didst smile;
And, though rebellious and perverse meanwhile,
thou hast not left me, oft as I left thee:
On to the close, O Lord, abide with me.

I need Thy presence every passing hour;
What but Thy grace can foil the tempter’s power?
Who like Thyself my guide and stay can be?
Through cloud and sunshine, O abide with me.

I fear no foe, with Thee at hand to bless:
Ills have no weight, and tears no bitterness.
Where is death’s sting? Where, grave, thy victory?
I triumph still, if Thou abide with me.

Hold Thou Thy cross before my closing eyes;
Shine through the gloom, and point me to the skies;
Heaven’s morning breaks, and earth’s vain shadows flee:
In life, in death, O Lord, abide with me.

This hymn he gave to one of the family members that very night. Leaving the following day, he began his trek to Rome, Italy, hoping to gain some relief from his sickness. Lyte make it as far as Nice, France where his sickness prevented his further travel. He passed away soon after the age of 55, on November 20, 1847. His last words were “Joy! Peace!”

The scene behind this hymn is that of the resurrected Christ Jesus walking on the road to Emmaus with two of His somewhat sad and discouraged disciples. As they neared the end of their seven-mile walk and approached the village where they were going, Jesus …made as though he would have gone further. But they constrained him, saying, Abide with us: for it is toward evening, and the day is far spent. And he went in to tarry with them –Luke 24:28-29.

We can draw a parallel between that scene and Henry F. Lyte’s own experience of drawing toward the close of his earthly journey. Thus, as the disciples besought the risen Lord to abide with them in the close of that ancient day, so was the meaning of this song written in the “shadows of death” to the hymn writer.

Lyte himself composed a tune for this hymn on the same evening that he wrote it, but it never became widely used. However, the tune universally used was written fourteen years later by William Henry Monk, a noted London musician, and editor of the well-known Anglican hymnal, Hymns Ancient and Modern. He included this song in his first edition, which was published in 1861.

In all, William H. Monk composed 50 tunes for the hymnal. It is said that Monk, being “inspired by the beauty of a glorious sunset while yet experiencing a deep personal sorrow,” composed (in only 10 minutes) the tune, Eventide, for the song, “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk also wrote the music for other familiar hymns such as “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious”, and “The Strife Is O’er”.

To summarize, Henry Lyte experienced many sorrows during his lifetime. Both of his parents died at an early age leaving him an orphan. And his own sickness and frailty caused him to be in ongoing danger of asthma and tuberculosis. Yet, in spite of all his trials, we find in him a resilient spirit to reach out to others; to touch and minister the Gospel to those poor people among whom he lived. “In no other writer,” says Dr. Breed (in the Treasury of Hymn Stories), “are poetry and religion more exquisitely united.”

Hierdie gesang word oor die algemeen beskou as een van die grootste gesange ooit geskryf en kom voor in byna elke sangbundel of boek van gesange wat vandag gepubliseer word. Dit is geskryf deur ’n man wat liggaamlik broos was, maar geeslik sterk. Hy was diegene wat die frase geskep het: “Dit is beter om uit te dra as om te roes.” Kom ons neem nou ’n blik in die lewe van hierdie diensbaar van God.

Henry Francis Lyte, die outeur van hierdie groot en merkwaardige gesang, is gebore op 1 Junie 1793 in Ednam, naby Kelso, Skotland. Op jong ouderdom het hy ’n wees geword en was in vergelykende armoede. Hy is opgevoed aan Trinity College in Dublin, Ierland. Dit was daar dat sy digtalent begin verskyn het, wat hom drie pryse besorg het. Sy primêre doel met sy studies was om ’n dokter te word; in plaas daarvan het hy, deur die voorzienigheid van God, ’n predikant van die evangelie van Jesus Christus geword.

Eendag in Cornwall het ’n medepredikant wat op sy sterfbed was, gevra dat Lyte sou kom en hom ’n geestelike troos gee. “Tot hulle gesamentlike smart het hulle hulself [albei] bevind dat hulle na die lig tas, werklike blinde leiers”. Terwyl hulle na die waarheid en die versekering van redding gesoek het, het hulle hul geloof op Christus gefokus, en Lyte het uit daardie siekekamer gekom as ’n veranderde man, nooit weer dieselfde nie. Daar word gesê dat dit sy ontmoeting met God aan die sybed van daardie sterwende man was wat Lyte se edele gesang, “Jesus, I My Cross Have Taken,” aangevuur het. In die jaar 1823 het Henry F. Lyte ’n kusparochie in beheer geneem, Lower Brixham, in Devonshire, Engeland. Dit was op daardie plek waar hy die laaste 23 jaar van sy lewe gespandeer het, werkend as ’n pastoor vir die geestelike welstand van die arm vissersmense en die rowwe seevaarders van daardie streek tot aan sy dood in die herfs van 1847. Vir al Henry se toewyding en arbeid het hy ’n beloning ontvang: ’n Sondagskool van verskeie honderde leerlinge, sowel as “’n pragtige geselskap van sewe- of tagtig onderwysers, persoonlik deur hom opgelei.”

Gedurende sy leeftyd is sy gesondheid voortdurend bedreig deur asma en tuberkulose. Nieteenstaande sy fisiese broosheid het hy onophoudelik gewerk met ’n gevestigde reputasie as digter, musikant en predikant. Waar hy ook al gegaan het, is hy baie deur sy mense gelief en bewonder. Teen die einde van hierdie latere jare het sy gesondheid geleidelik versleg. Dit was waarom hy gedurende die wintermaande gedwing gevoel het om na ’n warmer klimaat in Italië in die suide van Europa te soek.

Al was hy deur sy siekte sterk verflenter, op 4 September 1847, toe Lyte op die punt was om suidwaarts te vertrek, is hy deur ’n “onweerstaanbare begeerte” opgehou om nogmaals tot sy gemeente te preek. Hy het hierdie mense innig liefgehad en so baie jare onder hulle gewerk. “Teen die beleid van sy verbaasde vriende het hy hierdie doel bereik, en daar word aangeteken dat Lyte amper na die preekstoel moes kruip en sy boodskap gekom het as uit ’n sterwende man.” “O broeders,” het hy gesê, toe hy vir die laaste keer die bekende preekstoel betree het, “ek staan vandag hier onder julle as uit die dooies lewend, as ek mag hoop om dit op julle in te druk, en julle te beweeg om julle voor te berei vir daardie ernstige uur wat op almal sal kom, deur ’n tydige waardering en afhanklikheid van die dood van Christus.” Hierdie laaste woorde het ’n diep indruk op sy gemeente gemaak, waarna hy die erediens afgesluit het deur die Here se Avondmaal aan sy huilende mense toe te dien. Later daardie aand, na die erediens, is hy geïnspireer tot “poëtiese samestelling” en het die agt strofes van sy laaste en grootste gesang geskryf:

Wees by my: vinnig val die skemer;
Die duisternis verdiep; Here, wees by my:
wanneer ander helper faal, en vertroosings vlug,
Helper van die hulpeloses, O wees by my.

Vinnig vloei uit die lewe se kort dag tot sy einde;
Aardse vreugdes dof, sy glorieë gaan verby;
Verandering en vergaan sien ek oral om my;
O Gij wat nie verander nie, wees by my.

Nie ’n kort blik smeek ek, ’n voorbygaande woord;
Maar, soos Gij met U dissipels woon, Here,
Vertroudelik, neerbuigend, geduldig, vry,
Kom, nie om te bly nie, maar word, wees by my.

Kom nie in terreur, as die Koning van konings nie;
Maar vriendelik en goed, met genesing in U vlerke;
Trane vir alle smart, ’n hart vir elke versoek;
Kom, Vriend van sondaars, en bly so by my.

Gij het oor my geboë in my vroeë jeug;
En, al was ek rebels en verkeerd intussen,
het Gij my nie verlaat nie, dikwels soos ek U verlaat het:
Tot by die einde, O Here, wees by my.

Ek het U teenwoordigheid nodig in elke verbygaande uur;
Wat anders as U genade kan die versoeker se krag weerstaan?
Wie soos U kan my gids en steun wees?
Deur wolk en sonskyn, O wees by my.

Ek vrees geen vyand nie, met U naby om te seën:
Slegte dinge het geen swaarheid, en trane geen bitterheid.
Waar is die stekel van die dood? Waar, graf, is jou oorwinning?
Ek triomfeer steeds, as Gij by my bly.

Hou U kruis voor my sluitende oë;
Skyn deur die duisternis, en wys my na die hemele;
Hemelse môre breek, en die aardse skynsels vlug:
In lewe, in dood, O Here, wees by my.

Hierdie gesang het hy daardie nag aan een van die familielede geskenk. Die volgende dag het hy vertrek en sy reis na Rome, Italië begin, hoopvol om van sy siekte verligting te vind. Lyte het so ver as Nice, Frankryk, gekom waar sy siekte sy verdere reis verhinder het. Hy is kort daarna oorlede op 20 November 1847, kort ná die ouderdom van 55. Sy laaste woorde was “Vreugde! Vrede!”

Die skildery agter hierdie gesang is daardie van die verrewekte Christus Jesus wat op die pad na Emmaus met twee van Sy ietwat bedroefde en moedeloos gelaat dissipels wandel. Toe hulle die einde van hul sewemyl-wandeling nader en die dorpie nader waarheen hulle op pad was, …daarop het Hy asof Hy dalk verder sou gegaan het. En hulle het Hom getrek, en gesê: Blijf by ons; want dit is al na die aand, en die dag is al verby. En Hy het met hulle ingegaan om by hulle te bly — Lukas 24:28-29.

Ons kan ’n parallel trek tussen daardie skildery en Henry F. Lyte se eie ervaring van nader aan die einde van sy aardse reis. Soos die dissipels die verrewe Heer aangehou het om by hulle te bly aan die einde van daardie ou dag, so is die betekenis van hierdie lied in die “skaduwees van die dood” vir die liedjieskrywer geskryf.

Lyte self het ’n melodie vir hierdie gesang gecomponeer op dieselfde aand dat hy dit geskryf het, maar dit het nooit wyd gebruik geword nie. Die melodie wat egter universeel gebruik word, is veertien jaar later deur William Henry Monk geskryf, ’n bekende Londen-musikant en redakteur van die welbekende Anglikaanse sangbundel, Hymns Ancient and Modern. Hy het hierdie lied in sy eerste uitgawe ingesluit, wat in 1861 gepubliseer is.

In totaal het William H. Monk 50 melodieë vir die sangbundel gecomponeer. Daar word gesê dat Monk, geïnspireer deur die skoonheid van ’n heerlike sononder terwyl hy nog ’n diep persoonlike smart ervaar het, die melodie Eventide in slegs 10 minute geskryf het vir die lied, “Abide With Me, Fast Falls The Eventide”. William Monk het ook die musiek geskryf vir ander bekende gesange soos “Look, Ye Saints! The Sight Is Glorious”, en “The Strife Is O’er”.

Samengevat het Henry Lyte gedurende sy leeftyd baie smart ervaar. Albei sy ouers is op ’n vroeë ouderdom oorlede en het hom ’n wees gemaak. En sy eie siekte en broosheid het hom in voortdurende gevaar van asma en tuberkulose gehou. Tog, ten spyte van al sy beproewings, vind ons in hom ’n veerkragtige gees om ander te bereik; om die Evangelie te raak en te bedien aan daardie arme mense onder wie hy gewoon het. “In geen ander skrywer,” sê Dr. Breed (in die Treasury of Hymn Stories), “is poësie en godsdiens meer voortreflik verenig.”

And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus –Matthew 14:28-29.

Men who follow Jesus are men of faith. Discipleship is not for cowards or the faint of heart, nor is it for those who demand a rationale for acts of obedience. The disciples had spent the day with Jesus. After the feeding of the five thousand Matthew writes that …straightway Jesus constrained his disciples to get into a ship, and to go before him unto the other side, while he sent the multitudes away –Matthew 14:22.

If there was anything that the disciples were familiar with and skilled in, it was sailing the waters of Galilee. This was their territory. Peter and John had fished these waters with their father from their earliest remembrance. But tonight, they were making little headway… the wind was contrary.

And in the fourth watch of the night Jesus went unto them, walking on the sea. And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear. But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid –Matthew 14:25-27.

Peter then made this bold appeal …Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water –Matthew 14:28. What was Peter thinking? He had never walked on water. Jesus was not asking him to walk on water. It was not logical. It defied the laws of nature… yet when Jesus said “come”. Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water to go to Jesus. That’s right! He was treading on water.

Peter was responding to a clear call from Jesus. Jesus said “come”. It is important that we understand that faith is our response to the clear call of God on our lives. Too often in our ambition to be useful we choose our path and call our ambition “faith” when God may not be in it at all.

If you want to be a man of faith, open your Bible and pray. Ask God to reveal His plan for your life. The Bible contains many commandments that can provide practical direction for our lives. Take God at His Word. Step out in faith and obedience then you will experience the miracle of God’s power in your life.

Peter’s boat was his security. He and his boat had a long relationship. It had served him well for many years. Peter felt right at home in his old bark, although tonight she did not seem to respond well to his masterful seamanship. He had drawn many a draught of fish over her gunwales. Now as he stands on her deck watching Jesus approach, “walking on the water”, he was overcome with a desire to go to Jesus. In reckless abandonment he stepped off her deck …and a miracle happened.

A walk of faith often calls us away from that which is familiar and secure. If we make safety and security our priority—if we limit our actions to carefully calculated risks (limited to that which we can manage and control)—we limit the power of God working in and through us.

Our forefathers in Europe knew that if they embraced the journey of unreserved discipleship, it could be costly. They risked the seizure of their property; many of them lost all that they owned. Since they willingly faced imprisonment and death, we refer to them as heroes of the faith. These were men who were willing to abandon all for the sake of the gospel. Because of their faith we receive the benefits of a godly heritage.

I commend our younger generation of Anabaptist youth for their willingness to make following Jesus a priority. In the past our priority has been to build our security base, be it our farm or business, and then consider mission work as a possibility. That was never Jesus’ model for service. When Jesus sent out his disciples he said. And he said unto them, Take nothing for your journey, neither staves, nor scrip, neither bread, neither money; neither have two coats apiece –Luke 9:3.

Later, after they had returned, Jesus asked them, And he said unto them, When I sent you without purse, and scrip, and shoes, lacked ye any thing? And they said, Nothing –Luke 22:35.

You do not need to go into foreign missions to experience the power of God released in your life. Every act of radical obedience is an act of faith. There are men in our Anabaptist communities who are experiencing moral defeat. If we are going to succumb to a victim mentality (“I can’t help it”), and define moral failure as an addiction, we set ourselves up for ongoing defeat. Men of faith are men of action who take measurable steps of obedience which will lead them to ultimate victory. Moral failure begins with small compromises that end in crushing defeat.

Peter’s actions were not logical. If Peter would have processed his decision using the scientific method, he would not have taken such a risk. Many of the simple commands of Christ have no apparent scientific reasoning. From baptism, to communion, to foot washing, to anointing with oil, these are all acts of faith. The significance and the power of each lies in the doing of it with a heart of obedient faith, not in the thing itself.

So it is with many aspects of the Christian experience. We can analyze a thing endlessly, ultimately resulting in its demise. This happens in many churches. We reason away the woman’s head covering. We reason away the nonconformed lifestyle. We reason away the permanence of marriage. We reason away brotherhood accountability. What we have left has no resemblance to the simple teachings of Jesus. Discipleship calls us to faithful obedience. Jesus and the apostles taught it, so we do it. The blessing and the power lie in the doing of it.

That is what Peter discovered. He walked on water! He did not dip a toe to test the water first. I like to think he leaped from the boat and hit the water with both feet. That would be faith and Peter had faith.

But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? And when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:30-32.

Peter had faith to walk on water until he began to look around and began to process his situation using the scientific method. This is not to invalidate the scientific method. The scientific method proves the order of creation and the evidence of a creator.

In Hebrews 11 we read that …faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen –Hebrews 11:1.

It is our faith that is the substance and our faith that is the evidence of spiritual realities. Just as the scientific method proves the realities of the created world, so our faith proves spiritual realities.

Boisterous wind and crashing waves produced a fearful, sinking Peter. We sometimes criticize Peter for taking his eyes off of Jesus and sinking into the waves; however, Peter walked on water, I know of no one else who walked on water. When we transition from obedient faith to carnal rationalization, we lose power with God.

Are we suggesting that faith is irrational? No, not at all. As a matter of fact, the first act of faith is to believe that Jesus is the logos. John wrote, In the beginning was the Word [Logos], and the Word [Logos], was with God, and the Word [Logos], was God –John 1:1. It is from the Greek word Logos that we get our English word logic.

Just as there are laws in nature that make the scientific method durable and replicable, so there are spiritual laws that give order and cohesion to our inner man. Jesus is the embodiment of these truths. His teachings are the revelation of these truths and through his death and resurrection these truths have become accessible to all. Jesus promised, Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth… –John 16:13.

Men of faith are men who have eyes to see these spiritual realities. Their vision is not limited to the natural world. They understand that there are spiritual realities that have “cause and effect” in our lives that are every bit as powerful as the “cause and effect” that we see about us in the natural world every day.

These realities are only visible to men of faith. Paul wrote, But the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned –1 Corinthians 2:14. Men of faith, are men whose lives are governed by spiritual realities that are incomprehensible to the natural man. If you will be a man of faith, expect to be misunderstood. You are embarking on a journey that will run counter to the world view of many.

As Peter began to sink into the waves he cried out, “Lord, save me”. His plaintive cry revealed an absolute trust in his Lord. Jesus reached out His hand and rescued him. Jesus next words continue to challenge us. He said to Peter, …O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt? Matthew 14:31. Peter had just walked on water—a feat no man had accomplished before or since, yet Jesus called it “little faith” and asked, “why did you doubt?”.

Jesus said at another time, …If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you –Matthew 17:20.

If Peter’s “little faith” empowered him to walk on water, and if faith as tiny as a grain of mustard seed can remove mountains what does that say of your and my faith?

Perhaps it is evidence that our faith is littler than Peter’s “little faith” and tinier than the tiny grain of mustard seed?! It is also evidence that God honors little faith. What he does not honor is no faith. According to your faith be it unto you. Little faith…walk on water! No faith…sink beneath the waves!

Since Jesus is the “Logos”, He is the master of the natural world and the spirit world. He proved himself to be the Master of the wind and the waves—and when they were come into the ship, the wind ceased –Matthew 14:32. And He proved Himself to be the Master of the spirit world—then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God –Matthew 14:33.

We, in our western world, have become so satiated with materialism that we can easily be led to believe that natural realities are the most powerful realities. This materialism assaults us, not just with the abundance of material things, but also with a bombardment of humanistic philosophy. Humanistic philosophy is thinking that is devoid of spiritual reality… that is devoid of faith.

If you, as a man, find yourself sinking in waves of despair… be it financial struggles… be it relational difficulties… moral failure or maybe you find yourself being your own worst critic…may I challenge you to lift your eyes to the one who is Logos. Jesus is the one who is master of your circumstances and the one who would be Lord of your soul. To allow Jesus to be Lord of your soul is to live in faith obedience to the radical teachings of Jesus.

To live in harmony with the natural world we honor the laws of nature. When we are replacing a roof, we respect the law of gravity. When driving a vehicle, we slow down for turns out of respect for the law of inertia. Defy the natural laws and someone gets hurt.

To live in harmony with the spiritual world, we honor the law of Christ. We love our neighbor. We forgive our brother. We keep our marriage vows. We bear …one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ –Galatians 6:2.

Men of faith are men who are attune to these spiritual realities and order their lives accordingly.

Και ο Πέτρος αποκρίθηκε και είπε σ" Αυτόν, Κύριε, εάν είσαι σύ, πρόσταξόν μου να έλθω προς σε επάνω εις τα ύδατα. Και είπε, Έλα. Και καταβάντος του Πέτρου εκ του πλοίου, περιεπάτησεν επί των υδάτων δια να προπορεύση προς τον Ιησούν –Ματθαίος 14:28-29.

Οι άνδρες που ακολουθούν τον Ιησού είναι άνδρες πίστεως. Η μαθητεία δεν είναι για δειλούς ή όσους έχουν ταχυπαλμία, ούτε είναι για εκείνους που απαιτούν έναν λογικό λόγο για πράξεις υπακοής. Οι μαθητές είχαν περάσει την ημέρα με τον Ιησού. Μετά τον πολλαπλασιασμό των πέντε χιλιάδων ο Ματθαίος γράφει ότι …αμέσως τότε ο Ιησούς απέπνιξε τους μαθητάς του να εισέλθουν εις το πλοίον, και να προπορεύωνται αυτού εις την άλλην όχθην, ενώ αυτός απέλυσεν τους όχλους –Ματθαίος 14:22.

Εάν υπήρχε κάτι με το οποίο οι μαθητές ήταν εξοικειωμένοι και ικανοί, ήταν το να πλέουν στα νερά της Γαλιλαίας. Αυτό ήταν το πεδίο τους. Ο Πέτρος και ο Ιωάννης είχαν ψαρέψει σε αυτά τα νερά με τον πατέρα τους από τα πρώτα τους χρόνια. Αλλά απόψε, προχωρούσαν αργά… ο άνεμος ήταν αντίθετος.

Και εν τη τετάρτη αγρυπνία της νυκτός ήλθεν προς αυτούς ο Ιησούς, περπατών επί της θαλάσσης. Και ότε οι μαθηταί τον είδαν περιπατούντα επί της θαλάσσης, εταράχθησαν, λέγοντες, Εστίν πνεύμα· και εκραύγασαν από φόβου. Αλλά αμέσως ο Ιησούς ελάλησεν προς αυτούς, λέγων, Θαρρήσατε· εγώ ειμί· μη φοβεῖσθε –Ματθαίος 14:25-27.

Ο Πέτρος τότε έκανε αυτή την τολμηρή έκκληση …Κύριε, εάν είσαι σύ, πρόσταξόν μου να έλθω προς σε επάνω εις τα ύδατα –Ματθαίος 14:28. Τι σκεφτόταν ο Πέτρος; Ποτέ δεν είχε περπατήσει πάνω στο νερό. Ο Ιησούς δεν του ζητούσε να περπατήσει πάνω στο νερό. Δεν ήταν λογικό. Αντέβαινε στους νόμους της φύσης… όμως όταν ο Ιησούς είπε «έλα», ο Πέτρος βγήκε από το πλοίο και περπάτησε επάνω στα νερά για να πάει προς τον Ιησού. Είναι αλήθεια! Περπατούσε επάνω στο νερό.

Ο Πέτρος ανταποκρίθηκε σε μια σαφή κλήση από τον Ιησού. Ο Ιησούς είπε «έλα». Είναι σημαντικό να κατανοήσουμε ότι η πίστη είναι η απάντησή μας στην σαφή κλήση του Θεού στη ζωή μας. Πολύ συχνά στην επιθυμία μας να είμαστε χρήσιμοι επιλέγουμε τον δικό μας δρόμο και ονομάζουμε την φιλοδοξία μας «πίστη», ενώ ο Θεός μπορεί να μην βρίσκεται καθόλου σε αυτό.

Αν θέλεις να γίνεις άνθρωπος πίστεως, άνοιξε την Βίβλο σου και προσευχήσου. Ζήτησε από τον Θεό να αποκαλύψει το σχέδιό Του για τη ζωή σου. Η Βίβλος περιέχει πολλές εντολές που μπορούν να δώσουν πρακτική κατεύθυνση στη ζωή μας. Πάρε τον Θεό στο λόγο Του. Βήμασε με πίστη και υπακοή και τότε θα γνωρίσεις το θαύμα της δύναμης του Θεού στη ζωή σου.

Το πλοιάριο του Πέτρου ήταν η ασφάλειά του. Εκείνος και το πλοίο του είχαν μακρά σχέση. Το είχε εξυπηρετήσει καλά για πολλά χρόνια. Ο Πέτρος αισθανόταν σαν στο σπίτι του στην παλιά του βάρκα, αν και απόψε δεν φαινόταν να ανταποκρίνεται καλά στην επιδέξια ναυτοσύνη του. Είχε τραβήξει πολλά δίχτυα ψαριών πάνω από τα πλευρά της. Τώρα καθώς στεκόταν στην κατάστρωμα κοιτάζοντας τον Ιησού να πλησιάζει, «περιπατών επί του ύδατος», τον κατέλαβε μια επιθυμία να πάει προς τον Ιησού. Με απερίσκεπτη εγκατάλειψη πήδηξε από την κατάστρωμα… και συνέβη ένα θαύμα.

Ένα περπάτημα με πίστη συχνά μας καλεί να απομακρυνθούμε από ό,τι είναι οικείο και ασφαλές. Εάν κάνουμε την ασφάλεια και την σιγουριά προτεραιότητά μας — εάν περιορίζουμε τις ενέργειές μας σε προσεκτικά υπολογισμένους κινδύνους (περιορισμένους σε ό,τι μπορούμε να διαχειριστούμε και να ελέγξουμε) — περιορίζουμε τη δύναμη του Θεού που εργάζεται μέσα μας και μέσω μας.

Οι πρόγονοί μας στην Ευρώπη γνώριζαν ότι αν αγκάλιαζαν το ταξίδι της άνευ όρων μαθητείας, αυτό θα μπορούσε να είναι κοστοβόρο. Κινδύνευσαν να τους κατάσχουν την περιουσία· πολλοί από αυτούς έχασαν ό,τι είχαν. Επειδή πρόθυμα αντιμετώπισαν φυλάκιση και θάνατο, τους αποκαλούμε ήρωες της πίστεως. Ήταν άνδρες που ήταν πρόθυμοι να εγκαταλείψουν τα πάντα χάριν του ευαγγελίου. Εξαιτίας της πίστεώς τους λαμβάνουμε τα οφέλη μιας ευσεβούς κληρονομιάς.

Επαινῶ τη νεότερη γενιά των αναβαπτιστών νέων μας για την προθυμία τους να θέσουν την ακολουθία του Ιησού ως προτεραιότητα. Στο παρελθόν η προτεραιότητά μας ήταν να χτίσουμε τη βάση της ασφάλειάς μας, είτε ήταν το αγρόκτημά μας είτε η επιχείρησή μας, και μετά να εξετάσουμε το έργο της αποστολής ως πιθανότητα. Αυτό ποτέ δεν ήταν το μοντέλο του Ιησού για την υπηρεσία. Όταν ο Ιησούς απέστειλε τους μαθητές του είπε. Και είπε προς αυτούς, Μη πάρετε τίποτε δια το ταξείδιον υμών, ούτε ράμβους, ούτε σακκίδιον, ούτε άρτον, ούτε χρυσίον· ουδέ δύο χιτώνας έχθʼ έκαστος –Λουκάς 9:3.

Επιπλέον, όταν επέστρεψαν, ο Ιησούς τους ερώτησε, και είπε προς αυτούς, Ότε υμᾶς απέστειλα χωρίς χρηματοκιβώτιον, ούτε σακκίδιον, ούτε υποδήματα, εστέλει άνευ τινός λειπεῖν; και είπαν, Ουδέν –Λουκάς 22:35.

Δεν χρειάζεται να πας σε ξένες αποστολές για να γνωρίσεις τη δύναμη του Θεού που εκδηλώνεται στη ζωή σου. Κάθε πράξη ριζοσπαστικής υπακοής είναι μια πράξη πίστεως. Υπάρχουν άνδρες στις κοινότητες των Αναβαπτιστών μας που βιώνουν ηθική ήττα. Εάν πρόκειται να υποκύψουμε σε μια νοοτροπία θύματος («δεν μπορώ να το βοηθήσω»), και να ορίσουμε την ηθική αποτυχία ως εθισμό, αυτοτοποθετούμεθα για συνεχή ήττα. Οι άνδρες της πίστεως είναι άνδρες δράσης που παίρνουν μετρήσιμα βήματα υπακοής που θα τους οδηγήσουν στην τελική νίκη. Η ηθική αποτυχία ξεκινά με μικρές συμβιβαστικές πράξεις που καταλήγουν σε συντριπτική ήττα.

Οι ενέργειες του Πέτρου δεν ήταν λογικές. Εάν ο Πέτρος είχε επεξεργαστεί την απόφασή του χρησιμοποιώντας την επιστημονική μέθοδο, δεν θα είχε πάρει τέτοιο ρίσκο. Πολλές από τις απλές εντολές του Χριστού δεν έχουν εμφανή επιστημονική λογική. Από το βάπτισμα, μέχρι την κοινωνία, το πλύσιμο των ποδιών, μέχρι το χρίσμα με έλαιον, όλα αυτά είναι πράξεις πίστεως. Η σημασία και η δύναμη του κάθε ένα βρίσκεται στο να το κάνεις με καρδιά υπακούουσας πίστεως, όχι στο ίδιο το πράγμα.

Έτσι συμβαίνει και με πολλές πλευρές της χριστιανικής εμπειρίας. Μπορούμε να αναλύουμε ένα πράγμα ατέλειωτα, με αποτέλεσμα τελικά την καταστροφή του. Αυτό συμβαίνει σε πολλές εκκλησίες. Απολογούμαστε για την κάλυψη της κεφαλής της γυναίκας. Απολογούμαστε για τον μη συμμορφωμένο τρόπο ζωής. Απολογούμαστε για τη μόνιμη έννοια του γάμου. Απολογούμαστε για την λογοδοσία της αδελφότητας. Αυτό που απομένει δεν μοιάζει καθόλου με τις απλές διδασκαλίες του Ιησού. Η μαθητεία μας καλεί σε πιστή υπακοή. Ο Ιησούς και οι απόστολοι το δίδαξαν, άρα το πράττουμε. Η ευλογία και η δύναμη βρίσκονται στο να το κάνουμε.

Αυτό ανακάλυψε ο Πέτρος. Περπάτησε πάνω στο νερό! Δεν βύθισε ένα δάχτυλο για να δοκιμάσει πρώτα το νερό. Μου αρέσει να σκέφτομαι ότι πήδηξε από το πλοίο και χτύπησε το νερό με τα δύο του πόδια. Αυτό θα ήταν πίστη και ο Πέτρος είχε πίστη.

Αλλά ότε είδεν τον άνεμον οξύ και κύματα, εφοβήθη· και αρχόμενος καταβύθιζε, εκράξεν, λέγων, Κύριε, σώσόν με. Και αμέσως ο Ιησούς εκτείνους την χείρα αυτού, επιάσεν αυτόν και είπεν αυτώ, Ανθρωπε ολιγόπιστε, διά τι εδίστασας; Και ότε εισήλθον εις το πλοίον, ο άνεμος απέπνευσεν –Ματθαίος 14:30-32.

Ο Πέτρος είχε πίστη να περπατήσει πάνω στο νερό μέχρι που άρχισε να κοιτάζει γύρω και να επεξεργάζεται την κατάστασή του χρησιμοποιώντας την επιστημονική μέθοδο. Αυτό δεν είναι για να ακυρώσει την επιστημονική μέθοδο. Η επιστημονική μέθοδος αποδεικνύει την τάξη της κτίσεως και τα στοιχεία ενός δημιουργού.

Στους Εβραίους 11 διαβάζουμε ότι …η πίστις είναι υπόστασις των ελπιζομένων, τεκμήριον των μη βλεπομένων –Εβραίους 11:1.

Είναι η πίστη μας που είναι η υπόστασις και η πίστη μας που είναι το τεκμήριο των πνευματικών πραγματικοτήτων. Όπως η επιστημονική μέθοδος αποδεικνύει τις πραγματικότητες του κτιστού κόσμου, έτσι και η πίστη μας αποδεικνύει τις πνευματικές πραγματικότητες.

Ο θυελλώδης άνεμος και τα συντριπτικά κύματα παρήγαγαν έναν φοβισμένο, βυθιζόμενο Πέτρο. Μερικές φορές επικρίνουμε τον Πέτρο επειδή αφαίρεσε τα μάτια του από τον Ιησού και βυθίστηκε στα κύματα· ωστόσο, ο Πέτρος περπάτησε επάνω στο νερό, δεν γνωρίζω κανέναν άλλο που να περπάτησε επάνω στο νερό. Όταν μεταβαίνουμε από την υπακούουσα πίστη στην σαρκική ορθολογικοποίηση, χάνουμε την δύναμη με τον Θεό.

Λέμε μήπως ότι η πίστη είναι άλογη; Όχι, καθόλου. Στην πραγματικότητα, η πρώτη πράξη της πίστεως είναι να πιστέψεις ότι ο Ιησούς είναι ο Λόγος. Ο Ιωάννης έγραψε, Εν αρχή ήν ο Λόγος, και ο Λόγος ήν προς τον Θεόν, και Θεός ήν ο Λόγος –Ιωάννης 1:1. Από την ελληνική λέξη Λόγος προέρχεται η αγγλική μας λέξη logic (λογική).

Καθώς υπάρχουν νόμοι στη φύση που κάνουν την επιστημονική μέθοδο ανθεκτική και επαναλήψιμη, έτσι υπάρχουν πνευματικοί νόμοι που δίνουν τάξη και συνοχή στον εσωτερικό μας άνθρωπο. Ο Ιησούς είναι η ενσάρκωση αυτών των αληθειών. Οι διδασκαλίες του είναι η αποκάλυψη αυτών των αληθειών και μέσω του θανάτου και της αναστάσεώς Του αυτές οι αλήθειες έχουν γίνει προσιτές σε όλους. Ο Ιησούς υποσχέθηκε, Όταν δε έλθη εκείνος, το Πνεύμα της αληθείας, θα οδηγήσει υμάς εις πάσαν την αλήθειαν… –Ιωάννης 16:13.

Οι άνδρες της πίστεως είναι άνδρες που έχουν μάτια να ιδούν αυτές τις πνευματικές πραγματικότητες. Το όραμά τους δεν περιορίζεται στον φυσικό κόσμο. Κατανοούν ότι υπάρχουν πνευματικές πραγματικότητες που έχουν «αιτία και αποτέλεσμα» στη ζωή μας που είναι εξίσου ισχυρές με την «αιτία και αποτέλεσμα» που βλέπουμε γύρω μας στον φυσικό κόσμο κάθε ημέρα.

Αυτές οι πραγματικότητες γίνονται ορατές μόνο σε ανθρώπους πίστεως. Ο Παύλος έγραψε, Ο φυσικός άνθρωπος δεν δέχεται τα του Πνεύματος του Θεού· διότι πώρωσιν αυτός εις αυτόν· ούτε δύναται να τα γνωρίση· διότι πνευματικώς κρίνεται –Α΄ Κορινθίους 2:14. Οι άνδρες της πίστεως είναι άνδρες των οποίων οι ζωές διέπονται από πνευματικές πραγματικότητες που είναι ασύλληπτες στον φυσικό άνθρωπο. Εάν θέλεις να γίνεις άνθρωπος πίστεως, περίμενε να παρεξηγηθείς. Ξεκινάς ένα ταξίδι που θα αντιβαίνει στην κοσμοθεωρία πολλών.

Καθώς ο Πέτρος άρχισε να βυθίζεται στα κύματα, εκράτησε φωνήν, «Κύριε, σώσόν με». Η στεναγμένη του κραυγή αποκάλυψε απόλυτη εμπιστοσύνη στον Κύριό του. Ο Ιησούς έτεινε το χέρι Του και τον έσωσε. Τα επόμενα λόγια του Ιησού συνεχίζουν να μας προκαλούν. Είπε προς τον Πέτρο, …Ω λιγόπιστε, διά τι εδίστασας; –Ματθαίος 14:31. Ο Πέτρος μόλις είχε περπατήσει πάνω στο νερό — επίτευγμα κανείς άλλος δεν είχε κατορθώσει πριν ή μετά — όμως ο Ιησούς το αποκάλεσε «ολιγόπιστον» και ρώτησε, «διὰτί εδίστασας;».

Ο Ιησούς είπε σε άλλη περίσταση, Εάν έχετε πίστιν ως κόκκον μουστάρδος, θα είπητε εις τούτο το όρος, Μετάβηθι απ" εδω εις εκεί· και θέλει μεταβή· και ουδέν θέλει είναι ασυμβίβαστον προς υμάς –Ματθαίος 17:20.

Εάν η «ολιγόπιστος» του Πέτρου τον εξουσιοδότησε να περπατήσει πάνω στο νερό, και εάν η πίστις όσο μικρή σαν κόκκος μουστάρδου μπορεί να μετακινήσει όρη, τι λέει αυτό για τη δική σου και τη δική μου πίστη;

Ίσως είναι ένδειξη ότι η πίστη μας είναι μικρότερη από την «ολιγόπιστον» του Πέτρου και λεπτότερη από τον μικρό κόκκο της μουστάρδας;! Είναι επίσης ένδειξη ότι ο Θεός τιμά τη μικρή πίστη. Αυτό που δεν τιμά είναι η έλλειψη πίστεως. Κατά την πίστη σου να σοι γίνεται. Μικρή πίστις… περπάτησε πάνω στο νερό! Καμία πίστις… βυθίσου κάτω από τα κύματα!

Εφόσον ο Ιησούς είναι ο «Λόγος», Αυτός είναι ο κύριος του φυσικού κόσμου και του πνευματικού κόσμου. Απέδειξε ότι είναι Κύριος του ανέμου και των κυμάτων — και ότε εισήλθον εις το πλοίον, ο άνεμος επέπαυσεν –Ματθαίος 14:32. Και απέδειξε ότι είναι Κύριος του πνευματικού κόσμου — τότε οι εν τω πλοίω προσήλθον και προσεκύνησαν αυτώ, λέγοντες, Αληθώς ότι ει συ ο Υιός του Θεού –Ματθαίος 14:33.

Εμείς, στον δυτικό κόσμο μας, έχουμε γίνει τόσο κορεσμένοι με τον υλισμό που μπορούμε εύκολα να παρασυρθούμε να πιστέψουμε ότι οι φυσικές πραγματικότητες είναι οι πιο ισχυρές πραγματικότητες. Αυτός ο υλισμός μας πολιορκεί, όχι μόνο με την αφθονία των υλικών αγαθών, αλλά επίσης με έναν βομβαρδισμό ανθρωπιστικής φιλοσοφίας. Η ανθρωπιστική φιλοσοφία είναι ένας τρόπος σκέψης που στερείται πνευματικής πραγματικότητας… που στερείται πίστεως.

Εάν συ, ως άνδρας, διαπιστώσεις ότι βυθίζεσαι σε κύματα απόγνωσης… είτε είναι οικονομικές δυσκολίες… είτε είναι προβλήματα στις σχέσεις… είτε ηθική αποτυχία ή ίσως βρίσκεις ότι είσαι ο χειρότερος κριτικός του εαυτού σου… επιτρέψω να σε προκαλέσω να ανεβάσεις τα μάτια σου στον έναν που είναι ο Λόγος. Ο Ιησούς είναι εκείνος που είναι κύριος των περιστάσεών σου και εκείνος που θα γίνει Κύριος της ψυχής σου. Να επιτρέψεις στον Ιησού να είναι Κύριος της ψυχής σου σημαίνει να ζεις με πίστη και υπακοή στις ριζικές διδασκαλίες του Ιησού.

Για να ζήσουμε σε αρμονία με τον φυσικό κόσμο τιμούμε τους νόμους της φύσεως. Όταν αντικαθιστούμε μια στέγη, σεβόμαστε τον νόμο της βαρύτητας. Όταν οδηγούμε όχημα, επιβραδύνουμε στις στροφές από σεβασμό προς τον νόμο της αδράνειας. Παραβιάζεις τους φυσικούς νόμους και κάποιος τραυματίζεται.

Για να ζήσουμε σε αρμονία με τον πνευματικό κόσμο, τιμούμε τον νόμο του Χριστού. Αγαπάμε τον πλησίον μας. Συγχωρούμε τον αδελφό μας. Τηρούμε τους όρκους του γάμου μας. Φέρουμε …τα βάρη αλλήλων, και έτσι πληροίτε τον νόμον του Χριστού –Γαλάτας 6:2.

Οι άνδρες της πίστεως είναι άνδρες που συντονίζονται με αυτές τις πνευματικές πραγματικότητες και διατάσσουν τη ζωή τους αναλόγως.
